en: Those who wander as thrice-seven, bearing all forms—may the Lord of Speech today bestow their powers upon my bodies.
Return again, O Lord of Speech, together with the divine mind. O Lord of Wealth, cause me to rest; let there be [the gift] in me alone, let what is heard be in me alone.
Right here, like two bow-ends bound by a string, may the Lord of Speech bind them fast; let there be [the gift] in me alone, let what is heard be in me alone.
The Lord of Speech has been invoked; may the Lord of Speech invoke us in return. May we come together with what is heard; may I not be deprived of what is heard.
We know Parjanya, the father of the arrow, the one who provides abundant nourishment; and we well know his mother, the earth, who possesses many forms.
O Jyākā, bow down around us; make our bodies like stone. Make them firm and wide, and drive away hostilities and enmities.
When the cows embrace the tree, they honor the quivering arrow, the *ṛbhu*. O Indra, keep the arrow, the missile, far away from us!
Just as the shaft stands between heaven and earth, so let the *muñja* grass stand between disease and the discharge of pus.
We know Parjanya, the father of the arrow, who possesses a hundredfold virility; with him I shall bring health to your body. Let your outflow be upon the earth; let your hair fall outside.
We know the father of the arrow, Mitra, possessing a hundredfold virility; with him I shall bring healing to your body; let your discharge be upon the earth, let your *bāla* be outside!

We know the father of the arrow, Varuṇa, possessing a hundredfold virility; with him I shall bring healing to your body; let your discharge be upon the earth, let your *bāla* be outside! We know the father of the arrow, Candramas, possessing a hundredfold virility; with him I shall bring healing to your body; let your discharge be upon the earth, let your *bāla* be outside!
We know the father of the arrow, Sūrya, who possesses a hundredfold virility. With him, may I bring healing to your body; let your discharge be upon the earth—*bahiṣ te astu bāl*.
That which is settled in your intestines, in your kidneys, and in your bladder—let your urine be released thus: *bahiṣ te mūtraṃ mucyatāṃ bāl iti sarvakam*.
I split open your urethra as one [splits] the dam of a river; let your urine be released thus: *bahiṣ te mūtraṃ mucyatāṃ bāl iti sarvakam*.

Open wide your bladder, as the mouth of the ocean, the great sea; let your urine be released outside, O Bāla, for the sake of all. Just as an arrow, once discharged from the bow, flies far away, even so let your urine be released outside, O Bāla, for the sake of all.
The mothers go along their paths, like sisters of those performing the sacrifice, mingling the milk with honey.
Those waters which are near the sun, or those with which the sun is joined—may they speed our sacrifice forward.
I invoke the divine waters where our cattle drink; an oblation is to be prepared for the rivers.

Within the waters is immortality, within the waters is healing. By the praises of the waters, may you horses become vigorous; may you cows become rich in vigor. For you, O Waters, are indeed sources of bliss; grant us strength for great joy and for clear vision.
That most auspicious sap of yours, grant us a share of it here, like longing mothers.
To that we come readily for you, for whose abode you quicken us; O Waters, give us life.
You who are masters of desirable things, who dwell among the peoples—to you, the Waters, I beg for healing.
May the divine Waters be for our aid and for our drink; may they flow toward us with healing peace.
Within the Waters, Soma has declared all medicines to be present, as well as Agni, the bringer of universal welfare.
O Waters, bestow medicine as a protection for my body, so that I may long behold the sun.

May the waters of the desert be auspicious to us, and may those of the marshes be auspicious; may the waters dug from the earth be auspicious to us, and those brought in jars be auspicious; may the waters of the rainy season be gracious to us.
O Agni, bring here the Yātudhāna who is a Kimīdin while he is praising you; for you, O God, being adored, have become the slayer of the Dasyu.
O Supreme Lord Jātavedas, master of your own body, O Agni, consume the fat of the oblation and cause the Yātudhānas to wail.
Let the sorcerers, the devouring *attriṇas*, and those who are *kimīdins* cry out; then, O Agni, may you and Indra accept this our oblation.

Let Agni take hold first, and let Indra, the mighty-armed, drive them away. Let every sorcerer come forward and say, "Here I am! We shall see your power, O Jātavedas; O you who watch over men, declare to us who is the sorcerer. Let all of them, scorched by you from the front, come here speaking thus: "This is it!"
Seize them, O Jātavedas; you were born for our sake. Having become our messenger, O Agni, cause the sorcerers to wail.
O Agni, bring here the sorcerers who are bound; then may Indra shatter their heads with his thunderbolt.
May this oblation carry away the sorcerer like foam from the water. Whether it be a woman or a man who has done this, let that person here be praised.
This one has come praising; welcome him! O Bṛhaspati, having brought him under control, O Agni and Soma, pierce him through!
O Soma, strike down the offspring of the sorcerer and lead him away; cast down both the upper and the lower eye of the one who reviles you.
O Agni Jātavedas, you who know the secret births of these devouring demons who dwell in hiding—strengthened by our prayer, strike them down, O Agni, crushing them by the hundreds!
May the Vasus, Indra, Pūṣan, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni establish this man in wealth. And may the Ādityas and all the gods establish him in the highest light.
May the gods grant light in his direction—Sūrya, Agni, or even gold. May our rivals be lower than we; raise this man up to the highest heaven!
O Jātavedas, with that supreme *brahman* wherewith you brought forth the waters for Indra, with that, O Agni, cause him to prosper here; establish him in the preeminence over his kinsmen!
I have taken away their sacrifice and their splendor, O Agni, as well as their abundance of wealth and their thoughts. May our rivals be lower than we; raise this man up to the highest heaven!
This Asura of the gods shines forth; for the desire of King Varuṇa is indeed true. From there, exulting through the sacred word (brahman), I lead this man out from the wrath of the fierce one.

Homage be to you, O King Varuṇa, and to your wrath! For you, O fierce one, perceive every transgression. I release you together with a thousand others; may this man live for a hundred autumns under your [protection].
Since you have spoken much falsehood and crookedness with your tongue, I release you from King Varuṇa, whose laws are truth.
I release you from Vaiśvānara and from the great ocean. O fierce one, speak here to your kinsmen and abandon our sacred prayer (brahman).

Vaṣaṭ to thee, O Pūṣan! At this pressing, let Aryaman, the wise ordainer, act as the Hotṛ-priest. Let the woman who has given birth according to the cosmic order move forward; let her joints relax so that she may bring forth.

The four quarters of heaven and the four of earth—the gods have sent forth the embryo; may they unfold it for birth. May the woman in labor unfold it; we cause the womb to open wide. O woman in labor, loosen it; O you who are skilled, release it, let it go.

Not in the flesh, not in the fat, nor indeed struck into the marrow—let the speckled afterbirth fall away for the dog to eat; let the afterbirth fall down! I split open your bladder, I split open the womb, I split open the two labia; I separate the mother and the son, the child along with the afterbirth; let the afterbirth fall down!
Just as the wind, just as the mind, just as birds fly, so do you, O ten-month-old one, fly forth together with the afterbirth; let the afterbirth fall down!

The first-born from the womb, the bull, the ruddy one, born of wind and cloud, goes thundering with rain. May he, moving straight, crushing [the obstacles], be gracious to our bodies—he who has stepped forth in three ways with his singular power.

To you, who have taken up your dwelling in every limb with your flame, we pay homage and worship with oblation. We worship with oblation the Aṅkas and the Samaṅkas, who has seized the joints of this [earth] as its seizer.

Release him from headache and from cough; joint by joint, that which has entered him—whether born of the clouds, born of the wind, or whatever vital force (śuṣma)—let it resort to the trees and the mountains. May there be well-being for my outer limb, and may there be well-being for my inner one; may there be well-being for my four limbs, and may there be well-being for my entire body.
Homage be to you, O lightning; homage be to you, O thunder; homage be to the stone with which you strike the ill-sacrificing one.
Homage to you, O grandson of the mountain, from whom you gather forth heat! Be gracious to our bodies; grant well-being to our offspring.
O Son of the Torrents, let there be homage indeed unto you; we offer homage to your weapon and to your heat. We know your supreme abode which is in secret; you are the navel placed within the ocean.
O Goddess, you whom all the gods created, fashioning you as a bold arrow for the sake of striking—may you, being praised in our assembly, be gracious to us; let there be homage to you, that goddess.

I pluck her fortune and splendor from her, like a garland from a tree. Like a mountain with a vast base, may she remain long among her ancestors. O King Yama, let this maiden, your bride, be set down for you; let her be bound in the house of her mother, and then in the house of her brother, and then in the house of her father. O King, she is the protector of your lineage; we entrust her to you. May she dwell long among her ancestors, until the hair falls from her head.
As the sisters [bind] the inner sheath of Asita, of you, Brahmā Kaśyapa, and of Gaya, so do I bind your vulva. //4//

May the rivers flow together, may the winds come together, and may the winged birds gather; may they take pleasure in this sacrifice of mine from of old. With an offering of flowing libations, I sacrifice.
Come here indeed to my call; come here, O flowing streams, and cause this song to prosper. Let every animal that exists come here; let whatever wealth there is remain with him.
Those perennial, inexhaustible springs that flow from the rivers—with all those flowing waters, we cause wealth to flow together for me.
With all those outflows that flow from clarified butter, milk, and water— with all those outflows, we cause wealth to flow together for me.
Those devourers who rose up against the penfold on the night of the new moon—may Agni, the fourth slayer of demons, speak for us.

Varuṇa has spoken for lead; Agni protects with lead. Indra gave me lead; that indeed is the dispeller of demons. This overcomes the *viṣkandha* disease; this drives away the devourers. By this, I have overcome all the offspring of the *piśācī*.
Whether you kill our cow, whether our horse, or whether our man, we shall pierce you with lead so that you may not be a slayer of our heroes.

Those women who go there, the veins clothed in red garments—like sisters without brothers, let them stand there, their luster destroyed. Stand below, stand above, and you also stand in the middle. The littlest stands; let this great vessel stand as well.
Of a hundred arteries and a thousand veins, these middle ones have stood firm; together the ends have come to rest.
A great, sand-filled channel has encompassed you; stand still and move about at ease.
We drive away misfortune, we drive away want; we drive away the enemy. And those things which are auspicious, those we bring to our progeny; we lead the enemy away from them.

May Savitṛ drive it out from our feet; may Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman drive it out from our hands; may Anumati, bestowing gifts upon us, drive it out. O gods, you have impelled this woman toward good fortune.
Whatever terrible thing there is in your self, in your body, in your hair, or in your appearance—all that we drive away with our speech. May the god Savitṛ purify you.
Riśyapadī, Vṛṣadatī, Goṣedhā, Vidhamā, Vilīḍhya, and Lalāmyā—these we cause to perish away from us.
Let not those who pierce from afar find us, nor let those who strike from close by find us. O Indra, cast far away from us the arrow-shafts in every direction.
Let the arrows fall scattered away from us—those that have been shot and those yet to be; O divine and human missiles, pierce my enemies on all sides.
Whoever among our own kin, whoever is a stranger, whether a kinsman or a foreigner, who assails us—may Rudra pierce these enemies of mine with his arrow.

Whether he be an adversary or one who is not an adversary, whoever hates us or curses us—may all the gods destroy him; may the sacred prayer (*brahman*) be my inner armor. O divine Soma, be one who does not flow away; O Maruts, be gracious to us at this sacrifice. Let not overwhelming power find us, nor let ill-will find us; let not the treacherous hatred that seeks us find us.
Whatever murderous weapon of the wicked rises up today, O Mitra and Varuṇa, keep that far away from us.
Drive away from here and from there, O Varuṇa, whatever brings slaughter. Grant us great protection, a wide refuge; drive away the weapon of death.

Truly, you are a great ruler, the unsubdued subduer of enemies. He whose friend is never slain and who is never overcome at any time—may that Indra, the bestower of well-being, the lord of the people, the slayer of Vṛtra, the dispeller of foes, the controller, the bull, the drinker of Soma, and the creator of fearlessness, go before us.
O Indra, strike down our adversaries; cast those who attack us low. Send into the deepest darkness whoever seeks to harm us.
Drive away the demon, strike down the adversaries; break asunder the jaws of Vṛtra. O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, shatter the fury of the enemy who assails us.
O Indra, turn away the mind of the hater, turn away the weapon of him who seeks to overcome us. Grant us great and wide protection; keep the weapon far away.
Let the glow of the heart and the jaundice depart after the rising sun. With the color of the red cow, with that we encompass you.
We enclose you with ruddy colors for the sake of long life, so that this man may be free from disease and likewise become free from jaundice.
Those cows which belong to the gods and are ruddy, and those which are indeed ruddy—by means of them, each form and each vital power, we enclose you.
We transfer your yellowness to the parrots, we place it in the *ropaṇākās*; and furthermore, we deposit your yellowness in the *hāridravas*.
O herb, you are born at night—Rāmā, Kṛṣṇā, and Asiknī. O Dyer, dye this away: both the leprosy and whatever grayness there is.
Drive out and destroy the leprosy and the grayness; drive away the speckled spots! Let your own natural color enter you; cast off the white parts!
Black is your dissolution, black is your abode. You are Asiknī, O herb; drive out and destroy the speckled spots!

By means of this sacred prayer, I have destroyed the white mark of the leprosy that has arisen from the bone, that which has arisen from the body, that which is on the skin, and that which was produced by a corrupting agent.
The Suparṇa was born first; you were his bile. Then the Asurī, conquered in battle, took on the form of the trees.
The Asurī made this first remedy for leucoderma, this destroyer of leucoderma. It has destroyed the leucoderma and made the skin uniform in color.
Sarūpā is the name of your mother, Sarūpa is the name of your father. You, O herb, are the maker of uniformity; make this [skin] uniform.
The dark one, who bestows beauty, has been brought forth from the earth. Accomplish this well; fashion the forms again.

Where Agni, having entered the waters, burned them—where those upholders of the Law (Dharma) offered their salutations—there they say is your highest birthplace. Knowing us, O Fever (Takman), spare us!
Whether you are flame or whether you are glowing heat, whether you move among the wood-shavings or where your birthplace is—you are named Hrūḍu, O God of the Green One. Knowing us, O Fever, spare us!
Whether you are sorrow, or intense grief, or the son of King Varuṇa; O God, you are named Hrūḍu, the green one—being well-aware of us, spare us from Takman.
Homage to the cold Takman; homage do I pay to the burning heat. Homage be to the Takman that comes on the next day, on both days, or every third day.
May that missile, O Gods, be far away from us! Far away be the stone which you hurl! Far away be the stone which you hurl!
May he be our friend, a gift unto us; may Indra, Bhaga, and Savitar of wondrous bounty be our friends.
O Maruts, you who possess sun-like skins, O sons of the flowing waters, grant us wide-reaching protection.
Cook us well; be gracious; have mercy upon our bodies; grant happiness to our offspring.
Those snakes yonder on the far shore, the thrice-seven that are devoid of offspring—by means of their skins we wipe away the eyes of the malevolent adversary who lies in wait.
Let her go forth in all directions, cutting him down like one bearing a bow; let the malevolent ones, unsuccessful and born again and again, be scattered in every way.
Neither the many nor the few have been able to prevail; they have not dared to attack us. Like the joints of a reed on all sides, the malevolent ones are unsuccessful.
O ghost, let your feet tremble; carry away those who give to the householder! O Indrāṇī, may you go first, unconquered and unrobbed, before us.

The divine Agni has approached, the slayer of demons, the driver away of disease. Burning away the double-dealing sorcerers and the *kimīdin*s, burn against the sorcerers, O God; burn against the *kimīdin*s. O you whose path is black, burn the female sorceresses back toward themselves.
She who cursed with a curse, she who established evil and folly, she who undertook to seize the offspring for the sake of stealing the essence—let her devour her own child!
Let the sorceress devour her son, her sister, and her grandson; then let the long-haired sorceresses strike one another down. Let the Arāyīs be torn asunder!
With the *abhīvarta* amulet by which Indra grew preeminent—with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, cause us to grow for the sake of sovereignty.
Overpowering our rivals, overpower those who are hostile to us; stand over him who assails us, overpower him who seeks to harm us.
Thee, O Lord, has Savitṛ strengthened; thee, Soma has strengthened. Thee, all beings have strengthened, so that thou mayest be the *abhīvarta*.

This amulet, the *abhīvarta*, the conqueror, the destroyer of rivals—let it be bound upon me for the sake of sovereignty, to overcome my enemies. Yonder sun has risen; so too has this word of mine risen, so that I may be a slayer of foes, without rivals, a slayer of rivals.
The bull, the destroyer of rivals, the protector of the earth, the all-conquering one—so that I may rule over these heroes and over this people.

O All-Gods, Vasus, protect him; and you, Ādityas, remain watchful over him. Let no death from kin of the same lineage, nor from those of a different lineage, nor any human slaughter reach him. O Gods, you who are fathers and you who are sons, being of one mind, hear this word of mine. I entrust him to you all; carry him safely to old age.

O gods who abide in heaven, you who are on earth, you who are in the intermediate space, in the plants, in the cattle, and within the waters—grant him long life and old age; let him bypass a hundred other deaths.

Those gods for whom there are fore-offerings and after-offerings, who partake of the oblations and who consume even what is not offered; those whose five quarters are distributed for you—to them, the dwellers of the sacrificial session, I dedicate these for this man.
To the four guardians of the quarters, the immortals, the overseers of all that exists, we offer this oblation with our sacrificial gift.
O you gods who are the four guardians of the quarters, release us from the nooses of Destruction and from every distress.
I worship you, the unwearied, with an oblation; I offer to you, the uncrippled, with clarified butter. May that fourth god who is the guardian of the quarters bring us here to well-being.

May there be well-being for our mother and for our father; may there be well-being for our cattle, for all living beings, and for men. May everything that exists be auspicious and easy to find for us; may we long behold the sun.

O people, you shall know this great *brahman* that he will proclaim: there is nothing on earth nor in heaven by which the plants breathe, nor in the intermediate space their place of rest, like those who sit weary. Do the wise truly know the station of this being?
When the two worlds, heaven and earth, were fashioned, they were moist; even today it remains so, like the constant flow of the ocean.
The universe rests upon one [of these], while the other is supported above it. To Heaven, the all-knowing, and to Earth, I have paid homage.
Golden-hued, pure, and purifying—those in whom Savitṛ was born and in whom Agni was born; those golden ones who have received Agni as their embryo—may those waters be auspicious and gentle to us.
In whose midst King Varuṇa moves, discerning the truth and falsehood of men; those golden ones who have received Agni as their embryo—may those waters be auspicious and gentle to us.

Those whose food the gods consume in heaven, those who exist manifoldly in the intermediate space; those golden ones who have received Agni as their embryo—may those waters be auspicious and gentle to us.
Behold me with a gracious eye, O Waters; touch my skin with your auspicious body. May those waters, which drip with clarity, which are pure and purifying, be peaceful and pleasant to us.
This plant is born of honey; we dig you up with honey. You are produced from honey; make us full of honey.
On the tip of my tongue is honey, at the root of my tongue is sweetness; may you abide in this very sacrifice of mine, and may you conform to my thought.
Sweet is my stepping forth; sweet is my departing. With my speech I utter what is sweet; may I become full of sweetness, seeing sweetness.

I am sweeter than honey, even sweeter than the honey-maker. Surely you shall choose me alone, as one chooses a honey-sweet branch. I have come around you with an encircling cane, that there may be no enmity. So that you may be devoted to me, so that you may never depart from me. As the Dākṣāyaṇas, bestowing their favor upon Śatānīka, bound gold upon him, so do I bind it upon you for life, for splendor, for strength, and for long life lasting a hundred autumns.
Neither the *rakṣas* nor the *piśācas* prevail over him; for this is the first-born vigor of the gods. He who wears the gold of Dakṣa’s lineage secures for himself a long life among the living.
The brilliance of the waters, the light, the vital energy, and the strength of the trees—like Indra, we bestow these powers upon him. May he, being strengthened, wear the gold;
with the seasons of the equal months, I nourish you with the milk of the year. May Indra, Agni, and all the gods grant their approval to you, free from anger.
Vena beholds that which is supreme and hidden, wherein all becomes one in form. As she was being born, Pṛśni milked this [milk]; the hosts who find the light of heaven raised their voices in praise.

Let the Gandharva, the knower of immortality, proclaim that supreme abode which is hidden in the secret cave. His three steps are placed in the secret cave; he who knows them shall be the father of the Father. He is our father, our progenitor, and our kinsman; he knows all abodes and all worlds. He alone is the sole name-giver of the gods; to him all worlds go with their inquiries. In an instant, I have reached and approached him who pervades heaven and earth, the first-born of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*). Established among the worlds like speech in the speaker, he is indeed the one who bestows wealth; he is truly this Agni.
I have gone around all beings to behold the outstretched thread of *ṛta*, where the gods, having attained immortality, took their stand upon a common womb.

The celestial Gandharva, who is the sole lord of the world, worthy of homage and to be praised among the people—I seek you with a sacred prayer, O divine god; let there be obeisance to you. Your dwelling is in heaven. Touching the sky, O worshipful one, you possess a sun-like skin that wards off the divine heat. May the Gandharva, who is the sole lord of the world, worthy of homage and most gracious, be merciful.
He has united with these blameless ones; among the Apsarases was even the Gandharva. The ocean, they say, is their dwelling place, from which they go forth and return instantly.
O lightning-flashes, belonging to the stars, you who attend upon the Gandharva Viśvāvasu—to you, O goddesses, I offer this homage.
To those who are piercing, dark, craving dice, and bewildering the mind—to them, the Gandharvas and Apsarases, I have paid homage.
That which runs away from there, the watery spray from the mountain—that I make into a remedy for you, a good remedy, so that you may be well.
From your very limbs—surely you possess a hundred remedies—and among them, you are the most excellent, free from discharge and free from disease.
The Asuras dig this great wound-deep down; that is the remedy for the flow of blood, and it has destroyed the disease.
The ants bring forth the medicine from the ocean; that is the remedy for the discharge, and it has allayed the disease.
This great swelling has been lifted up from upon the earth; it is the remedy for the discharge, and it has destroyed the disease.

May the waters and the plants be auspicious and bring us peace. May Indra’s thunderbolt drive away the demons. May arrows, once discharged, fall upon the demons from afar. For the sake of long life and great joy, may we always remain unharmed and ever vigorous. We wear the *jaṅgiḍa* amulet, the destroyer of *viṣkandha*.
From the *jambha* demon, from the *viśara*, from the *viṣkandha*, and from the burning fever—may this amulet of a thousand powers protect us on every side.
This Jaṅgiḍa overcomes the Viṣkandha; this one drives away the Attrins. This all-healing Jaṅgiḍa shall protect us from distress.
With the jewel Jaṅgiḍa, bestowed by the gods, which brings delight, we overcome Viṣkandha and all demonic powers through our exertion.

May both the hemp and the Jaṅgiḍa protect me from Viṣkandha. One was brought from the forest, the other from the juices of the ploughed field. This amulet is a destroyer of sorcery and likewise a destroyer of enmity. Moreover, the powerful Jaṅgiḍa shall prolong our lives.
O Indra, take pleasure; come forth, go hither with your two bay steeds, O Hero! Drink of the pressed juice, desiring the sweet draught here for exhilaration—the lovely one for intoxication.
O Indra, fill your belly with this sweet juice as if it were new, like [the light] from heaven. Like the sun, the exhilarating, well-spoken words have gone toward you.
Indra is the overcomer of the swift, he who struck down Vṛtra like Mitra; he shattered Vala like the moving [rays], and like Bhṛgu he has overcome his enemies in the intoxication of Soma.

May the pressed juices enter you; O Indra, fill your two flanks. O Śakra, be mindful; come hither! Hear our call and my songs; O Indra, take pleasure with your own companions and rejoice here for great delight.

Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time: he slew the serpent, he released the waters, and he cleft open the bellies of the mountains.
I slew the serpent as he lay coiled upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the thunderbolt that roars through the sky. Like lowing cows, the flowing waters have gone straight down to the ocean.
Acting like a bull, he chose the Soma; at the Trikadruka rites, he drank of the pressed juice. Maghavan took up his weapon, the thunderbolt; he struck down this first-born of the serpents.
O Agni, may the seasons increase you, may the years and the seers increase you with their truths. Shine forth with the celestial light; illuminate all four quarters of the world.

Be kindled, O Agni, and cause this man to prosper; rise up for great good fortune. Let not those who attend upon thee, O Agni, come to harm; let these venerable priests be glorious, and not others. These Brahmins choose thee, O Agni; be auspicious to us in our dwelling, O Agni. Be the slayer of rivals, O Agni, the conqueror of those who plot against us; watch over our own home, never failing. With thy own sovereign power, O Agni, take hold of us; with Mitra as thy friend, O Agni, strive to win friends. Standing in the midst of thy kinsmen, O Agni, shine here as one to be invoked by kings.
Beyond insults, beyond assailants, beyond lack of understanding, and beyond enemies—you, O Agni, cross over all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons.
The plant born of the gods, which strikes down curses and is hated by the wicked, has looked upon all my curses as water looks upon impurity. May it remove them all from me.
Whatever curse comes from a rival wife, whatever curse comes from a sister, and whatever a Brahmin may curse in his anger—may all that be beneath our feet.
That which is rooted down from heaven and extends up from the earth—with that thousand-fold weapon, protect us on every side.

Protect me, protect my offspring, and protect our wealth; let no enemy overcome us, nor let our adversaries prevail. Let the curse return to the curser who is ill-disposed toward us, along with his own heart; we crush the ribs of the evil-hearted one with the eye of the mantra.
The two blessed stars named Vicṛtau have risen; may they release the lowest and highest bond of the *kṣetriya* disease.
May this night dawn away [the disease], and may the malevolent ones depart. May the plant that destroys the *kṣetriya* shine away the *kṣetriya*.
With the chaff of the brown, white-stalked barley, and with the husk of the sesame seed—may the plant that destroys *kṣetriya* drive away the *kṣetriya* disease.
Homage to your ploughs, homage to the poles and yokes; may the plant that destroys *kṣetriya* drive away the *kṣetriya* disease.
Homage to those with drooping eyes; homage to those who are to be pointed out. Homage to the Lord of the Field! O herb that destroys *kṣetriya*, may it drive away the *kṣetriya* disease.
O ten trees, release him from the seizing grasp of the *rakṣas* that has held him fast at his joints. And now, O Lord of the Forest, lead him up to the world of the living.
He has come; he has risen up; he has joined the company of the living. He has become a father of sons and the most blessed among men.
He has mastered the sacred sciences; he has ascended above the dwellings of the living. For he has a hundred physicians and a thousand healing plants.
The gods have found your growth, as have the Brahmins and the plants; all the gods have found your growth upon the earth.
He who made it shall undo it; he alone is the most skilled physician. He alone, the pure healer, shall prepare medicines for you.

From *kṣetriya*, from destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice, I release you from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.

May Agni be auspicious for you along with the waters; may Soma be auspicious for you along with the plants. Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice—from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.

May the wind in the mid-air bestow vigor upon you; may the four quarters of space be auspicious for you. Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, and from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be gracious to you.

These goddesses, the four quarters, whose lord is the wind, whom the sun surveys from all sides—just so do I release you from the field-disease, from destruction, from the curse of kinship, and from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.

Into these [plants] I place you within your old age; let consumption depart, and let Destruction go far away. Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from Destruction, from the curse of kin, and from the malice of Varuṇa’s noose. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.

You have been released from consumption, from misfortune, from reproach, and from the noose of malice and of *grāhi*; you have been released upward. Even so do I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, from malice, and from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.

Day after day you have found a pleasant dwelling; you have entered into the auspicious world of the well-doer. Even so do I release you from hereditary disease, from Destruction, from the curse of kin, and from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be gracious to you.

The gods released Sūrya from the grasp of darkness; freeing him from sin, they set him free. Even so do I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, and from the noose of Varuṇa. By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless. May both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. You are the corrupter of the corruptible; you are the missile of the missile; you are the malady of the malady. Attain that which is better; pass beyond your equal.
You are a garland; you are a protective amulet; you are a counter-attack. Attain that which is better; surpass your equal.
Go against him who hates us and whom we hate; reach one who is better, surpass one who is equal.
You are a wise seer; you are the bestower of splendor; you are the protector of the body. Attain what is better; surpass and transcend your equal.
You are the bright; you are the radiant; you are the heavenly light; you are the luminous. Attain what is better; surpass and transcend your equal.
Heaven and Earth, the wide mid-air, the two wives of the field, the far-striding and wondrous one—may the wide mid-air, protected by the wind, heat itself here for me as I am being heated.
Listen to this, O gods, you who are worthy of sacrifice: Bharadvāja recites hymns for me. Let him who injures this mind of ours be bound in fetters and cast into misfortune.
Hear this, O Indra, drinker of Soma, as I call upon you with a grieving heart. Like a tree with an axe, I shall cut down him who injures this mind of ours.
With the eighty-three Sāmagas, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases—may they protect our ancestral offerings and pious works. I take that man away by divine power;
O Heaven and Earth, look upon me with favor! O All-Gods, hold fast to me! O Soma-loving Fathers, the Aṅgirases, let evil seize the doer of what is undesirable.

Let burning pains fall upon him who holds us in contempt, O Maruts, or who reviles the sacred prayer (*brahman*) as it is being performed. May his crooked deeds be consumed by fire; may the heavens scorch the hater of sacred prayer.
The seven vital breaths, the eight thoughts—these I cut away from you with the sacred word (*brahman*). The goat, the messenger of Yama, has been made ready;
I place your foot upon the kindled Jātavedas. May Agni pervade the body; may the breath and speech go forth.

O Agni, giver of life, choosing old age, you whose face is ghee and whose back is ghee—having drunk the sweet and pleasant ghee of the cow, protect this man as a father protects his sons. Clothe him, endow him with splendor; make this death by old age [your own] and grant him long life. Bṛhaspati has bestowed this garment for King Soma to put on.
You have put on this garment for well-being; you have become the protector of the young cows against curses. Live for a hundred abundant autumns, and clothe yourself in the increase of wealth.
Come, step upon this stone; let your body become as firm as stone. May all the gods grant you a lifespan of a hundred autumns.
We take from you that garment which was first worn; may all the gods protect you. May many brothers, increasing and well-born, follow after you as you grow strong and well-established.
We destroy Niḥsālā, Dhṛṣṇu, Dhiṣaṇā, Ekavādyā, Jighatsvā, and all the granddaughters of Caṇḍa—the Sadānvās.

We drive you out from the cow-pen, out from the axle, out from the wagon-board; we drive you away from your houses, O daughters of Magundi. Let those who are *arāyī* demons dwell in that house which is down below; let exhaustion settle there, along with all the sorceresses. Let Bhūtapati and Indra drive the Sadānvās out from here. Seated at the base of the house, may Indra trample them down with his thunderbolt.
Whether you belong to those who suffer from hereditary disease, or whether you are sent by men, or whether you are born of the Dasyus—perish from here, O Sadānvās!
I have run around their dwellings like a swift horse to its goal; I have won all your races. Perish from here, O Sadānvās!
Just as heaven and earth do not fear and do not come to harm, so, O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
Just as day and night neither fear nor suffer harm, so, O Prāṇa, do you not fear for me.
Just as the sun and the moon neither fear nor suffer harm, even so, O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
Just as the Brahmin and the Kshatriya do not fear and do not come to harm, so, O Prana, may you not fear for me.
Just as truth and falsehood do not fear and do not suffer harm, so, O Prāṇa, may you not fear for me.
As that which has been and that which is to be do not fear nor suffer harm, even so, O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
O Prāṇa and Apāna, protect me from death; Svāhā!
O Heaven and Earth, having heard me, protect me; svāhā!
O Sūrya, protect me with your eye; svāhā!
O Agni Vaiśvānara, protect me with all the gods; Svāhā!
O Sustainer of All, protect me with all-sustaining nourishment; Svāhā!
You are vital energy; grant me vital energy, svāhā! You are power; grant me power, svāhā!
You are strength; grant strength! Svāhā!
You are life; grant me life! Svāhā!
You are the ear; grant me the ear, svāhā!
You are the eye; grant me the eye. Svāhā!
You are a protection; grant me protection, svāhā!
You are the destroyer of rivals; grant me the dispeller of rivals, svāhā!
You are the destroyer of rivals; grant me the driving away of rivals. Svāhā!
You are the destroyer of the Arāya; grant me the driving away of the Arāya, svāhā!
You are the destroyer of Piśācas; grant me the driving away of Piśācas, svāhā! You are the destroyer of Sadānvās; grant me the driving away of Sadānvās, svāhā!
O Agni, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Agni, with that flame of yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Agni, with that flame of yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Agni, with that flame of yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Agni, with that splendor which is yours, make him lusterless who hates us and whom we hate.
O Vāyu, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Vāyu, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Vāyu, with that flame which is yours, blaze against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Vāyu, with that flame which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Vāyu, with that splendor which is yours, make him lusterless—he who hates us and whom we hate. O Sūrya, with that heat which is yours, burn him up—he who hates us and whom we hate.
O Sūrya, with that heat of yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Sūrya, with that flame which is yours, radiate against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Sūrya, with that radiance which is yours, blaze against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Sun, with that splendor which is yours, make him lusterless who hates us and whom we hate. O Moon, with that heat which is yours, burn him up who hates us and whom we hate.
O Moon, that which is yours, take it away; with that, take it from him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Moon, with that radiance of yours, shine against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Moon, with that radiance of yours, blaze against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Moon, with that splendor which is yours, make him lusterless who hates us and whom we hate.
O Waters, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Waters, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Waters, with that flame which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Waters, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate.
O Waters, with that power which is yours, make him powerless who hates us and whom we hate.
O Śerabhaka, O Śerabha, let your sorceries return, let the missile of the Kimīdins return! Devour him by whose side you stand; devour him who sent you forth; devour your own flesh!
O Śevṛdhaka, O Śevṛdha, let your sorceries return, let the missile of the Kimīdins return! Devour him by whose side you stand; devour him who sent you forth; devour your own flesh!

Mroka and Anumroka, let your sorceries go back to you again; let the missile of the Kimīdin go back! Devour him by whom you are sent, devour him who sent you; eat your own flesh! Sarpa and Anusarpa, let your sorceries go back to you again; let the missile of the Kimīdin go back! Devour him by whom you are sent, devour him who sent you; eat your own flesh! Jūrṇi, let your sorceries go back to you again; let the missile of the Kimīdin go back! Devour him by whom you are sent, devour him who sent you; eat your own flesh!

Let your sorceries go back to their source, O Yātus; let the missile of the Kimīdin go back! Devour him from whom you come; devour him who sent you; devour your own flesh! O Arjunī, let your sorceries go back to their source, O Yātus; let the missile of the Kimīdin go back! Devour him from whom you come; devour him who sent you; devour your own flesh! O Bharūjī, let your sorceries go back to their source, O Yātus; let the missile of the Kimīdin go back! Devour him from whom you come; devour him who sent you; devour your own flesh!
May the goddess Pṛśniparṇī bring us peace; she has brought misfortune to Nirṛti. For she is fierce, the crusher of the Kaṇvas; I have partaken of her, the powerful one.
This Pṛśniparṇī was born first as a conqueror; with her, I sever the heads of those with evil names, like those of a bird.
Destroy the Arāya, the drinker of blood, and him who seeks to steal our prosperity; O Pṛśniparṇī, destroy the embryo-devouring Kaṇva and overcome him!
Cause these Kaṇvas, who sustain life, to enter this mountain; O Goddess Pṛśniparṇī, go forth and consume them as fire does [the forest].

Drive them away, these Kaṇvas who seek to prolong their lives; I have sent the flesh-eaters to that place where the darknesses go. Let the cattle come here, those which have gone abroad and whose companion Vāyu has enjoyed; Tvaṣṭṛ knows their forms—may Savitṛ settle them here in this cow-pen.
May the cattle flow together into this pen; may Bṛhaspati lead them here, knowing the way. May Sinīvālī lead them to the front; O Anumati, restrain those who have arrived.
May the cattle flow together, may the horses and the men come together. Whatever abundance there is of grain—that I offer with the oblation of flowing libations.
I pour together the milk of the cows, together with the strength and essence of the clarified butter. May our heroes be well-sprinkled; may the cows remain firm while I am the lord of the herd.
I bring hither the milk of the cows; I have brought hither the grain and the essence. Our heroes have been brought back, as have the wives to this home.
Let no enemy consume us; you are the subduer, the overcomer. Strike down the consumer with the counter-consumer; O herb, render them sapless!
The Suparṇa found you; the boar dug you up with its snout. Strike down the consumer and the secondary consumer; render them sapless, O herb!
Indra indeed placed you in his arm to strike down the Asuras. Strike down the consumer and the secondary consumer; render them sapless, O herb!
Indra tore open the Pāṭā plant to strike down the Asuras. Strike down the consumer and the secondary consumer; render them sapless, O herb!

With her, may I, like Indra with his dice, devour my enemies as if they were wolves. O herb, destroy them; devour them, devour them again! Render them powerless. O Rudra, O cooling medicine, O blue-crested one, O performer of deeds, devour him, devour him again! Destroy him who assails us, O Indra! Speak for us with your powers; make me the superior devourer.

May this man increase in old age for you alone; let not other deaths harm him, those hundreds that exist. Like a well-disposed mother her son in her lap, may Mitra protect him from distress with his friendship.

May Mitra and Varuṇa, the destroyers of enemies, acting in harmony, bring about his death through old age. Agni, the Hotṛ priest who knows all sacred ordinances, proclaims all the generations of the gods.

You rule over the domestic animals of the earth, both those already born and those yet to be born. Let neither the out-breath nor the in-breath abandon this one; let neither friends nor enemies slay him.
May Heaven as father and Earth as mother, acting in harmony, grant you old age until death. So that you may live in the lap of Aditi, protected by out-breath and in-breath for a hundred winters.
O Agni, lead this man to long life and splendor; O King Varuṇa and Mitra, grant him beloved seed. Like a mother, O Aditi, bestow protection upon him, so that he may reach old age, O All-Gods.
From the essence of the earthly realm, O Gods, from the body of Bhaga and from strength—may Agni and Sūrya bestow long life and splendor upon him, and Bṛhaspati [bestow] splendor.
Grant him long life, O Jātavedas; O Tvaṣṭṛ, bestow progeny upon him. O Savitṛ, impel for him the increase of wealth; may he live a hundred autumns under your care.
Bestow upon us nourishment, progeny, and wisdom, as well as wealth, O you who are of one mind! Grant victory over the lands; by your power, O Indra, make our rivals low.

Sent by Indra, instructed by Varuṇa, and dispatched by the Maruts, this fierce one has come to us. O Heaven and Earth, in your lap, let him not hunger nor thirst. O you who are full of strength, bestow strength upon him; O you who are full of milk, bestow milk upon him. Heaven and Earth have bestowed strength upon him; so too have all the gods, the Maruts, and the waters.

With auspicious [waters] I satiate your heart; may you rejoice, free from disease and endowed with excellent luster. Wearing the form of the Aśvins through your creative power (*māyā*), may the two of you, dwelling together, drink this stirred drink (*mantha*).

Indra created this [plant] in the beginning when he was pierced; it is the undecaying self-power of vital strengths. This is yours. Live through many autumns with it, full of luster. Let it not flow away from you; the physicians have prepared it for you.

Just as the wind stirs the blade of grass upon the earth, so do I stir your mind, so that you may be loving toward me, so that you may not turn away from me like rivers. O Aśvins, if you two lead her here as one who loves, and if you bring her together, then your blessings shall meet, your thoughts shall meet, and your vows shall meet.
Where the fair-winged ones desire to speak, where the disease-free ones desire to speak—there let my pain go, like a thorn from a wooden splinter.
That which is the interior, let that be the exterior; that which is the exterior, let that be the interior. O Herb, seize the hearts of maidens of every form!
This woman has come desiring a husband; I have come desiring a wife. Like a neighing horse, I have come together with fortune.
The great stone of Indra, which crushes every worm—with that I grind the worms together like grain upon a millstone.
I have crushed the seen and the unseen; I have crushed the *kurūru* as well. All the *algaṇḍu*s and *śalūna* worms—we crush them with our word.

I strike down the *algaṇḍu*s with a great slaughter; those who were pained have become unpained and sapless. I drive away the remaining ones, whether disciplined or undisciplined, by my word, so that not one of the worms shall be left behind.
The intestinal, the cranial, and the spinal worms—I crush the worms with our speech, even those that crawl and those that move through the air.
The worms that are in the mountains, in the forests, in the plants, in the cattle, and within the waters—those which have entered our bodies, all those broods of worms I destroy.
May the rising sun slay the worms; may he slay them with his rays as he sets, as well as the worms that are within the cow.

The worm that is multiform, four-eyed, speckled, and white—I crush its ribs and cut off its head. Like Atri, like Kaṇva, and like Jamadagni, I slay you worms; with the sacred spell of Agastya, I grind the worms to powder.
Slain is the king of worms, and slain is their chieftain. Slain is the worm whose mother is slain, slain its brother, and slain its sister.

Slain are his attendants, slain are his followers; and those who are like small creatures—all those worms are slain. I pluck out your two horns with which you gore; I split open your poison-bag, that which is your vessel for venom. From your eyes, from your nostrils, from your ears, and from your chin, from the brain in your head and from your tongue, I tear away the consumption that afflicts you.
From your neck, from your uṣṇihā-joints, from your vertebrae, and from your spine—diseases of the shoulders, from your shoulder-blades and from your arms, I tear away from you.
From your heart, from your lungs, from your liver, and from your ribs—disease from your kidneys, from your spleen, and from your liver, we tear away from you.
From your intestines, from your bowels, from the large intestine, and from the belly; from your two sides, from the bladder, and from the navel—I tear away your consumption.
From your two thighs, from your two knees, from your two heels, and from your two forefeet; from your anus, from your hips, and from the pubic region—I tear away your consumption.
From your bones, from your marrow, from your sinews, and from your arteries; from your two hands, from your fingers, and from your nails—I tear away your consumption.
In every limb, in every hair, and in every joint of yours, we root out with the tearing power of Kaśyapa the consumption that dwells in your skin, driving it away in all directions.

He who rules as Paśupati over cattle, both those that are four-footed and those that are two-footed—may he, being redeemed, attain his share in the sacrifice; may the increases of wealth attend the sacrificer. Releasing the seed of the world, O Gods, grant a path for the sacrificer. May the animal, once brought forward and having stood still while performing its service, go to the dear domain of the Gods.

May Agni, the god, the creator of all, releasing them with his progeny, first set free those who, watching over what was being bound, beheld it with their mind and their eye. May Vāyu, the god Prajāpati, releasing them with his progeny, first set free those domestic animals which are of every form—though diverse in appearance, they become uniform in many ways.

May the ancestors, knowing this, receive him as he moves away from his limbs toward the vital breath. Go to heaven; stand firm with your bodies; go to the world of light by the paths traveled by the gods.

Those who, while consuming riches, did not prosper, and for whom the sacrificial fires on their hearths felt remorse—may Viśvakarman make that ill-sacrificed rite of theirs a well-sacrificed one for us.

The seers say that the lord of the sacrifice is afflicted by sin when he is excluded from his share and his offspring feel remorse; may Viśvakarman unite us with those drops that were lost through negligence.
Thinking himself a drinker of Soma though he is unworthy, the wise man knows the proper time for the sacrifice; O Viśvakarman, release him who has committed sin and is bound, for our well-being.

Terrible are the seers; let there be homage to them, for that which is their eye and the truth of their mind. To Bṛhaspati, O mighty and radiant one, be homage; to Viśvakarman, homage to thee! Protect us.
The eye, the beginning, and the mouth of the sacrifice—I offer with speech, with hearing, and with the mind. May the gods, being well-disposed, come to this sacrifice spread out by Viśvakarman.

O Agni, may the supporter bring to us a favorable thought along with this maiden and our good fortune. Cherished among suitors, lovely in assemblies, may she quickly attain prosperity through her husband.

I bring about the discovery of a husband for this woman through the truth of the god Dhātṛ, by means of Soma’s favor, by means of the Brahman’s favor, and by that which was gathered together by Aryaman as fortune.
O Agni, may this woman find a husband; for King Soma makes her blessed. Giving birth to sons, she shall become a queen; having gone to her husband, may she shine forth as one who is fortunate.

Just as this pleasant den, O Maghavan, has become a lovely resting place for the deer, so let this woman be dear to Bhaga, beloved by her husband, and not causing him harm. Ascend the full ship of Bhaga, which never fails; with it, ferry across the bridegroom who is desired by you.
Cry out, O Lord of Wealth! Make the bridegroom well-disposed toward you. Make everything favorable for the bridegroom who is desired by you.
This gold, this bdellium, this ox, and furthermore Bhaga—these have given you over to your husbands so that you may be known by him who desires you.

May Savitṛ lead you; may he who is desired by you lead you as your husband. May Agni, the wise one, go forth against our enemies, burning away the curse and the ill-will. May he confound the army of our adversaries and render them handless, O Jātavedas.
O Maruts, you are fierce; such as you are, advance, crush them, and overcome them! These Vasus have been crushed while seeking protection, for Agni, the wise one, shall go forth as their messenger.

O Maghavan, against the hostile army that acts as an enemy toward us—O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, and Agni, burn it up! Urged on by you, O Indra, let your two bay steeds and your thunderbolt go forth, crushing the enemies. Slay those who face you, those who follow from behind, and those who flee away; scatter them in all directions and make their resolve come true!
O Indra, confound the army of our enemies; with the rush of fire and wind, destroy them, scattering them in all directions.
May Indra bewilder the army; may the Maruts strike it down with their might. May Agni take away their sight; let the defeated host return.
May Agni, our wise messenger, come back to us, burning away the curse and the enemy. May he bewilder the minds of our foes and render them handless, O Jātavedas.
This Agni has bewildered those thoughts that are in your hearts. May he blow them from your dwelling; may he blow them away from every side.
Bewildering the minds of men, O Indra, come hither with our intention; by the swift rush of Agni and Vāta, scatter them in all directions.
Let their intentions depart, and let their thoughts be confounded; then, whatever is in their hearts today, drive that out from them completely.
Bewildering their minds, seize their limbs, O *Apvā*, and pass them by! Advance against them; burn them up with sorrows in their hearts! Seize the enemies; pierce the foes with darkness!

That army of the adversaries which approaches us, O Maruts, challenging us with its might—pierce it with a lawless darkness so that not one of them knows another! He has bellowed; may he be present here as a skillful worker. O Agni, reveal the two wide worlds! May the all-knowing Maruts harness you; lead that man, to whom oblations are offered, with reverence!
May the ruddy ones bring hither from afar the sage Indra for our friendship, since the gods, through the Sautrāmaṇī, have dared to offer the Gāyatrī, the Bṛhatī, and the hymn to him.
O King Varuṇa, let him call you from the waters; let Soma call you from the mountains; let Indra call you from these subjects. Having become a falcon, fly to these subjects!
May the falcon carry the oblation from the other’s domain to you, who were wandering, excluded, in another’s field. O Aśvins, make the path easy for you; O kinsmen, settle yourselves around him!
(5) Let the rival clans call upon you; let your friends show their favor. Indra, Agni, and all the gods have established security for you within this clan. (6)
O Indra, whoever among our kinsmen or strangers speaks against your call—having turned him away, bring this man here.

May the kingdom come to you together with splendor; rise up toward the east as the lord of the people, the sole ruler—shine forth! Let all the quarters call upon you, O King; may you be one to be approached and honored here.
May the people choose you for kingship, and may these five divine quarters choose you. Rest upon the height, upon the summit of the kingdom; from there, O fierce one, distribute wealth among us.
Let your kinsmen come hither with oblations; let Agni, the swift messenger, move among them. May your wives and sons be well-disposed; as a formidable one, look upon the abundant tribute.
Let the Aśvins first, both Mitra and Varuṇa, and all the gods and Maruts call upon you. Now set your mind upon bestowing wealth; then, O formidable one, distribute riches among us.
Run forth from the furthest distance! May both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. Thus has King Varuṇa spoken; he has summoned you—come hither!

O Indra, O Indra, go forth to the men; for you have come together in harmony with Varuṇa. He has called you here to your own dwelling; as a god, he shall sacrifice to the gods and he shall arrange the people.

The wealthy paths, manifold and of various forms, having all come together, have made wide room for you. Let them all, being in harmony, call upon you here—on this tenth day, O fierce one, well-disposed and according to your will.
This leaf-amulet has arrived, powerful with power, crushing rivals. May the vigor of the gods, the milk of the plants, and their splendor quicken me, never failing.
In me let the *parṇa*-jewel establish sovereign power; in me let it maintain wealth. May I be the foremost, the native-born leader, in the attainment of the kingdom.

That beloved jewel, secret and divine, which the gods deposited in the tree—may the gods grant that to us, along with long life, so that we may wear it. The leaf of Soma has come with mighty force; given by Indra and instructed by Varuṇa, may I hold it, shining brightly, for the sake of long life lasting a hundred autumns.
The leaf-ornament has ascended unto me for great security from harm, so that I may be superior to Aryaman and to those who share his counsel.
O leaf, make me superior to all these people around me: the wise, the chariot-makers, and the smiths who are skilled in thought.
O leaf, make me superior to all these people around me: the kings, the royal officials, the heralds, and the village headmen.
You are a leaf, a protector of the body, sharing a common womb with me, a hero with me, a hero. With the splendor of the year, with that I bind you, O amulet!

A male born from a male, the *aśvattha* tree from the *khadira*—may it slay my enemies, those whom I hate and those who hate me. O *aśvattha*, crush them; O *vaibādha*, crush the defiant enemies! May I be united with Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, and with Mitra and Varuṇa.

Just as the *aśvattha* tree grows within the great ocean, so do you shatter all those whom I hate and those who hate me. O *aśvattha*, with you who move as a conquering bull, ever victorious, may we overcome our rivals.
May Nirṛti seize them with the unloosable nooses of Death. O Aśvattha, [seize] my enemies—those whom I hate and those who hate me.
Just as you, O Aśvattha, climbing the trees, bring them low, so do thou shatter the head of my enemy in every direction and overcome him.
Let them float away downward like a boat cut loose from its mooring. For those driven away by the Vaibādha, there is no returning again.
I drive them away with my mind, with my thought, and with my prayer; we drive them away with a branch of the *aśvattha* tree.
Upon the head of the swift-moving antelope is the remedy; it has destroyed the *kṣetriya* disease with its horn, driving it out in all directions.
The male antelope has followed you with his four feet; O horn, unbind that which is knotted within his heart, the *kṣetriya* disease.
That which shines yonder like a four-sided canopy—with that we destroy all *kṣetriya* disease from your limbs.
Those two auspicious stars in heaven named Vicṛtī (the Liberators), may they release from the field-disease the lowest and the highest bond.
The waters indeed are healers; the waters are the drivers away of disease. The waters are the healers of everything; may they release you from field-disease.
Whatever field-disease has entered you while the pressing was being performed—I know the remedy for that; I destroy the field-disease within you.
With the departure of the stars and the departure of the dawns, may all that is evil drive away from us, and may consumption be driven away.
May Mitra come, harmonizing with the seasons, laying to rest the earth with the rays of dawn; then may Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni bestow upon us a vast kingdom to be laid to rest.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ enjoy this; may Indra and Tvaṣṭṛ welcome my word. I invoke the goddess Aditi, mother of heroes, so that I may stand in the midst of my kinsmen.

I have called upon Soma and Savitṛ with salutations, and all the Ādityas for my protection. May this Agni shine forth for a long time, kindled by his kin who do not oppose him. Stay here; do not go away to another place. The watchful guardian and lord of prosperity has driven you hither. For this desire, may all the gods come together to you, O longing ones.
We bend your minds together, your vows together, and your intentions together. Those of you who are of contrary vows, we cause them all to submit to you.
I seize your minds with my mind; follow my thought with your thoughts. I place your hearts under my control; come as those who follow my path.
Karśapha and Viśapha—Heaven is their father, Earth is their mother. O gods, just as you turned them back, so do you turn this away again.
Without spitting, they held it firm; thus was it done by Manu. I make the *viṣkandha* disease impotent, like the castration of bulls.

Upon a tawny cord, the wise ones bind that tethering-rope; may they make the vigorous Kābava Śuṣma a captive, that he may be brought low. By means of which you, seeking glory, move like the gods through the power of the Asuras' magic—like the monkey among dogs, a source of ruin, and like the tethering-rope of Kābava. For I shall threaten you for your malice, and I shall cause Kābava to be ruined. Like swift chariots, you shall rush forth by means of these curses.
A hundred and one *viṣkandha* demons are stationed throughout the earth; of these, they first took you up as a jewel that destroys the *viṣkandha*.

She who was the first to dwell [in the womb] became a milch-cow for Yama; may she, rich in milk, yield for us in each succeeding year. That night which the gods welcome as she approaches like a milch-cow, she who is the mistress of the year—may she be auspicious for us.
O Night, you whom we worship as the image of the year—endow us with long-lived progeny and with the increase of wealth.
She is indeed she who first shone forth; having entered these other nights, she moves within them. Great powers dwell within her; the bride, the mother of the new-born, has prevailed.
The wooden pressing-stones have raised their voice, preparing the oblation that returns every year. O Ekāṣṭakā, may we be possessed of good offspring and brave sons, and may we be masters of riches.
The footprint of Iḍā is dripping with clarified butter; O Jātavedas, accept the oblations. May there be delight for me in those seven domestic animals of every form.
O Night, may we be in the good favor of the gods, both for nourishment and for increase. Fly away, full ladle; fly back again, well-filled! You enjoy all sacrifices; bring us food and strength.
This year has come, O Eka-aṣṭakā, as your lord; as such, endow our long-lived progeny with the increase of wealth.
Sacrifice to the seasons, to the lords of the seasons, and to the seasonal periods; sacrifice to the years, the full years, the months, and to the Lord of Being.
I sacrifice to you for the seasons, for the seasonal periods, for the months, and for the years; to Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Samṛdh, and the Lord of all that has come into being.
With the *iḍā* we offer oblations; may we worship the gods with clarified butter. May we enter our homes, never losing them, and filled with cattle.
The Ekāṣṭakā, performing penance, gave birth to a child, the greatness Indra. By him the gods overcame their enemies; he became the Lord of Might (*śacīpati*), the slayer of the Dasyus.
O daughter of Prajāpati, you are the son of Indra and the son of Soma. Fulfill our desires; accept our oblation.

I release you by means of this oblation so that you may live, from the unknown wasting disease and from the royal consumption. If the Seizing One has gripped him here, O Indra and Agni, release him from her! Whether his life is exhausted, or whether he has departed, or if he is already at the very presence of Death—him I bring back from the lap of Destruction, making him free from touch for a hundred autumns.
With an oblation that possesses a thousand eyes, a hundred powers, and a hundredfold life, I have brought him back. May Indra lead him through the autumns to the further shore of all misfortune.

Live a hundred autumns, growing strong; a hundred winters, and a hundred springs. For a hundred years, may Indra, Agni, Savitṛ, and Bṛhaspati have brought him here with this oblation of a hundred-fold life.
Enter, O out-breath and in-breath, like two oxen entering their stall! Let other deaths pass away—those they call the "other hundred.
Remain right here, O out-breath and in-breath; do not depart from him! Carry his body and its limbs back again for the sake of old age.

I entrust you to old age; I settle you down for old age. May auspicious old age lead you away; let other deaths go elsewhere—those which they call the other hundred. O Jarimā, you have bound me as one binds an ox with a rope. That death which seized you with a strong noose as you were being born—that very death Bṛhaspati has released from your hands by means of the hands of Truth.
Right here I fix the firm dwelling; may it stand in security, dripping with clarity (*ghṛta*). To that dwelling, O House, may we approach with all our heroes, with good heroes, with unharmed heroes.
Right here, O house, stand firm and secure—rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in pleasant speech; full of vigor, full of clarity, and full of milk; rise up for great good fortune!
You are the supporter, O house, with great meters and abundant grain. May the calf come to you, may the youth come, and may the milch-cows come in the evening, lowing.
May Savitṛ, Vāyu, Indra, and Bṛhaspati, knowing [the way], establish this house. May the Maruts sprinkle it with water and with ghee; may King Bhaga extend our cultivation.

O Mistress of the dwelling, be a refuge and a pleasant place; O Goddess, you were built by the gods in the beginning. Wearing the grass, may you be well-disposed; then grant us wealth along with heroic sons.

By means of *ṛta*, ascend the pillar, O beam; being fierce and shining forth, drive away the enemies. Let not those who dwell near thee come to harm. In this house, O hall, may we live for a hundred autumns with all our heroes.

Hither has come the young boy, hither the calf together with the moving world. Hither have come the jar of flowing liquor and the vessels of curd. O woman, lift up this full jar; pour forth this stream of clarified butter gathered with immortality. Anoint these drinkers with immortality; may it protect this [house] through their sacrifices and charitable works.
I bring these waters, free from disease, destroyers of disease. I enter the house together with the immortal Agni.
Because you were crying out as you flowed together when the serpent was slain, therefore you bear the name "Nadyas" (Rivers); those are your names, O Sindhus.
Because you leaped forward swiftly when impelled by Varuṇa, Indra reached you as you were going; therefore you are called "Āpas" (Waters).
Flowing against their will, you did not open the way for him; Indra, O goddesses, by means of his powers [restrained you], and therefore the name "vār" was assigned to you.
One god alone stood over you as you flowed according to his desire; because they rose up (*ud-aniṣuḥ*) as great ones, therefore water is called *udaka*.

The waters are auspicious; the waters were indeed clarified butter; the waters bear Agni and Soma. May the sharp essence of the sweet-blended [waters], which goes readily to its goal, come to me together with breath and luster.
Now indeed I see, or else I hear; the sound of their voices reaches me. I think that I have partaken of immortality when I was satisfied by you, O golden-hued ones.
Here is your heart, O Waters; here is your calf, O you who follow the cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*). Come here in this manner, O powerful ones (*śakvarī*), to where I settle you.
We unite you with a comfortable cow-pen, with wealth, and with prosperity. By the name of that which was born on this day, we unite you.
May Aryaman unite you; may Pūṣan unite you; may Bṛhaspati unite you; and may Indra, the winner of wealth, unite you—so that whatever riches there are may flourish within me.
Assembling here without fear in this stall, you who provide manure, bearing the honey-sweetness of Soma, come hither free from disease.
O cows, come right here; thrive here like young falcons. Right here indeed procreate! May there be harmony among you within me.
May your stall be auspicious; thrive here like young falcons. Right here indeed procreate! We unite you with me.
O cows, stay with me, the lord of cattle; this is your stall, providing nourishment here. Becoming abundant through the increase of wealth, living and full of life, may we sit near you.
I impel Indra the merchant; may he come to us and be our leader. Driving away the enemy, the waylayer, and the wild beast, may he, the sovereign, be a giver of wealth to me.
Those many paths leading to the gods that travel between heaven and earth—may they favor me with milk and clarified butter, so that having purchased [the goods], I may bring home wealth.
Desiring [success] with fuel and clarified butter, O Agni, I offer this oblation for speed and strength. Praising with a prayer as much as I am able, I offer this divine hymn for a hundredfold gain.

O Agni, forgive us this transgression; whatever distant path we have traveled, may our buying and selling be auspicious, and may the counter-bargain bring me fruit. May you two, being in agreement, enjoy this oblation; may our conduct and our rising be auspicious.

O Gods, that wealth with which I carry on my trade, seeking wealth with that wealth, O Agni—may that become more for me, not less. O Agni, slayer of those who withhold their gifts, ward off the gods with the oblation. O Gods, that wealth with which I carry on my trade, seeking wealth with that wealth, O Agni—may Indra bestow his favor upon it for me, as may Prajāpati, Savitṛ, Soma, and Agni.
With reverence we praise you, O Vaiśvānara Hotṛ; be watchful for us among our offspring, our bodies, our cattle, and our vital breaths.

May we ever bring [offerings] to you at all times, O Jātavedas, as one brings fodder to a standing horse; rejoicing in the increase of wealth and in nourishment, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm, O Agni.

In the morning we invoke Agni; in the morning Indra; in the morning Mitra and Varuṇa; in the morning the Aśvins; in the morning Bhaga, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati; in the morning we invoke Soma and Rudra.

We invoke the fierce Bhaga, the winner in the morning, the son of Aditi who is the distributor. Even the weak man, even the swift man, even the king, thinking "May I partake of Bhaga," calls upon him.
O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, favor this prayer and grant it to us. O Bhaga, increase us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men through our heroes.

And may we now be prosperous, O Blessed Ones—at the departure [of night], at the midday of the days, and at the rising of the sun, O Maghavan—may we abide in the good favor of the gods. May the god Bhaga alone be the possessor of fortune; through him may we be prosperous. As such, O Bhaga, everyone here invokes you; as such, O Bhaga, be our leader here. Let the dawns bow down for the sacrifice, like Dadhikrāvan for the pure station. Like spirited horses drawing a chariot, let them bring hither to me Bhaga, the finder of wealth.
May the auspicious Dawns shine upon us always—rich in horses, rich in cattle, and rich in heroes; yielding clarified butter, swelling from every side. Do you protect us evermore with your blessings!
The sages yoke the ploughs and stretch the yokes apart, the wise ones seeking favor among the gods.
Yoke the ploughs, stretch out the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared womb. May our harvests be abundant and bring us plenty; may the sickles come closer to the ripened grain.
May the plough, sharp-edged, with its iron-pointed share and well-fashioned handle, turn up the earth—cows, sheep, a wagon for the chariot, and a stout, prolific mare.

May Indra hold down the furrow; may Pūṣan protect it. May she yield us milk-filled abundance year after year. May the well-sharpened ploughshares cleave the earth happily; may the ploughmen follow their draft-animals happily. O Śuna and Sīra, being gratified by our oblation, make the plants bear fine fruit for him.
May the draft-oxen be auspicious, may the men be auspicious; may the plough furrow auspiciously. May the traces be bound auspiciously; may you raise the goad auspiciously.
O Śuna and Sīra, may you both take pleasure here with me! With that milk which you created in heaven, sprinkle this [earth]!
O Sītā, we revere you; O auspicious one, turn toward us, so that you may be well-disposed toward us and so that you may bear us good fruit.
May the furrow be anointed with ghee and honey, approved by all the gods and the Maruts! O Sītā, turn toward us with your milk—swelling, rich in strength, and full of ghee.
I dig up this herb, the most powerful of plants, by which one overcomes a rival wife and by which one finds a husband.
O you with upturned leaves, auspicious one, impelled by the gods, victorious one: drive my rival away; make my husband mine alone.
For you do not even mention our name; you take delight in this husband of yours. We shall send your rival to the furthest distance.
I am the superior; may I be superior to those who are superior. My rival wife is beneath me; may she be lower than those who are low.
I am the conqueror, and you, moreover, are the victorious one. Having both become powerful, let us two together overcome my rival.
I have placed the conqueror beneath you; I have placed the more powerful one beneath you. Let your mind run toward me like a cow toward her calf; let it run like water along its path.

Sharpened is this my sacred prayer (*brahman*), sharpened is my heroism and strength; let the dominion (*kṣatra*) of those for whom I am the domestic priest be sharpened and undecaying, victorious. May I unify their kingdom, may I unify their vigor, heroism, and strength. With this oblation, I cut off the arms of my enemies.
Let them fall low, let them be beneath us—those who would attack our patron, the liberal giver. With my sacred prayer I destroy the foes; I raise up my own people.
Sharper than the axe, O Agni, and even sharper than that; sharper than Indra’s thunderbolt are those for whom I am the domestic priest.
I shall sharpen their weapons; I cause their kingdom, with its heroic men, to prosper. May their dominion be invincible and victorious; may all the gods favor their intent.

Let the strengths of the liberal patrons be uplifted; let the shout of the conquering heroes go up. Let the various shouts, tumultuous and accompanied by banners, arise. Let the Maruts, with Indra as their chief, come with their army, O Gods.

O hungry ghosts, conquer! O men, let your arms be fierce; with sharp arrows and strong bows, strike down those who bear fierce weapons. O you of fierce arms, let them be powerless against the weak. Loosed forth, fly away, O arrow-shaft sharpened by prayer (*brahman*). Conquer the enemies, advance against them, and slay their best man after best man; let not one among them escape. This is your seasonal womb, from which born you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and then increase our wealth.
O Agni, speak here for us; turn toward us with a gracious mind. Bestow upon us, O Lord of the People, for you are the giver of wealth to us.
May Aryaman bestow it upon us, may Bhaga, may Bṛhaspati, may the goddesses, and may Sūnṛtā bestow it. May the goddess bestow wealth upon me.
We invoke King Soma for protection, Agni with our songs, Āditya, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati the priest.
O Agni, with your fires, increase our prayer and our sacrifice. O God, impel us to bestow wealth upon us for the sake of giving.

Indra and Vāyu, both of you who are easily invoked, we call here so that all this people may be well-disposed toward us in assembly, and so that they may be desirous of giving to us. Urge Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, Indra, Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the vigorous Savitṛ to grant us gifts.

We have indeed come together at the impulse of strength (vāja), within all these worlds. May he, the wise one, cause even him who is reluctant to give to bestow; and grant us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
May the five regions yield for me; may the wide expanses yield according to my strength. May I attain all my intentions through mind and heart.
May I utter speech that wins cattle; do thou rise up toward me with splendor. May Vāyu encompass me from every side; may Tvaṣṭṛ bestow prosperity upon me.

Those fires which are within the waters, those which are in Vṛtra, those which are in man, those which are in stones, he who has entered the plants and he who has entered the trees—let this be an oblation to those fires.

That which is within the Soma, that which is within the cattle, that which has entered into the birds, that which is in the wild beasts; that which has entered into the bipeds and the quadrupeds—to those Agnis let this be offered as an oblation.
That god Vaiśvānara who travels on the same chariot with Indra, who is the giver of all things, whom I invoke repeatedly in battles as the conqueror—to those Agnis let this be offered as an oblation.
