Savitṛ has come here with the razor; O Vāyu, come with warm water! May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, being of one mind, moisten [the hair]; O wise ones, shave [the hair] for King Soma!
May Aditi shave the beard; may the waters moisten it with luster. May Prajāpati provide for its healing, so that there may be long life and sight.
With that razor wherewith the wise Savitṛ shaved King Soma and Varuṇa, with that, O Brahmans, shave this [beard] of his. May he be possessed of cattle, possessed of horses, and possessed of progeny.
Whatever glory is in Mount Ararāṭi, in gold, in cattle, in flowing wine, and in the sweetness of honey—may that be in me.

O Aśvins, lords of splendor, anoint me with the honey of the bee, so that I may utter speech full of luster among the people. May Prajāpati establish in me brilliance, glory, and whatever essence belongs to the sacrifice, as firmly as the sky is fixed in heaven.

As is the case with meat, as with wine, as with dice upon the gaming board, as the mind of a man full of desire is struck down toward a woman—so, O inviolable cow, let your mind be struck down toward your calf. As an elephant follows step for step after a female elephant, as the mind of a man full of desire is struck down toward a woman—so, O inviolable cow, let your mind be struck down toward your calf.

Just as the rim, just as the felly, just as the nave is upon the rim; just as the mind of a man full of desire is fixed upon a woman, so let your mind, O inviolable cow, be fixed upon your calf. Whatever food I eat in many forms—gold, horse, cow, goat, or sheep—whatever I have accepted, may Agni, as the Hotṛ priest, make that a well-offered oblation.

Whatever has come to me as an offering, whether formally sacrificed or not, given by the ancestors and approved by men—from which my mind leaps up as if in joy—may Agni, as the Hotṛ-priest, make that a well-offered oblation.

O Gods, whatever food I eat through falsehood—whether promising it or not promising it, whether I vow to give it or not—may that food become auspicious and sweet for me through the greatness of the mighty Vaiśvānara. Just as the black antelope spreads itself according to its will, fashioning its beautiful forms through the creative power (*māyā*) of the Asura, so may this hymn of yours, by its force, join limb with limb together.
As the hoof-print of a wild ass was made large by the wind, so may your hoof-print increase as much as the hoof-print of a wild ass.
As far as the foot of the domestic animal, the wild ass, the elephant, and the donkey; as far as that of the swift horse—so far may your hoof grow.

May Varuṇa come here, may Soma, Agni, and Bṛhaspati come here with the Vasus! O kinsmen, all of you, being of one mind, approach the splendor of this formidable lord who knows all. That vigor which is within your hearts, and that intention which has entered your minds—I bind them together with this oblation of clarified butter. O kinsmen, let your delight be in me! Stay right here; do not depart from us. May Pūṣan make a pathless way for you beyond. May Vāstoṣpati call out after you; O kinsmen, let your delight be in me!

May your bodies be united, may your minds be united, and may your vows be united. May this Brahmaṇaspati and Bhaga bring you into harmony. This is the unification of your mind, and this is the unification of your heart; and by that which is the essence of Bhaga, I bring you into harmony. Just as the Ādityas were united with the Vasus, and the fierce Maruts were united without malice, even so, O three-named one, being without malice, make these people here of one mind.
Drive that rival away from his home who attacks us; with this oblation that excludes others, Indra has cast him out.
May Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drive him to the furthest distance, from which he shall not return for eternal years.

Let him go beyond the three distant realms; let him go beyond the five peoples. Let him go beyond the three luminous spheres, from whence he shall not return for eternal years, as long as the sun remains in heaven.
Those who sit around him and prepare him for sight—let Agni, fully kindled by his tongues, rise up from the heart.
I take hold of the footprint of Agni Sāṃtapana for the sake of long life—he, the true-seer, whose smoke rising from his mouth one beholds;

he who knows his fuel, prepared by the Kṣatriya, does not set foot upon the path to death. Those who pursue him do not slay him, nor does he fall into the pit; that Kṣatriya who, being wise, utters the name of Agni for the sake of long life.

The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, and this entire living world has stood firm. The mountains have stood fast; I have established the horses in their place. I call upon that guardian who has reached the farthest goal, who has reached the downward path, who knows the turning back and the returning. O Jātavedas, cause him to turn back! May there be a hundred turnings for you, a thousand returnings for you; with these, bring us back again.
By that true oblation, let this man swell again. Let him prosper with the essence of the wife whom they have brought for him;

let him prosper with milk, let him prosper with royal power, let him prosper with wealth of a thousandfold luster. May these two be undecaying. Tvaṣṭṛ produced the wife; Tvaṣṭṛ [produced] you as her husband. May Tvaṣṭṛ grant you both a thousand lifespans and long life.
May this Lord of the Cloud, the nourisher, protect us; may he grant us peerless prosperity in our homes.
O Lord of the Cloud, do thou bestow strength upon our houses; let nourishment and wealth come to us.

O God, you are the nourisher of the thousandfold increase; grant us of that, bestow upon us of that, and may we be partakers of that which is yours. He flies through the mid-air, beholding all beings; with that greatness of the divine dog, let us worship you with this oblation.
Those three Kālakāñjas who are stationed like gods in heaven—I invoke them all for protection and for his safety.

In the waters is your birth, in heaven is your dwelling; your greatness is within the ocean and upon the earth. With that greatness of yours which belongs to the divine dog, we shall worship you with this oblation.
You are the restrainer; you extend your two hands and drive away the demons. Grasping offspring and wealth, this has become the *parihasta* (the hand-encircler).
O *parihasta*, hold fast the womb so that the embryo may be placed therein. At the appointed time, bestow a son; bring him to us at our arrival.
The bracelet which Aditi wore out of desire for a son—Tvaṣṭṛ fastened it upon her so that she might give birth to a son.

As he approaches and has arrived, I take his name from afar: "I win for Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the son of Vasu, the lord of a hundred powers—the path by which the Aśvins carried Sūryā, the daughter of Savitṛ; by that same path, Bhaga has told me, 'Bring Jayā hither.'"
O Indra, with that great golden goad of yours which bestows wealth, by means of it, O Lord of Might, grant me a wife for procreation.
Fly away, you disgrace, like a bird from its nest; let the Sun provide the remedy, and let the Moon shine light upon you.
One is tawny, one is falcon-colored, one is black, and two are ruddy. I have seized the names of them all; depart, you who do not slay heroes!
The woman who brings no offspring, the Rāmāyaṇī, and the Apacit shall fly away; Glau shall fly away from here, and he shall perish like a snail.
Enjoying your own oblation with the mind, Svāhā! With the mind I offer this which is here.
Into whose terrible mouth I offer these captives for their release—whom the people call "Earth," but whom I know from every side as Nirṛti.

O Earth, be full of oblations; this is your portion which belongs to us. Release these and those from sin, Svāhā! Thus, O Nirṛti, may you be free from malice toward us; loosen these iron fetters. Yama gives you back to me; let there be homage to that Yama, to Death. You were bound here upon the iron post by thousands of deaths. In harmony with Yama and the Fathers, cause him to ascend to the highest heaven.
May this divine Vanaspati ward it off; the consumption that has entered into him—that very thing the gods have warded off.
By the word of Indra, and by the word of Mitra and Varuṇa, and by the speech of all the gods, we ward off your consumption.
Just as Vṛtra held back these waters flowing in every direction, so do I ward off your consumption with Agni Vaiśvānara.

This bull is the bull of Indra, the bull of heaven, the bull of earth; may you be the sole bull of all that exists. The ocean rules over the flowing streams, Agni is the master of the earth, and the moon rules over the stars; may you be the sole bull.

You are the sovereign of the Asuras, the summit of men; you are the sharer of half the realm of the gods—be you the sole bull. I have brought you here; you have come within. Stand firm, immovable. Let all the subjects desire you; let not the kingdom fall away from you.
Be right here, do not waver; like a mountain, stand immovable. Like Indra, stand firm here; uphold the kingdom here.
Indra has established this [king] as firm with a firm oblation. For him may Soma speak in favor, and may this Brahmanaspati as well.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, and firm is this entire moving world. Firm are these mountains; firm is this king of the people.
May King Varuṇa make your [rule] firm, and may the god Bṛhaspati make it firm. May both Indra and Agni maintain your kingdom as firm.
Firm and unshakable, crush the enemies; cast down those who act as foes. May all the quarters of space be of one mind and turned toward you; may the assembly be favorable for you here, O Firm One.
This head of the beloved one, which has been given with Soma’s virility—by that which is born from it, we cause your heart to burn.
We burn away your heart; we burn away your mind. Like smoke following the wind, let your mind follow after me alone.
For me, O Mitra and Varuṇa, for me, O divine Sarasvatī, for me, let both ends of the earth cast you together into the middle.
That arrow which Rudra shot at your limbs and at your heart—that today we pull out from you in all directions.
Those hundred vessels of yours that are distributed throughout your limbs—from all of them, we summon forth the poisons.
Homage to you, O Rudra, when you are being discharged; homage to you when you are aimed; homage to you when you are being released; homage to you when you have fallen.
They have ploughed this barley with eight teams and six yokes; by that means, drive the affliction from your body away toward the west.
Downward blows the wind, downward shines the sun; downward the cow is milked—downward let your affliction go.
Truly, the waters are healers, the waters are the drivers away of disease; the waters are the healers of everything. May they provide healing for you.
Become one whose speed is like the wind when you are yoked, O steed; go forth at Indra’s impulse, swift as thought. Let the all-knowing Maruts harness you; may Tvaṣṭṛ bestow swiftness in your feet.

O steed, that speed of yours which is hidden in secret, or that which moved within the hawk and the wind when you were bestowed [upon us]—with that strength, O powerful one, being victorious in the assembly, win the race with your might. Your body, O steed, leading your own body, let it run for our welfare and for your protection; may the unswerving great god, like light in heaven, measure out his own support.
Yama, Mṛtyu, Aghamāra, Nirṛtha, Babhru, Śarva the archer, and Nīlaśikhaṇḍa—the divine hosts who have risen up with their army—let them spare our heroes.

With thought, oblations, fervor, and clarified butter, I pay homage to Śarva the archer and to King Bhava; I offer salutations to these who are worthy of reverence. Let those whose poison is evil lead it away from us.
Protect us from evil poisons and from slaughter, O All-Gods, O Maruts, possessors of all wealth! May we abide in the good graces of Agni and Soma, Varuṇa of pure strength, and of Vāta and Parjanya.
We bend your minds together, your vows together, and your intentions together. Those who are of contrary vows, them among you we cause to bend in harmony.

I seize your minds with my mind; follow my thought with your thoughts. I place your hearts under my control; follow the path of my departure. Woven are Heaven and Earth for me, woven is the goddess Sarasvatī for me; woven are Indra and Agni for me—may we succeed in this, O Sarasvatī!
The Aśvattha tree, the seat of the gods, is in the third heaven from here. There the gods found Kuṣṭha, the manifestation of immortality.
A golden ship with golden moorings moved in the sky; there the gods found Kuṣṭha, the flower of immortality.
You are the embryo of plants, and the embryo of the snowy mountains; you are the embryo of every living being—make this man of mine free from disease.

The many herbs whose king is Soma, possessing a hundredfold vision, impelled by Bṛhaspati—may they release us from distress. May they release me from the curse, and also from that which pertains to Varuṇa, and from the fetter of Yama, and from every offense against the gods.
Whatever we have committed with the eye, with the mind, or with speech, whether waking or sleeping—may Soma purify those things for us by his own power.

Overpowering is the sacrifice, overpowering is Agni, overpowering is Soma, overpowering is Indra. May I be the overcomer of all hostile armies; thus let us worship with this oblation at the Agnihotra.

Let there be self-sustaining power for Mitra and Varuṇa, the wise ones; let them swell our princely dominion here with honey. Drive far away Destruction to a distance; release us from whatever sin we have committed.

Rejoice after this hero; O friends, rally together after the fierce Indra! He who conquers the hosts, who wins the cattle, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, who conquers the race and crushes it with his might—Indra shall conquer, he shall not be conquered; as supreme ruler among kings, let him rule. Worthy of praise, worthy of invocation, worthy of homage, and worthy of being approached, be thou here an object of reverence.
Thou, O Indra, art the supreme ruler seeking glory; thou hast become the overcomer of men. Do thou rule these divine clans; may thy dominion be long-lived and undecaying.

O Indra, you are the king of the eastern quarter; O slayer of Vṛtra, slayer of enemies, you are the protector of the northern quarter. Wherever the rivers flow, that is your conquest; as the Bull, you go forth from the south, worthy of invocation. O Indra, before distress reaches us from afar, I call upon you; I invoke the fierce one, the perceiver, the one with many names, the sole-born.
Whatever weapon of an army rises today, seeking to strike us down, we place the two arms of Indra all around it for protection.
We entrust ourselves to the arms of Indra, the protector on all sides; may he protect us. O divine Savitṛ, O King Soma, make me well-disposed for my well-being.
The gods have given; Sūrya has given; Heaven has given; Earth has given. The three Sarasvatīs, being of one mind, have given this poison-destroyer.
O Upajīkas, with that water which you poured upon the desert, O gods, by that which is sent forth by the gods, do you now corrupt this poison.
You are the daughter of the Asuras; you are the sister of the gods. Born from heaven and earth, you have rendered the poison powerless.
Be virile, breathe forth, grow, and spread out! May the penis grow according to its proper measure; with it, strike the woman.
With that by which they urge the plow, with which they drive the sick man, with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, draw his penis like a bowstring.
I draw your bond tight, like a string upon a bow. Step forward like a seer toward a red steed, never tiring.
Just as this vehicle, O Aśvins, comes together and turns back again, so may your mind come together with me and turn back toward me.

I draw your mind toward me, as a king’s horse draws its back; like grass severed by a storm, let your mind coil itself around me. From the hands of Bhaga, the swift one, I bring forth this enticement: of *āñjana*, *madugha*, *kuṣṭha*, and *nalada*.
May Bṛhaspati make for you a bond; may Savitṛ make a bond. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, and the Aśvins make a bond.
I bind together those who are highest, those who are lowest, and likewise those who are in the middle. Indra has encompassed them with a bond; you, O Agni, bind them together.
Those who come here to battle, having raised their banners in ranks—Indra has encompassed them with a bond; you, O Agni, bind them together.
With this seizing, with this binding, we seize our enemies. Those who are their out-breaths, may we cut off their in-breaths with our own life-force.
I have made this seizing, sharpened by austerity and by Indra. O Agni, seize those enemies who are here against us!
May Indra and Agni, and King Soma, the two allies, seize them. May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, make this seizing for us against our enemies.
Just as the mind flies swiftly away with its mental conceptions, even so, O cough, fly forth along the swift course of the mind.

Just as a well-sharpened arrow flies swiftly away, so do you, O cough, fly forth along the expanse of the earth. Just as the rays of the sun fly swiftly away, so do you, O cough, fly forth along the flow of the ocean.
Upon your path hither and your path thither, let flowering durvā grass grow; let there arise either a spring or a lake filled with lotuses.
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean; our houses are in the middle of the lake—turn your faces away from them.
With the caul of winter, O house, we enclose thee. May Agni make medicine for us, so that we may become possessed of cool pools. O Viśvajit, entrust me to Trāyamāṇā.

O Trāyamāṇā, protect all our bipeds and our quadrupeds, and whatever is our own. O Viśvajit, entrust me to Trāyamāṇā. O Trāyamāṇā, protect all our bipeds and our quadrupeds, and whatever is our own. O Viśvajit, entrust me to Trāyamāṇā. O Trāyamāṇā, protect all our bipeds and our quadrupeds, and whatever is our own. O Viśvajit, protect all our bipeds and our quadrupeds, and whatever is our own.

O Viśvajit, entrust me to Kalyāṇī; O Kalyāṇī, protect all our bipeds and whatever quadrupeds are ours. O Kalyāṇī, entrust me to Sarvavid; O Sarvavid, protect all our bipeds and whatever quadrupeds are ours.
O Medhā, you are the first among us; come with cattle and horses, come with the rays of the sun; you are worthy of sacrifice for us.

I invoke for the protection of the gods that foremost wisdom which is possessed of sacred formulation (*brahman*), impelled by *brahman*, praised by the seers (*ṛṣi*), and drunk in by those practicing the life of sacred study (*brahmacārin*).
That wisdom which the *Ṛbhus* know, that wisdom which the *Asuras* know, and that auspicious wisdom which the seers know—that we cause to enter into me.
O Agni, with that wisdom which the seers, the creators of beings, and the wise know, make me wise today with that wisdom.

Wisdom at evening, wisdom at dawn, wisdom throughout the midday—through the rays of the sun, we cause wisdom to enter by means of our speech. The *pippalī* is a medicine for the pierced and a medicine for the deeply wounded; the gods fashioned it, saying, "This is sufficient for living. The *pippalī* plants conversed as they came forth from their birth: "The man whom we reach while he is alive shall not suffer harm."
The Asuras dug thee in; the gods dug thee out again. Thou art the remedy for one afflicted by wind, and the remedy for one who has been cast down.

For thou, O Agni, art the ancient one worthy of praise at the sacrifices; from of old thou hast sat as the Hotṛ-priest, both new and ever-present. Fill thy own body with nourishment, O Agni, and win for us prosperity through sacrifice.
Born under Jyeṣṭhaghnyā, deliver him from the uprooting power of Yama’s two looseners (vicṛtī). May he lead him beyond all misfortunes for the sake of long life lasting a hundred autumns.
On a tiger-like day this hero was born; being born under a lunar mansion, may he be a source of good heroes. Let him not slay his father as he grows, nor let him harm his mother, his progenitress.
O Agni, release this man of mine! He who is bound and well-restrained yet prattles on—out of that, you shall make for him a portion when he has become sober again.
May Agni pacify that which is inflamed in your mind; being wise, I prepare a remedy so that you shall not be driven mad.
O God, I, the wise one, prepare a remedy for this man who has been driven mad and rendered insane by a Rākṣasa, so that he shall no longer be maddened.
May the Apsarases restore you, may Indra restore you, may Bhaga restore you; may all the gods restore you so that you shall no longer be intoxicated.
May this one not slay the eldest among them; O Agni, protect him from being uprooted. Knowing the way, loosen the snares of Grāhī; may all the gods acknowledge this for you.
Unloose their snares, O Agni—those three by which they were bound threefold. Knowing the way, loosen the snares of Grāhī; release father, son, and mother—all of them.

O Pūṣan, those snares with which he who has superseded his younger brother is bound, fastened limb by limb, and ensnared—may they be loosened for you, for your bonds are indeed meant to be released; wipe away, O Pūṣan, the misfortunes of the slayer of the embryo.
The gods wiped this sin away upon Trita; Trita wiped it away among mankind. Therefore, if the seizing spirit has reached you, may the gods destroy it for you by means of the sacred word (brahman).
Enter the rays of light, O Evil One, or follow the rising mists; vanish after the froth of the rivers, O Pūṣan, slayer of the embryo, wipe away our misfortunes!

The twelvefold [sin] deposited by Trita, the human transgressions wiped away—should the seizing grip have reached you from that, may the gods destroy it for you by means of the sacred word (*brahman*).
O Gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed, O Ādityas, release us from that by means of the Truth (*ṛta*) through Truth.
O worshipful Ādityas, release us here by means of the Truth through Truth. Since we, though desiring to perform the sacrifice, were unable to accomplish it, O bearers of the sacrifice;
though offering clarified butter with the fat-filled ladle as sacrificers, we were unable to accomplish it, O all you Gods, even though we desired to do so.
Whatever sins we have committed, whether knowingly or unknowingly, O All-Gods, being of one accord, deliver us from that!
Whether waking or sleeping, if I, a sinner, have committed an offense, may the past and the future release me from it as if from a wooden post!
Like one released from a wooden post, like one who has sweated and bathed away impurity, like clarified butter purified by a strainer—may all the Gods cleanse me from sin!

Whatever offense the farmers, seeking food, committed in former times while digging for a path, not through knowledge but by their labor—I offer that before King Vaivasvata; may our food thereafter be worthy of sacrifice and full of sweetness.

May Vaivasvata grant us our portion; may he, whose share is honey, mingle it with honey. Whatever sin has come upon us, sent by our mother, or whatever wrong was committed and provoked by our father—[may he forgive that].

If this sin has come upon us from our mother, or from our father, or from our brother, or from our son, or from our mind—if all the fathers who accompany us, may the wrath of them all be auspicious. Whatever debt I have incurred that remains unpaid, by which I move as a tribute-bearer for Yama—O Agni, through this [act] I become free from that debt; you know how to loosen all fetters.
Remaining right here, we give this back; being alive, we deliver it to those who are alive. Whatever grain I have consumed on loan—O Agni, through this I become free from that debt.

Free from debt in this world, free from debt in the next, may we be free from debt in the third world. May we dwell free from debt upon all paths—those leading to the gods and those leading to the fathers.
Whatever sins we have committed with our two hands, seeking to win the rolling of the dice, may the two Apsarases, Ugrapashyā and Ugrajit, grant us release from that debt today.

O Ugrapashyā, O Rāṣṭrabhṛt, whatever debts were incurred through the play of dice, may you grant us release from them. May he who seeks to exact debt from us in the world of Yama not draw us in with his cord.

To whomsoever I owe a debt, whose wife I approach, and whomsoever I come to as a suppliant—O Gods, let them speak words superior to mine; O divine consorts and Apsarases, take heed of this! When I incur a debt while not gambling, or when I promise to pay but fail to do so, O Agni—may Vaiśvānara, our most excellent protector, lead us upward to the world of the righteous. I declare before Vaiśvānara whatever debt or agreement I have made among the gods. He knows how to loosen all these bonds; then may we be united with what is cooked (the ripened reward).
May Vaiśvānara, the purifier, cleanse me when I run toward a compact or a direction without knowing it, merely begging in my mind; whatever sin is therein, I cast that away.

If we have harmed the atmosphere, the earth, or the sky, or if we have injured our mother or our father—may this Gārhapatya Agni lead us up from that to the world of the righteous. May Mother Earth and Aditi be our place of birth; may the atmosphere as our brother protect us from imprecation. May Father Heaven grant us peace from the ancestral realm; having reached my kin, may I not fall away from the world. Where those of kind hearts and good deeds rejoice, having cast off disease from their own bodies—there in heaven, with unshriveled limbs and undiminished, may we behold our parents and our children.
Untie the snares from us—the nooses of Varuṇa, whether they be the highest or the lowest. Drive away from us evil dreams and misfortune; then may we go to the world of the righteous.
Whether you are bound in wood, or in a rope, or bound upon the earth, or by speech—from all that, may this Gārhapatya Agni lead us up to the world of the righteous.
The two auspicious stars named Vicṛtau have risen. May they bestow immortality here; may the release of the bound proceed forth.
Open wide, make room; release the bound one from his bond. Like an embryo fallen from the womb, dwell along all the paths.
Knowing this, O Viśvakarman, first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), I bestow this portion upon you. May we, having given what was granted by us beyond old age, cross over along the unbroken thread.

Some cross along the stretched thread—those for whom the ancestral gift has been handed down through the traditional path. Others, lacking kinship, give and bestow; if they learn how to give, that very act leads them to heaven.

Take hold of one another, support one another; those who have faith attain this world. Whatever cooked food has been served for you in the fire, take refuge together as husband and wife for its protection.
With my mind, I ascend after the great sacrifice as it proceeds, sharing a common womb through austerity. O Agni, invited beyond old age, may we rejoice in communal feasting in the third heaven.

These pure, purified, and sacrificial women I set down separately in the hands of the Brahmins. Whatever desire I have for which I sprinkle you here, may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, grant that to me.
O fellow-dwellers, I entrust this treasure to you, which Jātavedas shall bring hither. The sacrificer will follow in well-being; recognize him in the highest heaven.
The gods dwelling together in the highest heaven knew him; they found his place here. The sacrificer shall follow after in well-being. Make manifest for him his sacrifices and charitable works!
O gods, you are fathers; O fathers, you are gods. Who I am, that I am.
I cook; I give; I sacrifice; may what has been given by me not fail.
O King, establish yourself in the firmament; let this be established there for us. Know our merit, O King; as a god, be well-disposed toward us.

From the great heaven, from the mid-air, a drop of water has flown down toward me with its essence. O Agni, may I be united with power, with milk, with the meters, with sacrifices, and with the deeds of the righteous. Whether it fell from a tree as a fruit, or from the mid-air—that indeed is Vāyu himself. Wherever it has touched my body or my garment, may the Waters drive away Destruction to a distance.

The fragrant ointment is prosperity; gold is splendor and indeed purity. All purifiers are spread out over us; may neither Destruction nor Enmity overcome me. O Lord of the Forest, may you be firm of limb, our friend, a furtherer, and a possessor of brave sons. You are bound with cow-hides; be strong! May your rider conquer all that is to be won.

From heaven and from earth strength has been uplifted; from the trees vigor has been brought hither. Worship with an oblation the chariot—the thunderbolt of Indra, the might of the waters, encompassed by cattle.
The vigor of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, and the navel of Varuṇa—O divine chariot, taking pleasure in this our offering of oblations, accept these gifts.
Make the earth and the sky resound; let the world scattered in many places take heed of you. O drum, in alliance with Indra and the gods, drive our enemies far, even to the furthest distance.
Roar aloud; bestow strength and vigor upon us. Thunder forth, driving away all misfortunes. O drum, drive calamity away from here; you are the fist of Indra—be firm!
Conquer yonder foe; let these men conquer. Let the drum speak out with its signal-call. Let our horse-winged warriors fly together; O Indra, let our chariot-fighters be victorious!
O Lord of the Forest, O Herb, leave nothing remaining—not even a trace of flesh—of the abscess, the phlegm, the blood, or the erysipelas.
Those two swellings of yours, O Balāsa, which remain in the armpit or have taken refuge in the testicles—I know the remedy for that; the *cīpudru* tree is the visible cure.

Whatever erysipelas is in the limbs, whatever is in the ears, or whatever is in the eyes—we tear away the erysipelas, the abscess, and the disease of the heart. We drive away that unknown wasting disease downward and cast it out.
When the stars made Śakadhūma their king, they bestowed upon him prosperity, saying, "May this kingdom belong to him.
May there be prosperity for us at midday; may there be prosperity for us in the evening. May there be prosperity for us at the dawn of days; may there be prosperity for us by night.
From day and night, from the stars, and from the sun and moon—O King Śakadhūma, grant us prosperity!

To you who have made our days auspicious in the evening, at night, and likewise by day—to you, O King of the Constellations, son of Śakadhūma, be perpetual homage! Together with Bhaga, with the Śāṃśapa tree, and with Indra who is accompanied by Medinī, I make myself fortunate. May my enemies flee away!
With that same Bhaga and splendor by which you overcame the trees, make me fortunate. May my enemies flee away!

That Bhaga who is blind, who returns again, and who is placed within the trees—by him make me beloved; let the enemies flee away. This is the love-spell of the *rathajit* and *rāthajiteyī* Apsarases. O gods, send forth the Love-god! Let him burn with longing for me.
"May he remember me," "May my beloved remember me"—O gods, send forth the god of love so that he may feel longing for me.
Just as he remembers me, so may I never remember him; O gods, send forth the god of love (Smara) so that he shall grieve after me.
Exhilarate me, O Maruts; exhilarate me, O Atmosphere; O Agni, do you exhilarate me! Let that one burn after me!
I drive away your mental anguish from the head and from the feet. O Gods, send forth the god of love (Smara)! Let that one burn after me!
O Anumati, agree to this; O Akuti, accept this homage. O gods, send forth the god of love; let that one burn with longing for me.
Whether you run three leagues or five leagues—the distance of a horse—thence you shall return again; may you be a father to our sons.

That *smara* (mind/love) which the gods poured into the waters, burning with fever along with the *adhyā*, that I heat for you by the law of Varuṇa. That *smara* which all the gods poured into the waters, burning with fever along with the *adhyā*, that I heat for you by the law of Varuṇa.

The passion that Indrāṇī poured into the waters, burning with intense heat along with her longing—that I subject you to by the law of Varuṇa. The passion that Indra and Agni poured into the waters, burning with intense heat along with their longing—that I subject you to by the law of Varuṇa.
The passion that Mitra and Varuṇa poured into the waters, burning with intense heat along with their longing—that I subject you to by the law of Varuṇa.

The god who bound this girdle upon me, who fastened it, and who has joined us together; by whose command we move about—may he seek our welfare and may he release us. You are invoked, you are invoked with oblations; you are the weapon of the seers. O girdle, eating first of the vow, become a slayer of my enemies. Since I am a student of sacred knowledge (brahmacārī) begging for a person from the being for Yama, him I bind with the sacred word (brahman), with austerity, with exertion, and with this girdle.

The daughter of Faith, born from austerity, has become the sister of the seers who are the creators of beings. O girdle, bestow upon us thought and wisdom; furthermore, grant us austerity and sensory power.
You whom the ancient seers, the creators of beings, wore around them—do you, O girdle, embrace me for the sake of long life.
May this thunderbolt of Truth satisfy him; may it strike down his kingdom and take away his life. May it shatter his neck-bones and crush his nape-joints, just as the Lord of Might did to Vṛtra.
Lower and lower than the higher ones, hidden from the earth, do not spring up! Struck down by the thunderbolt, may you lie prostrate!
Seek out him who conquers; slay indeed him who conquers! O Thunderbolt, as he conquers, strike his hair-parting downward along its course.
When I eat, I produce strength; thus do I take up the thunderbolt, felling his shoulders as the Lord of Might (Indra) did those of Vṛtra.

When I drink, I drink up completely; like the ocean, I am a drinker-up. Having drunk up his vital breaths, we drink him up entirely. When I swallow, I swallow up completely; like the ocean, I am a swallower-up. Having swallowed his vital breaths, we swallow him up entirely.
O herb, you are divine, born upon the divine earth; as such, O Nitatnī, we dig you up from the hair for the sake of strengthening.
Strengthen those of old, give birth to those unborn, and make those already born more excellent.

That hair of yours which falls out, along with its root, and that which is torn away—this I sprinkle upon it with a plant containing all healing powers. That hair-increasing herb which Jamadagni dug up for his daughter, Vītahavya brought from the houses of Asita.
They were to be measured with a bridle, to be measured by a fathom. Let your black hairs grow all around your head like reeds.
Strengthen the root, hold fast the tip, and cause the middle to grow out, O herb! Let your black hairs grow all around your head like reeds.
You, O herb, are the most excellent of plants, renowned far and wide. Make this man of mine today a eunuch, one who wears a crest-ornament.
Make him a eunuch wearing a head-ornament; moreover, make him wear a turban. Then may Indra, with his two pressing-stones, split both his testicles asunder.
O eunuch, I have made you a eunuch; O impotent one, I have made you impotent; O sapless one, I have made you sapless. We place a turban upon his head and a water-pot upon it.

Those two testicles of yours, O god, which were fashioned by the gods and in which virility resides—those I split apart with a peg upon the testicles of that woman, just as women split a reed with a stone for the sake of a mattress. Thus I split your penis upon the testicles of that woman. You have grown up as a Nyastikā plant, making me fortunate; you have a hundred spreading shoots and thirty-three descending roots.
With that thousand-leaved plant, I dry up your heart.
May your heart wither within me, and may your mouth wither as well; then wither away through desire for me, and wander about with a parched mouth.
O enchanting one, endowed with lotuses, tawny and beautiful, drive them together! Drive her and me together, and make our hearts one.

Just as the mouth of one who has drunk no water dries up, so may you dry up with desire for me; then go about with a parched mouth. Just as a mongoose, having severed [the snake], joins the serpent together again, even so, O powerful one, join together what has been severed by desire.

Those two tigers that have descended, desiring to devour their father and mother—O Brahmanaspati, O Jatavedas, make those two teeth auspicious for them. Eat the rice, eat the barley, and also the beans, and also the sesame. This portion has been set aside for you both for the bestowing of treasures; O teeth, do not harm the father and the mother.
Invoked together, yoked, gentle, and most auspicious are the two teeth; let the terrible nature of your bodies depart elsewhere. O teeth, do not harm the father and the mother.

May Vāyu bring these together; may Tvaṣṭṛ sustain them for prosperity. May Indra speak in their favor; may Rudra provide for their abundance. With a red axe, fashion a pair upon the two ears. May the Aśvins create the mark; may that be multiplied through progeny.
Just as the gods and asuras, and just as humans [have done], so do you two, O Aśvins, create a sign for a thousandfold prosperity.
Rise up, become abundant through your own greatness, O barley! Crush all vessels; let not the divine thunderbolt strike you down.
O divine barley that hears us, where we call out to you, there rise up like the sky, be like the inexhaustible ocean.

Inexhaustible be your Upasad rites; let the heaps of grain be inexhaustible. Let those who bestow be inexhaustible; let those who consume be inexhaustible. Those who by their devotion brought forth the summit of speech, or those who with their mind spoke the eternal truths—having increased by the third sacred formulation (*brahman*), they perceived the name of the Cow by the fourth.

He knows the father, he knows the mother; he becomes the son, he becomes the one who bestows wealth again. He spread out the sky, the mid-air, and the light; he became this entire universe; he brought it all hither.

Atharvan, the father, kinsman of the gods, the embryo of the mother, the vital breath of the father, the youth who has conceived this sacrifice with his mind—proclaim him for us here; speak of him here.

Through this manifestation, generating mighty deeds—for he is indeed glowing—he is the wide path for the sacrifice. He rose up toward the support, the summit of the honey; by his own body, he extended his body.
With one and with ten, O well-invoked one, with two and with twenty for our sacrifice, and with three and with thirty yoke-pairs you carry [the offerings]; O Vāyu, unyoke them here.
By means of sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances. They, the majestic ones, attained the firmament where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide.
The sacrifice came into being; it has come into existence; it was born; and it has grown again. It became the overlord of the gods; may it bestow wealth upon us.
When the gods, being mortal in mind, sacrificed with oblation to the immortal gods, may we rejoice there in the highest heaven; may we behold that at the rising of the sun.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation, was there indeed anything more powerful than that, when they sacrificed with the *vihavya* hymn?
Confused, the gods even sacrificed with a dog; they sacrificed in many ways with the limbs of a cow. He who has perceived this sacrifice with his mind—proclaim him to us here, proclaim him!

Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-air; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son. All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what is to be born. We invoke for our protection the great Mother of those who observe holy vows, the consort of Cosmic Order (Ṛta)—the mighty sovereign, the undecaying, the far-reaching, the well-sheltering Aditi, the excellent guide.

May we ascend for our well-being the earth, the good protector, the heaven, the faultless, Aditi who provides excellent refuge and excellent guidance—the divine ship with fair oars, sinless and leakless. Now, at the impulse of strength, let us celebrate with our speech the great Mother named Aditi, in whose lap is the wide mid-air; may she grant us a triple-layered shelter. I have performed this rite for the sons of Diti, for Aditi, for the lofty and unfailing gods; for their domain is deep-seated like the ocean, and there is no one whatsoever beyond them to whom one may offer homage.

From good go forth to better; may Bṛhaspati be your leader. Then, in the choice portion of this earth, make this man one whose enemies are far away and who possesses all heroes. Pūṣan was born upon the far path of paths, upon the far path of heaven, and upon the far path of earth. He moves to and fro between both most beloved dwellings, knowing them well.
Pūṣan knows all these regions; may he lead us by the path most free from fear. Bestowing well-being, glowing, possessing all heroes, may he go before us, watchful and knowing.
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never come to harm; we here are your praisers.
May Pūṣan stretch forth his right hand from beyond; may he bring back to us what we have lost, and may we be reunited with that which is lost.

That breast of yours which is ever-yielding, which is bliss-bestowing, which seeks out happiness, which is easy to invoke, and which is most generous—that by which you nourish all desirable things, O Sarasvatī, bring that here for us to suck. That broad thunder of yours, the lofty divine banner which encompasses this entire world—O Goddess, do not strike our crop with lightning, nor destroy it with the rays of the sun.
May the Assembly and the Council, the two daughters of Prajāpati who are in harmony, protect me. May he with whom I meet instruct me; may I speak what is pleasing among those gathered, O Fathers.
We know your name, O Assembly, you are indeed named "The Unharmed. Whatever members sit in this assembly, may they all be of one voice with me.
From these who are seated here, I take the splendor and the insight. Make me the brother of this entire gathering, O Indra.

Your mind that has gone away, whether it be bound here or there—we draw it back to you; let your mind delight in me. Just as the rising sun takes up the splendors of the stars, so do I take up the luster of both women and men who are my enemies.
As many as you see me approaching among my rivals, from all those sleeping enemies, like the rising sun, I take up their luster.
I praise that god Savitṛ, the protector of the two worlds, whose will is wisdom; I praise him who possesses true impulsion, who bestows jewels, and who holds dear thoughts.
Whose lofty splendor has shone forth in its impelling power—the golden-handed one of excellent wisdom has measured out the light from his creative impulse.
For you, O God, have impelled the highest form for the first father, and for him, the wide expanse; then, O Savitar, impel toward us day by day many desirable things and abundant cattle.

The domestic god Savitar, the most excellent, bestows treasures and long lives upon the fathers. Let him drink the Soma; let him rejoice in it when he is sacrificed to; even the wanderer moves according to his law.
I choose that most wonderful favor of Savitṛ, whose impulse is true, which possesses all boons; that swelling, thousand-streamed [milk] which Kaṇva, like a buffalo, milked for his fortune.

O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, cause him to grow; illumine him for great good fortune. Sharpen him further, even though he is already sharpened; let all the gods rejoice after him. May Dhātṛ, the lord and master of the world, bestow wealth upon us; may he grant it to us with fullness.

May Dhātṛ grant to the donor an eastern, undecaying life; may we obtain the favor of the god who bestows all wealth. May Dhātṛ grant all desirable things to the donor who desires offspring within his home. May all the gods, together with Aditi, being of one accord, bestow immortality upon him. May Dhātṛ, Rāti, Savitṛ, Prajāpati, Agni the lord of treasures, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Viṣṇu, rejoicing in our progeny, bestow riches upon the sacrificer.
Heave yourself up, O Earth; burst open this celestial cloud. O Dhātṛ, as the sovereign lord, release for us the leather bag of the heavenly waters.

The heat did not scorch, nor did the cold destroy; the earth, yielding her gifts, bowed down before him. Even the waters pour out ghee for him where Soma is ever present; there indeed is perpetual prosperity.
Prajāpati generates these creatures; may Dhātṛ, being well-disposed, establish them. Being of one accord, of one mind, and of one origin, may the Lord of Prosperity bestow prosperity upon me.

May Anumati today approve our sacrifice among the gods, and may Agni, the bearer of oblations, be present for me, the donor. O Anumati, do thou grant us thy consent and bestow peace upon us; enjoy the offered oblation and, O Goddess, grant us progeny.
May he, being well-disposed, grant us wealth accompanied by offspring and never-failing; may we not fall into his displeasure, but abide in his great mercy and favor.

O Anumati, who art well-guided and of easy invocation, whose name is approved and whose gifts are bountiful—with that [name], fulfill our sacrifice, O thou of all boons; bestow upon us wealth, O blessed one, together with heroic sons.

Anumati has come to this sacrifice for the sake of goodly fields and for the sake of heroic sons; for her providence has become auspicious; may she, the guardian of the gods, protect this sacrifice. Anumati has become all this: whatever stands, whatever moves, and whatever stirs—O Goddess, may we abide in thy favor; O Anumati, do thou indeed grant us thy consent.

Come together, all of you, with our speech to the Lord of Heaven—the one pervasive guest of men. He, the ancient one, desires the new; him alone, though manifold, the path follows. This is he who has come to us by the thousands for the sight of the seers; his thought is the light within the firmament.
The radiant one has brought together the converging dawns; they are stainless, harmonious, most full of spirit in their own abode, mindful of the cow.
Bad dreams, a miserable life, demons, the monstrous, and all ill-named, foul-tongued witches—we cause them to perish away from us.

That which Indra dug for us, that which Agni, the All-Gods, and the Maruts with their beautiful hymns [dug], may Savitṛ of true laws, Prajāpati, and Anumati bestow that upon us. By whose power the worlds were established, who are most heroic and most mighty in their deeds, who rule as irresistible through their strengths—to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa has my first invocation gone. In whose direction this world shines, whom he breathes forth and beholds with his powers; before the law of the God by his strengths—to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa has my first invocation gone.
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms; who, striding thrice with wide-gazing steps, propped up the highest dwelling place.

For those heroic deeds is Viṣṇu praised, like a fearsome beast that wanders at will and dwells in the mountains. May he come hither from the furthest distance—he under whose three wide strides all living beings abide. O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; grant us ample space for our dwelling. Drink the clarified butter, O you whose source is butter; further evermore the lord of the sacrifice.
Vishnu strode across this; he established his foot in three places, gathered together in his dust.
Vishnu, the undeceivable guardian, strode forth three steps, maintaining the laws from here.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest—he who is the close ally and friend of Indra.
The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu, like an eye fixed in the sky.

From heaven, O Viṣṇu, and from earth, O Viṣṇu, from the great and wide mid-air, fill your hands with many treasures; bestow them from the right and from the left. May Iḍā herself clothe us according to her sacred law, she at whose footstep those seeking the gods purify themselves—she who is *ghṛtapadī* (leaving a trail of ghee), *śakvarī*, and *somapṛṣṭhā* (having Soma upon her back); she has approached the sacrifice as the one belonging to all the gods (*vaiśvadevī*).

May the *veda* (the sacrificial grass-bundle) be our well-being, the *drughaṇa* (the wooden mace) be our well-being, the axe and the altar be our well-being, and the axe itself be our well-being. May those gods—the preparers of the oblation, worthy of sacrifice, and lovers of sacrifice—enjoy this sacrifice.

O Agni and Viṣṇu, great is that majesty of yours; you guard the secret name of the hidden ghee. Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, may your tongue move toward the ghee. O Agni and Viṣṇu, you enjoy the dear, great abode of yours; taking pleasure in the secret [portions] of the ghee, increasing through beautiful praise in every house, may your tongue rise up toward the ghee. Well-anointed for me have been Heaven and Earth; well-anointed has this Mitra made for me. Well-anointed for me has Brahmaṇaspati been; Savitṛ shall make it well-anointed for me.
O Indra, with your manifold aids that are most excellent today, O Maghavan, O Hero, quicken us! May he who hates us fall low; may the vital breath abandon him whom we hate.
We have approached the beloved, the praiseworthy youth, who increases through oblations, bearing our homage. May he grant me long life.
May the Maruts sprinkle me, may Pūṣan, may Bṛhaspati, and may this Agni sprinkle me with offspring and wealth; may he grant me long life.

O Agni Jātavedas, drive away my born rivals; repel those yet unborn. Place beneath our feet those who attack us; may we be sinless before Aditi. Overpower with might other rivals; O Jātavedas, repel those yet unborn. Prosper this kingdom for its good fortune; let all the gods rejoice after it.
These hundred veins of thine and the thousand arteries—of them all, I have sealed the openings with a stone.
I place what is lower than your womb; let neither offspring nor a child bear you. I make you barren and childless; I make a stone your covering.
Our two eyes are like honey; our countenance is anointing us both. Place me within your heart; let our minds be one.
I clothe you with my garment, born of Manu, so that you may be mine alone, and not even mention the names of other women.
I dig this medicine: it makes me look upon you with longing, bringing back the one who has departed and welcoming the one who approaches.
With that by which the Asura woman brought Indra down from among the gods, with that I bring you down, so that I may be very dear to you.
You face toward Soma; you face toward the Sun; you face toward all the gods—toward you, such as you are, we call out.
I say this, not you; you speak in the assembly. This [man] is yours alone; do not mention the names of others at all.
Whether he be beyond the foreign tribes or across the rivers, this herb has brought you here for me as if by binding.

May it establish in our cow-pen the one who dwells in wealth—the celestial, well-winged, milk-yielding, great one, the embryo of the waters, the bull of the plants, who satisfies us with rain from on high.

We invoke for our protection Sarasvat, whose vow all creatures follow, in whose vow the waters abide, and in whose vow the Lord of Prosperity is established. Toward the worshipper, may he come facing us—the giver, Sarasvat, the Lord of Prosperity, the dweller in wealth. Clad in the increase of riches, the seeker of fame, and the seat of treasures here, he has pierced through the desert wastes and across the waters; like a hawk, he gazes upon men and beholds his dwelling place. Crossing all the lower regions, may he, auspicious through friendship with Indra, come hither.

The falcon, the celestial eagle with the gaze of a man, thousand-footed and hundred-fold born, bestower of vital strength—may he deliver to us the wealth that has been carried away; may it belong to our ancestors, accompanied by the *svadhā* offering. O Soma and Rudra, drive far away in all directions the disease that has entered our home; banish Destruction to a distance, and release us from whatever sin we have committed.
O Soma and Rudra, place within our bodies all these healing remedies; loosen and release from us whatever sin has been committed and remains bound within our bodies.
Some of them are auspicious for you, some are inauspicious; you bear them all with a well-disposed mind. Three voices are deposited within him; of these, one has flown away following the sound.

Both of you have conquered; you are not defeated, nor has either of these two been defeated. O Indra and Viṣṇu, when you two strove together, you two distributed a thousandfold [booty] in three parts.
Brought from the people of all nations, from the Sindhu river; I consider you, brought from afar, the remedy for the name of envy.
Like the fire of this forest burning separately, O water, quench this envy of his like fire.

O Sinīvālī of the broad tresses, you who are the sister of the gods, accept this offered oblation; O goddess, grant us progeny. She who has beautiful arms, beautiful fingers, who is prolific and bears many children—to that Sinīvālī, the mistress of the people, offer the oblation. You who are the mistress of the people, O goddess, facing Indra, approaching with a thousand locks—O wife of Viṣṇu, for you the oblations are bestowed; O goddess, impel your husband toward our prosperity.

I repeatedly invoke at this sacrifice Kuhū, the goddess who performs good deeds with wisdom and is swift to hear our call. May she bestow upon us wealth containing all boons; may she grant us a praiseworthy hero-son who gives a hundredfold.

Kuhū, the consort of the gods and of immortality, may she enjoy our invocation and this oblation. Desiring us, may she hear our sacrifice today; may she, the wise one, grant us the increase of riches.

I invoke Rākā with fair invocations and excellent praise; may the fortunate goddess hear us and take note of us herself. May she sew together our works with a needle that never breaks, and grant us a praiseworthy hero-son who bestows a hundred gifts.

O Rākā, those benevolent favors of yours which are well-adorned, by which you bestow riches upon the donor—with those, come to us today well-disposed, O fortunate one, granting us prosperity consisting of a thousandfold nourishment.

May the willing wives of the gods protect us; may they aid us for the sake of progeny and the winning of booty—those who belong to the earth and those who abide in the domain of the waters; may those goddesses, who are swift to hear our call, grant us refuge.
And let the divine wives, the consorts of the gods—Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, Aśvinī, and Rāj—the two worlds (Rodasī) and Varuṇānī hear us; let the goddesses who are the seasons of women come.
Just as the lightning bolt strikes a tree every day without fail, so may I today overcome the gamblers with the dice without fail.
May Bhaga come from every side to those swift and unswift tribes who have not yet accepted me; may he place within my hand that which has been made ready.

I praise Agni, the possessor of good wealth, with prostrations; may he, being well-disposed here, discern what we have done for him. Like chariots seeking booty, I offer my praise; may I successfully accomplish the hymn of the Maruts in a clockwise direction.
May we conquer the enemy with you as our ally; protect our share in every battle. O Indra, grant us wide space and a path easy to traverse; O Maghavan, shatter the manly strength of our foes.
I have conquered you who were marked out; I have conquered you who were hemmed in. Just as a wolf seizes a sheep, so do I seize what you have won.

Moreover, the superior gambler wins the prize; like a dog-keeper at the proper time, he sorts through his winnings. He who loves the gods does not withhold his wealth; he pours it forth with riches by means of his own powers.

May we overcome evil-minded poverty with cattle, O Much-invoked One, and hunger with barley—may all [of us] do so. May we, remaining unharmed, be the first among kings to win riches through our military hosts.
Victory is in my right hand; victory is placed in my left. May I be a winner of cattle, a winner of horses, a winner of wealth, and a winner of gold.
O Dice, give me a fruitful throw, like a cow that yields milk. Bind me with a stream of winnings, as one binds a bow with sinew.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, and from below against the evildoer; may Indra from the front and from the middle grant us, as a friend to his friends, a wide space.
May there be common understanding with our own people, common understanding with strangers; O Aśvins, bestow upon us here that common understanding.

Let us be of one mind and of one understanding; let us not be separated by the divine mind. Let no cries of lamentation arise when the great funeral pyre is prepared; let no arrow of Indra fall upon the day that has arrived. Since you, O Bṛhaspati, have released him from the curse and from dwelling in the world beyond under Yama’s power, may the Aśvins drive death away from us. O Agni, through the powers of the physicians among the gods, may you both step forward together and leave his body behind. May out-breath and in-breath remain here in union with him. Live for a hundred autumns, growing in strength; Agni is your protector, your supreme guardian, most excellent.

The life-force that has been cast away from you, let both the out-breath (*apāna*) and the in-breath (*prāṇa*) return. Agni has brought that back from the lap of Destruction (*Nirṛti*); I cause it to enter into you again within your own self.
Let not the out-breath abandon him and depart; let not the in-breath leave him behind. I entrust him to the Seven Seers (*Saptarṣis*); may they carry him safely to old age.
Enter, O out-breath and in-breath, like two oxen into their pen. May this man, a secure treasure for his old age, grow here unharmed.
We draw forth your breath; I drive away your consumption. May this most excellent Agni bestow life upon us from every side.

Rising up from the darkness, ascending to the highest firmament, we have gone to Sūrya, the god among gods, the supreme light. We worship the *ṛc* and the *sāman*, by which they perform the sacred rites. These two shine in the assembly hall; may they present the sacrifice to the gods.
The *ṛc*, the *sāman*, the oblation, vigor, the *yajus*, and strength—may this Veda, when questioned by me, not harm me, O Lord of Might!
Those paths of yours that descend from heaven, by which you have set forth the universe—with those, O Vasu, bestow upon us your favor!

The poison collected from the transverse king, the black viper, and the *pr̥dāku*—that poison of the *kaṅkaparvan*, this plant has destroyed. This plant is born of honey, dripping with honey, honey-sweet, and full of honey; it is the remedy for the displaced [bone], and moreover, the crusher of mosquitoes.
From where it has bitten, from where it has stung, from there we call your poison away. The poison of the small, piercingly biting gnat is rendered powerless.
You who are crooked, deformed, and maimed—you who make your mouths crooked and twisted—those you make, O Brahmaṇaspati, do you bend back like a blade of grass.
The poison of the sapless *śarkoṭa*, which creeps along downward, I have indeed sucked out; furthermore, I have crushed it.
There is no strength in your arms, nor in your head, nor even in your middle; then why do you carry this tiny thing on your tail, you wretched one?
The ants eat you; the peacocks tear you apart. All of you together shall declare: "The poison of the *śārkoṭa* is sapless.
O you who strike with both tail and mouth—there is no poison in your mouth; how could it be in your tail?

Whatever has been disturbed in me while speaking with hope, whatever while wandering among people begging for alms, whatever damage has occurred in my own body—may Sarasvatī fill that up with clarified butter.

Seven flow for the youth accompanied by the Maruts; the sons have furthered the eternal laws for their father. Both worlds indeed belong to him; both shine for him; both strive for him; both nourish him.

O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed juice, drink this pressed Soma, the intoxicating, you who uphold the sacred vows. May your chariot come toward the sacrifice to enjoy the feast of the gods, arriving at the dwelling place to drink. O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bulls, drink of the most honey-sweet, virile Soma. This juice has been poured out for you; having sat down upon this sacrificial grass (*barhis*), rejoice.
Whoever shall curse us—whether he be one who has not been cursed or one who has been cursed—let him wither away from the root, like a tree struck by lightning.
Bearing strength, a winner of wealth, wise, with a non-terrible, friendly eye, I come to the house with a benevolent mind, offering praise. Rejoice; do not fear me.
These houses are sources of bliss, full of vigor, full of milk, standing filled with all that is desirable. May they recognize us as we approach.
Those from whom one departs while traveling abroad, and in whom one has much goodwill—we invoke those houses; may they recognize us as we approach.
Invoked are our friends who possess abundant wealth, who share in sweet delights; may you be free from hunger and thirst—O houses, do not fear us!

Invoked here are the cows, invoked are the goats and sheep; and furthermore, the sweet essence of food is invoked within these homes. O houses, full of pleasant speech, fortunate, rich in nourishment, and joyful with laughter; may you be free from hunger and thirst—do not fear us!
Stay right here; do not follow after me. Nurture all forms. I shall return with prosperity; may you become more abundant through me.
O Agni, since we practice fervent austerity through our ascetic heat, may we become dear to sacred learning, long-lived, and wise.
O Agni, we perform the heat of austerity; we practice the heat of austerity. Hearing what has been heard, may we be long-lived and wise.

This Agni is the lord of the virtuous, the mighty bull; like a charioteer, he has conquered the foot-soldiers as our domestic priest. Established upon the navel of the earth, may he flash forth his light and cast beneath his feet those who seek to attack us. We invoke with hymns Agni, the conqueror in battle, the subduer, from his highest dwelling place. May he carry us across all difficulties; may the god Agni consume and overcome all misfortunes.
Whatever the black bird, flying down, has dropped here—may the waters protect me from all that evil and from distress.
That which the black bird has pecked with your mouth, O Nirṛti—may Agni Gārhapatya release me from that sin.

For you, O Apāmārga, have grown with your fruit turned backward; drive all my curses far away from here. Whatever evil deed, whatever impurity, or whatever we have done as sinners—with you, O Apāmārga, facing every direction, we wipe that all away.
Whatever we have sat with one who has black teeth, a deformed nail, or is a eunuch—that too, O Apāmārga, we wipe away entirely with you.
Whether it was in the intermediate space, or in the wind, or in the trees, or in the shrubs—if the cattle heard it being raised, may that *brāhmaṇa* come back to us again.
May my sensory power return; may my self, my wealth, and the *brāhmaṇa* return. May the sacrificial fires belonging to the hearths be established here again, each in its proper place.
O Sarasvatī, in your divine vows and in your celestial abodes, O Goddess, accept this offered oblation; O Goddess, bestow progeny upon us.

This oblation of yours, rich in ghee, is for Sarasvatī; this offering is the mouth of the ancestors. These most auspicious words are for you; through them may we be full of sweetness. Be gracious and most auspicious to us, O Sarasvatī, most merciful one; may we not be separated from your sight. May the wind blow auspiciously for us; may the sun shine auspiciously for us. May the days be auspicious for us; may the night be established as auspicious for us. May the dawn shine upon us with auspiciousness.

Whatever he offers with his mind, whatever with his speech, with sacrifices, with oblations, and with sacred formulas—may Nirṛti, in agreement with Mṛtyu, strike down that offering of his before it reaches the Truth. May the sorcerers, Nirṛti, and the Rākṣasa slay him with untruth; may the gods, impelled by Indra, churn away his sacrificial butter. May that which he offers never reach its intended goal.
Like two hawks, swift and sovereign, swooping down together, strike down the one who seeks to attack our clarified butter and whoever plots against us.
I bind both your outstretched arms and your mouth; by the wrath of the divine Agni, with that I have struck down your oblation.
I bind your arms; I bind your mouth. By the wrath of the terrible Agni, with that I have struck down the oblation.
O Agni, O powerful one, we place you around us like a fortress—you the inspired sage, whose color is bold day by day, the slayer of the treacherous.

Stand up and look down; [offer] the portion of Indra due at the proper season. If it is cooked, offer it; if it is not cooked, wait. The oblation is cooked; come hither, O Indra! The sun has traveled to the midpoint of his path. Your friends sit around you with their offerings, like householders surrounding the lord of the clan as he moves about.

I consider it cooked in the udder, cooked on the fire; I consider this newest *ṛta* to be well-prepared. Drink, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, performer of many deeds, enjoying the curd of the midday libation.

Kindled is Agni, the charioteer of heaven, O Bulls; the heated *gharma* is milked for you both as sweet nourishment. For we, the singers, rich in dwellings, invoke you both, O Aśvins, at our communal feasts. Kindled is Agni, O Aśvins; the *gharma* is heated—come hither! Now indeed the milch-cows are milked here, O Bulls; the skillful masters rejoice.

Like a pure oblation offered with the cry of "svāhā" among the gods, that cup of the Aśvins which is the drink of the deities—him all the immortals, taking pleasure in him, lick from the mouth of the Gandharva.

That which has been offered into the cows—ghee and milk—that is your portion, O Aśvins; come hither! O lovers of sweetness, upholders of the assembly, lords of the virtuous, drink the heated *gharma* from heaven.

Let the heated *gharma* reach you as your own priest; let the Adhvaryu move forward for you with the milk-offering. O Aśvins, partake of the stream of the pressed honey; drink of the milk of the ruddy cow.

Run hither with milk, O milker of cows; quickly pour the milk of the ruddy cow into the heated vessel. Savitar, the most excellent, has looked out upon the firmament; he shines forth following the departure of the Dawn.

I invoke this well-milking cow; may the skillful milker milk her. May Savitṛ impel for us the most excellent stimulation. The cauldron is heated; proclaim that clearly! Lowing, mistress of treasures, she has come hither seeking her calf in her mind. Let this inviolable cow yield milk for the Aśvins; may she increase for our great good fortune.
Welcomed as the domestic guest in the dwelling, come to this our sacrifice, O wise one! Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the possessions of those who act as enemies.
O Agni, be bold for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent. Secure for us a household that is easy to govern, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.
May you be blessed with good pasture; may we likewise be blessed. Eat grass, O inviolable one, at all times; drink pure water as you wander.
We have heard that the mother of the red, spotted flies is black. With the root of the divine sage, I pierce them all.
I pierce their first; I pierce their middle; here I cut off their hindmost like a lock of hair.
With a word belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ, I have allayed your jealousy; and furthermore, O husband, that anger which is yours, we pacify for you.
O Lord of Vows, anointed by our vow, shine here forever with a gracious mind. May we all, possessing offspring, sit near you when you are kindled, O Jātavedas.

May we drink pure waters at a good watering-place—waters that are bright, rich in fine grass, and abundant for our progeny. Let no thief nor any speaker of evil have power over us; may the weapon of Rudra pass us by.

You who know the quarters, who are delightful, joined together, and named after all things—come hither to me, O goddesses, with the gods! Sprinkle us with ghee in this cow-pen, in this dwelling place.
May they be more frail than the frail, more non-existent than the non-existent; may they be weaker than the weak, more moist than the moistening.
Those scars upon the neck, and those upon the flanks, the scars upon the joints, and those that fall away of their own accord.
He who crushes the ribs and settles in the hollow of the breast—drive out all that *jāyānya* disease, whoever has taken refuge upon the crown of the head.
Winged, the *jāyānya* flies and enters the man. This is the remedy for both the undecaying and the well-healed wound.
We know indeed your origin, O *jāyānya*, from where you are born, O *jāyānya*. How can you strike there, in whose house we offer the oblation?
Drink boldly the Soma from the jar, O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, hero in the battle for riches! At the midday libation, pour yourself full; as the bestower of wealth, bestow wealth upon us.
O Maruts, you who are the Sāṃtapanas, may you graciously accept this oblation; you are our protectors, O destroyers of enemies.

O Vasus, whatever mortal man, full of malice toward us, seeks to strike us down despite his thoughts being contrary to ours—let him be caught in the snares of deceit; slay him with your most scorching heat! The Maruts, who abide for a year, who possess beautiful hymns, who dwell in wide spaces, who move in their hosts, and who are kind to men—they shall release us from the snares of sin. O Sāṃtapanas, you who are exhilarating and gladdening, [grant us protection].
I loosen thy cord, I loosen thy yoke-thong, I loosen thy fastening. Right here, O Agni, be thou eternal.
I yoke thee, O Agni, with the divine prayer, so that thou mayest maintain lordships for him. Shine upon us here with auspicious wealth; proclaim this giver of the oblation among the gods.

Whatever portion the gods, dwelling together in greatness, have prepared for you, O Amāvāsyā, with that, O possessor of all boons, fulfill our sacrifice; bestow upon us, O fortunate one, wealth accompanied by heroic sons. I myself am Amāvāsyā; the doers of good deeds dwell within me, and in me all the gods—both those who sit together and those led by Indra—have come together.
Night has arrived, the gatherer of treasures, bringing strength, nourishment, and wealth. Let us worship Amāvāsyā with an oblation; milking out strength, she has come to us with her milk.

On the new moon day (*amāvāsye*), none other than you has brought forth all these forms as their encompasser. Whatever desire we offer to you with this oblation, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches. The full moon (*paurṇamāsī*) has triumphed. Dwellings together with the gods in her greatness, may we rejoice upon the back of the firmament with nourishing food.
We sacrifice to the full moon, the vigorous bull. May he grant us imperishable wealth that never fails.
O Prajāpati, none other than you has brought forth all these forms as their encompasser. Whatever desire we cherish as we offer oblations to you, let that be ours; may we be masters of riches.

The full moon was the first among the days to be worthy of sacrifice, surpassing the nights in the depths of darkness. Those who honor you with sacrifices, O worshipful one, have entered your high heaven as doers of good deeds.

These two move one after the other by means of creative power (*māyā*); like two playing children, they traverse the ocean. One beholds all beings, while the other, ordaining the seasons, is born anew.

You become new and ever-new as you are born; as the banner of the days, you go at the forefront of the dawns. Coming, you distribute a portion to the gods; O Moon, you extend a long life. You are a shoot of Soma, O Lord of Battles; indeed, your name is "The Whole" (*anūna*). Make me whole with offspring and with wealth!

You are the New-Moon day (*darśa*); you are beautiful to behold; you are complete (*samagra*), you are all-encompassing (*samanta*). May I be complete and all-encompassing through cattle, horses, offspring, livestock, houses, and wealth.

He who hates us and whom we hate—of him may you swell with breath. May we swell with cattle, horses, progeny, livestock, houses, and wealth. With that stalk which the gods cause to swell, which the imperishable ones consume as the imperishable, with that may Indra, Varuṇa, and Bṛhaspati, the guardians of the world, cause us to swell.

Sing forth a beautiful hymn of praise; win the prize of cattle! Bestow auspicious riches upon us. Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; let the streams of clarified butter flow pure and honey-sweet. In me first I take Agni, together with dominion, splendor, and strength. In me I place progeny, in me long life—*svāhā*! In me, O Agni, I establish Agni. Right here, O Agni, maintain our wealth. Let not the malevolent ones, who think of you first, overcome you. O Agni, may [the people] be well-governed by your dominion; may those who sit near you increase, unsubdued.
Agni has looked along the forefront of the dawns; Jātavedas, the first-born, has looked along the days. Sūrya has looked along the dawns and along his rays; he has entered heaven and earth.

Agni has looked back upon the forefront of the dawns; Jātavedas, the first-born, has looked back upon the days. He has looked back upon the many rays of Sūrya and has stretched himself across heaven and earth.

O Agni, clarified butter (*ghṛta*) is yours in the celestial dwelling-place; with clarified butter Manu kindles you today. May the divine daughters bring clarified butter for you; may the cows yield clarified butter for you, O Agni.
O King Varuṇa, your golden house is built within the waters; from there, may the King who maintains his vows release us from all bonds.

O King Varuṇa, release us from our bonds, both the tight and the loose. Whatever we have uttered here—“O Waters, O Invincible Ones,” or “O Varuṇa”—from that, O Varuṇa, release us. Loosen the uppermost bond from us, O Varuṇa, loosen the lowermost, and loosen the middle one. Then, O Āditya, in your service, may we be sinless before Aditi.
Release all our bonds, O Varuṇa, whether they be the uppermost or the lowest, those belonging to Varuṇa. Drive away from us bad dreams and misfortune; then may we go to the world of the righteous.
Invincible, immortal Jātavedas, O Agni, shine here as a sovereign ruler who upholds the *kṣatra*. Dispelling all maladies, protect our household today with your auspicious human-like [powers].
O Indra, you were born for the sake of desirable dominion and vigor, the bull among the peoples. You drove away the unfriendly folk and made wide space for the gods.

Like a terrifying beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, may he come hither from the furthest distance. Sharpening your bolt, O Indra, and whetting your keen blade, strike down the enemies and drive away the adversaries.

We invoke here for our well-being that very Tārkṣya, the prize-winning steed, impelled by the gods, the possessor of overwhelming power, the overcomer of chariots, whose rim is uninjured, the swift victor in battle.

I call upon Indra, the protector, Indra, the helper; at every invocation, I call upon the hero Indra who is easily invoked. Now I call upon the mighty Indra, who is invoked by many. May the bounteous Indra grant us well-being.

That Rudra who is in the fire, who is within the waters, who has entered the plants and the herbs—he who has fashioned all these worlds: let there be homage to that Rudra, to Agni. Depart! You are an enemy; indeed, you are an enemy. You have mixed with poison; indeed, you have mixed with poison. Go toward the serpent itself; slay him!
I have sought the celestial waters; we have been united with their essence. Rich in milk, O Agni, I have come; endow me with splendor.

Endow me, O Agni, with splendor, with progeny, and with long life. May the gods take note of this of mine; may Indra, together with the seers, take note. O Waters, carry away this: whatever is blameworthy and whatever is impurity; whatever treachery I have committed, whatever falsehood, and whatever harsh word I have uttered.
You are fuel; may I prosper. You are kindling; may I thrive. You are splendor; bestow splendor upon me.
Tear it away as of old; strike down the power of the Dāsa, like the hidden tangle of a creeping vine.

Let us, together with Indra, divide that gathered wealth of his. I cause your bright glow to fade away by the decree of Varuṇa, so that your member may fall away, and you may become one who is unproductive among women. Of the one who stands below, the moistening, the piercing Śāṅkura, whatever is stretched out, let that be loosened; whatever is drawn up, let that be lowered.

May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, through his aids, be very gracious to us—he who possesses all knowledge. May he drive away our enemies and grant us security; may we be masters of heroic vigor.

May that Indra, the good protector and possessor of wealth, drive our enemies far away from us. May we abide in the favor of him, the worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious goodwill. With Indra and with wrathful zeal, may we overcome those who attack us, slaying the Vṛtras without opposition.
With the firm oblation, we lead forth Soma firmly, so that Indra may make the clans ours alone and of one mind.
His two dark, trembling, greedy birds have flown up toward heaven like [eagles]. Burning upward, burning intensely, they burn the heart of this man.
I have caused these two to stand up, like two oxen resting after their toil. Like two barking dogs, like two howling wolves, they rise up.
Piercing, pricking, and even thoroughly piercing, I bind the penis of whoever has carried off my woman from here, whether she be a female or a male.
The non-existent cows have flown to their dwelling; the birds have reached their nest. The mountains stand firm in their place; I have established the two kidneys in their station.
Since today, at the commencement of this sacrifice, we have chosen you here, O wise Hotṛ—come with certainty, O most powerful one, come with certainty to the Soma, knowing the sacrifice well.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, unite us in mind with cattle, with patrons, and with well-being; unite us with the prayer established by the gods, and with the favor of the gods worthy of sacrifice.
