O Śatakratu, having thrice cleansed Apālā in the hole of the chariot, the hole of the wagon, and the hole of the yoke, you made her skin like the sun, O Indra.
Desiring goodwill, progeny, fortune, and wealth, and becoming devoted to your husband, gird yourself for the sake of immortality.
Just as the bull Sindhu brought forth sovereign rule over the rivers, so may you become a sovereign queen after going to your husband’s home.

Be a sovereign queen among your fathers-in-law, and a sovereign queen among your brothers-in-law. Be a sovereign queen among your sisters-in-law, and a sovereign queen among your mothers-in-law. O goddesses who cut the cloth, who wove it, and who stretched it out—you who placed the borders all around—may they clothe you for old age. Put on this garment, O long-lived woman! The men weep for the living; they lead him away from the sacrifice. They gaze upon his long-lasting lineage. This is a blessing for the ancestors who have prepared this rite; may it be a joy for the husbands as they embrace their wife.
I place this pleasant and firm stone for you in the lap of the goddess Earth, for the sake of progeny. Ascend it with joy, O lady of fair luster; may Savitṛ grant you a long life.
With that same [hand] by which Agni took the right hand of this earth, with that I take your hand; do not falter together with me, through progeny and through wealth.
May the god Savitṛ take your hand; may King Soma make you one of noble offspring. May Agni Jātavedas make you a fortunate wife, reaching old age with your husband.

I take your hand for the sake of good fortune, so that with me as your husband you may reach old age. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Purandhi—the gods have given you to me for the state of a householder. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Purandhi—the gods have given you to me for the state of a householder. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Purandhi—the gods have given you to me for the state of a householder.
Bhaga has taken your hand; Savitṛ has taken your hand. You are my wife by sacred law (dharma); I am the master of the house for you.

May she be the one to be nourished by me; Bṛhaspati has given you to me. With me as your husband, O mother of offspring, live a hundred autumns. Tvaṣṭṛ has fashioned this garment for beauty, by the instruction of Bṛhaspati, the seers. With that, may Savitṛ and Bhaga clothe this woman with progeny, even as they clothed Sūryā.
May Indra and Agni, Heaven and Earth, Mātariśvan, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Brahma, and Soma cause this woman to increase with progeny.
Bṛhaspati was the first to fashion the hair upon the head of Sūryā; with that, O Aśvins, we adorn this woman for her husband.

This is that form which the maiden assumed as she moved about in her mind, desiring to know her husband. I shall pursue her with my companions, the Navagvas; who, knowing this, has untied these bonds? I shall unbind them; I perceive her form within me. Behold the nest of the mind! I do not consume the theft with my mind; I have released myself, loosening by my own power the fetters of Varuṇa.
I release you from the noose of Varuṇa, with which the most gracious Savitṛ bound you. Here I make for you and your husband a wide space, an easy path to travel, O bride.
Lift it up! You shall slay the demon; place this woman with one who performs good deeds. The wise Dhātṛ has found a husband for her; may King Bhaga go before her, knowing the way.
Bhaga fashioned the four feet; Bhaga fashioned the four cross-pieces. Tvaṣṭṛ carved out the side-boards from the middle. May she be highly auspicious for us.

O Sūryā, ascend this bridal procession, which is adorned with *kiṃśuka* flowers, multiform, golden-hued, well-wheeled, and easy to turn. Ascend to the world of immortality; make the bridal procession pleasant for your husbands.
O Varuṇa, bring her who does not kill her brothers; O Bṛhaspati, bring her who does not kill cattle; O Indra, bring her who does not kill her husband; O Savitṛ, bring to us one who shall have sons.
Do not harm the young bride on the path prepared by the gods, O two pillars; we make the door of the divine hall auspicious as a path for the bride.

Let the Brahman be joined behind, let the Brahman be joined before; let the Brahman be at the end, in the middle, and on every side. Having entered the unassailable divine fortresses, may you be auspicious and gracious, and shine forth in the world of your husband.
For you they first led Sūryā around with her bridal procession; O Agni, give this wife to our husbands along with offspring.

Agni has given back the wife with life and with splendor; may he who is her husband live a long life for a hundred autumns. Soma was your first husband, Gandharva was your next; Agni was your third husband, and your fourth is born of man.
Soma gave [her] to the Gandharva; the Gandharva gave her to Agni. And Agni has given me wealth and sons, as well as this woman.

Your benevolence has come to us, O Lords of ample riches; O Aśvins, desires have settled deep within our hearts. You two have become our protectors, a pair of radiant lords. May we dwell in the beloved home of Aryaman.

Smiling with a gracious mind, bestow upon us wealth consisting of all-heroic sons and eloquence. O auspicious Lord, grant us a pleasant path, a good ford, and a fine watering place; strike down the tree-stump that stands as an obstacle on the road and destroy ill-will.
May the herbs, the rivers, the fields, and the forests protect you, O bride, along with your offspring, from the Rākṣasas.
We have ascended this path, easy to traverse and carrying well-being, upon which a hero is not harmed and finds the wealth of others.

Listen well to this from me, O men: by what blessing a husband and wife obtain what is desirable. Those Gandharvas and divine Apsarases who dwell upon these trees—may they be gracious to this bride; may they not harm the bridal procession as it is being led away.
The diseases that follow people when the bride’s radiant bridal procession passes—may the worshipful gods lead them back to the place from which they came.
May those highwaymen who lie in wait for the couple not find them; may they pass through the difficult path by an easy way, and let the enemies flee away.

With a gracious countenance, with a friendly eye, and with sacred prayer, I cause the bridal procession to appear from the houses. Whatever garment of every form has been bound on, may Savitṛ make it pleasant for her husbands.
Auspicious is this woman; she has come to rest. The Creator (Dhātṛ) has assigned this world for her. May Aryaman, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and Prajāpati increase her with progeny.
This woman, rich in soul, has come to the fertile field; sow your seed within her. May she bring forth offspring for you from her wombs, bearing the milk of the bull’s semen.
Stand firm; you are Virāj, like Viṣṇu here, O Sarasvatī. O Sinīvālī, may he be procreated; may he abide in the favor of Bhaga.
May your wave strike against the pins; O Waters, release the thongs! Let not the two inviolable bulls, though free from fault or sin, come to harm.

May she be of non-terrible gaze, not a slayer of her husband, pleasant, helpful, most kind, and easy to manage for our homes. May we prosper together with you—she who brings forth heroes, loves her brothers-in-law, and is well-disposed.

Be here a non-slayer of brothers-in-law, a non-slayer of husbands, auspicious to the cattle, easy to manage, and full of luster. Rich in offspring, bringing forth heroes, loving your brothers-in-law, and pleasant—worship this Gārhapatya fire.

Arise from here! Why have you come here seeking this? I, the conqueror, summon you from my own home. O Nirṛti, you who wander seeking empty places, arise! O Arāti, fly away; do not remain here. When this bride has worshipped the former Gārhapatya fire, then, O woman, pay homage to Sarasvatī and to the ancestors.
(8) Bring this protection and armor for this woman to spread beneath her. O Sinīvālī, let her give birth; may she abide in the favor of Bhaga.

The *balbaja* grass that you lay down and the skin that you spread out—let her who is blessed with good offspring, the maiden who finds a husband, ascend upon it. Spread the *balbaja* grass upon the red skin; sitting there, may she, possessed of good offspring, serve this fire.
Ascend the hide, sit down near the fire; this god slays all the demons. Procreate offspring here for this husband; may this son of yours be preeminent.

Let the animals of various forms, being born, spread forth from the lap of this mother. Sit down near this fire with auspicious fortune; as a wife, adorn the gods here. With auspicious fortune, a furtherer of the household, very gracious to the husband and well-disposed toward the father-in-law, be pleasant to the mother-in-law; enter these dwellings.
Be gracious to the fathers-in-law, gracious to the husband and the household; be gracious to this entire community, and be gracious for their prosperity.
This bride is most auspicious; come together and behold her. Having bestowed good fortune upon her, depart with your misfortunes.
Those young women who are ill-disposed, and those here who are old—bestow your splendor upon her now, and then go back to your own homes.

Ascend the couch with a well-disposed mind; here, procreate offspring for this husband. Like Indrāṇī, waking with clear understanding, you shall be watchful like the dawns that have light at their head.
In the beginning, the gods descended; they united their bodies with wives. Like Sūryā, O woman of every form, endowed with greatness, become here united with a husband who brings offspring.
Arise from here, Viśvāvasu; we entreat you with reverence. Seek a sister born of the fathers, one who is well-disposed; that is your portion by birth—be mindful of it.
The Apsarases rejoice in the company of the sacrifice between the sun and the vessel of oblation. They are your source; go toward them. O Gandharva, I pay homage to you according to the season.

Homage to the Gandharva Namasi; homage we pay to Bhāma and to Cakṣus. O Viśvāvasu, with this prayer we offer homage to you; go forth to your wives, the Apsarases. May we be well-disposed toward wealth. We have caused the Gandharva to turn back from there. That god has gone to the highest dwelling place; we have gone where they prolong their life. O parents, unite at the proper time; may you both become the mother and father of seed. Like a young man mounting a maiden, mount her; create offspring here and prosper wealth.
Send forth that most auspicious Pūṣan, in whom men sow their seed; she who, longing for us, shall part her thighs, so that we, longing, may cast our member within her.
Climb onto her thigh, place your hand upon her, and embrace your wife with a well-disposed mind. May you two produce offspring here, rejoicing; may Savitṛ grant you both a long life.

May Prajāpati produce offspring for you both; may Aryaman anoint you with day and night. O you of no ill fortune, enter the world of your husband. Be auspicious to us, bringing peace to our bipeds and peace to our quadrupeds.
(10) This bridal garment and the bride’s robe were given by the gods together with Manu. He who gives them to a learned Brahmin indeed strikes down the demons from his bed.

That portion of the *brahman* which was given to me by the two brides—the bridal garment and the bride’s own clothing—may you two, Indra and Bṛhaspati, grant it together to the *brahman*, being well-disposed toward him. Bound from a pleasant womb, laughing and exulting with great joy, may you two cross over to good cattle, good sons, and a good house, remaining alive through the radiant dawns.
Clothed in new raiment, fragrant and well-dressed, I have come forth alive through the radiant dawns; like a winged bird from its shell, I have emerged free from all sin.

May the purifying Heaven and Earth, who are near with their benevolence and possess great ordinances, and the seven divine Waters—may they all release us from distress. To Sūryā, to the gods, to Mitra, and to Varuṇa—to those who are the wise perceivers of all that exists—I have offered this homage.
He who, even without a binding, before piercing the joints, is the restorer of the connection—Maghavan, the possessor of many riches—he shall repair what was shattered again.
May darkness depart from us: the blue, the tawny, and the red. That which is the consuming, speckled night-spirit, I fasten it upon this wooden post.
Whatever spells are in the undergarment, however many are the snares of King Varuṇa, whatever failures and whatever misfortunes there are in this man—I lay them all upon this wooden post.

That body of mine which is most dear has been afraid of the garment. O Lord of the Forest, spread out its hem before it; may we not come to harm. Whatever ends there are, however many fringes, whatever warp-threads and woof-threads there may be—let that garment which has been woven by the wives touch us with comfort.
These longing maidens, going from the world of the fathers to their husband, have released their consecration; Svāhā!
Released by Bṛhaspati, all the gods have sustained it. That luster which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this woman.
That brilliance which was released by Bṛhaspati and which the All-Gods sustained, having entered into the cows—with that we unite this woman.
Released by Bṛhaspati, all the gods have sustained it. It is Bhaga who has entered among the cattle; with him we unite this [woman].
The All-Gods sustained that which was released by Bṛhaspati; that glory which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this woman.
That which was released by Bṛhaspati, all the gods sustained; the milk that has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [earth].
Released by Bṛhaspati, all the gods have sustained it; that essence which has entered the cows—with that we unite this [earth].
If these long-haired people have danced together in your house, causing evil with their wailing—may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin.

If this daughter of yours, with disheveled hair, wept in the house, bringing evil by her weeping—may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin; may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin.

When sisters and young women have danced together in your house, creating evil with their weeping—may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. Whatever evil has been committed by evildoers, whether it has settled upon your offspring, your cattle, or in your houses—may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. This woman speaks thus as she scatters the parched grain: "May my husband be long-lived; may he live for a hundred autumns."
O Indra, drive these two together here like a pair of *cakravāka* birds; through offspring, may they, well-established, attain a full span of life.
Whatever spell was cast upon the throne, upon the pillow, or upon the covering, whatever magic they wrought at the wedding—upon the seat, that we now lay down.
Whatever ill-deed, whatever impurity there is in the wedding and in the bridal procession—that evil we wipe away upon the blanket of Saṃbhala.

Having laid down the impurity upon Saṃbhala and our misfortune upon Kambala, we have become worthy of sacrifice and pure; may he prolong our lives. This artificial thorn, which has a hundred teeth—may it scratch away the hair-borne impurity from her and the impurity from her head.

From limb by limb, we drive the consumption (yakṣma) out of her. May that not reach the earth, nor the gods, nor may it reach the sky or the wide atmosphere. May this impurity not reach the waters, O Agni, nor Yama, nor all the ancestors.

May the noble ones take note of us; may the liberal givers desire sons for us. May we, unharmed, attend upon them for the sake of great victory in battle.
Those fathers who have come to this bridal procession, beholding their daughter-in-law—may they grant protection, rich in progeny, to this bride and her husband.

That cord which came here first, acting as a tether—having bestowed upon her offspring and wealth here, let them carry it back along the path of the one who has not yet arrived; this Virāj, possessing good progeny, has emerged victorious.

The Vrātya was indeed moving forward; he brought Prajāpati into being.
That Prajāpati beheld gold within himself; he brought it forth.

That became one; that became a mark; that became great; that became the eldest; that became Brahman; that became austerity; that became truth. That became truth. That became truth. That. That became truth. It was born.
He grew; he became great; he became Mahādeva.
He went around the lords of the gods; he became the sovereign lord.
He became that one Vratya; he took up a bow, and that indeed is the rainbow.
His belly is blue and his back is red.
"By the black [color] he indeed covers the unpleasant rival, and by the red [color] he pierces the hater," so say those who discourse on sacred knowledge.
He arose; he moved forth toward the eastern direction.
The *bṛhat* and the *rathantara*, as well as the Ādityas and all the gods, followed after him.
He who reviles a Vrātya knowing this cuts himself off from the *bṛhat* and the *rathantara*, and from the Ādityas and all the gods.

He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, of the Ādityas, and of the Viśvedevas. For him, in the eastern direction, Faith is the courtesan, Mitra is the bard, discernment is the garment, day is the turban, night is the hair, the two golden ear-rings are the two earrings, the shimmering gem is the jewel, the past and the future are the two attendants, the mind is the crossroads, Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two chariot-drivers at the crossroads, Vāta is the charioteer, Reṣman is the whip, and fame is the banner.
And glory and fame are their precursors. [6–7]
Fame comes to him, glory comes to him, who knows thus.
He rose up; he moved along toward the southern direction.
After him followed the Yajñāyajñiya and the Vāmadevya [sāmans], as well as the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle.
He who, knowing this, reviles a Vrātya, cuts himself off from the Yajñāyajñiya and the Vāmadevya, and from the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Yajñāyajñiya chant, the Vāmadevya chant, the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the sacrificial animals.
To the south of him, Dawn is the harlot; the Mantra is the bard; Knowledge is the garment; Day is the turban; Night is the hair; the two green ear-rings are the gems;
the New Moon and the Full Moon are the two attendants; the Mind is the carriage; Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two side-horses of the carriage; Wind is the charioteer; and the Storm is the whip.
And fame and glory go before him;
renown comes to him and glory comes to him who knows this.
He arose and moved toward the western direction.
Vairūpa and Vairāja, as well as the Waters and King Varuṇa, followed after him. [16]

He who reviles a Vrātya who knows this cuts himself off from Vairūpa, from Vairāja, from the Waters, and from King Varuṇa. For him, in the western direction, Night is the courtesan; laughter is his garment, knowledge his lower robe, day his turban, night his hair, the two green [leaves] his earrings, and the *kalmali* flower his jewel. [18–19]

Day and night are the two attendants; the mind and Mātariśvan the purifier are the two charioteers of the crossroads; Vāta is the driver and Reṣman is the whip; and Fame is the two precursors. Vāta is the driver and Reṣman is the whip; and Fame is the two precursors.
Fame comes to him, glory comes to him, who knows this.
He rose up; he moved along toward the northern direction.
Śyaita and Naudhasa, the Seven Seers, and King Soma followed after him.
He who, knowing this, reviles a Vrātya, cuts himself off from Śyaita, from Naudhasa, from the Seven Seers, and from King Soma.
He who knows this possesses the beloved abode of the Śyaita and the Naudhasa, of the Seven Seers, and of King Soma.

[24] In his northern direction are lightning as his courtesan, thunder as his bard, discernment as his garment, day as his turban, night as his hair, two green ear-rings, and fame and glory as his two precursors. [26–27]
Fame comes to him, glory comes to him, who knows this.
He stood upright for a year; the gods said to him, "O Vrātya, why do you stand?"
He said, "Let them prepare a throne for me."
For that Vrātya, they brought together a throne-seat.
Of her, summer and spring were the two feet, and autumn and the rainy season were the other two.
The Bṛhat and the Rathantara were on the two longitudinal beams; the Yajñāyajñiya and the Vāmadevya were on the two cross-beams.
The *ṛc* verses are the longitudinal threads, the *yajus* formulas are the transverse threads;
the Veda is the carpet, and the Brahman is the pillow.
The Sāman is the seat, the Udgītha is the support.
The Vrātya ascended that throne.
O God, his attendants were the people; his messengers were the volitions; and all beings were his followers.
All beings indeed become his Upasad-offerings for him who knows thus.
For him, they made the two months of spring the guardians of the eastern quarter, and the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans] the attendants.
The two months of spring guard the eastern quarter for him, and the Bṛhat and Rathantara attend upon him, for whoever knows thus—for whoever knows thus—for whoever knows thus. [3]

This Agni has declared, and Soma has declared it; may Pūṣan place me in the world of the righteous.

For greater prosperity, may the sacrifice be wealthy; may I win wealth; may I become wealthy; bestow wealth upon me!

Guarded by the Eternal Law (*ṛta*) and by all the seasons, guarded by what has been and what is to be, may neither evil nor death reach me; I have hidden myself within the waters of speech.

I would indeed turn my friend toward friendship, having traveled even across the vast ocean. May the wise one, contemplating further upon the earth, take up the grandson of the father.

Your friend does not desire this friendship, for she who shares the same mark becomes one of different form. The sons of the great Asura, the heroes, the upholders of heaven, look far and wide around.
Truly, those immortals desire this: even the offspring of the single mortal. Your mind has been placed within our mind; as a husband, you shall enter the body of your wife.
What have we ever done before, that now, speaking truth, we should speak falsehood? The Gandharva in the waters and the watery maiden—she is our kin, she is our ultimate bond of relationship.

In the womb, who was our progenitor, the god who made us husband and wife? It was Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, the omniform one. No one violates his ordinances; both Earth and Heaven know this of us. Who today yokes to the pole the oxen of Order—those vigorous, impetuous, and fiercely angry ones, whose arrows are near, who pierce the heart, yet bring delight? Only he shall live who fulfills their service. Who knows of that first day? Who has seen it? Who here can declare it? Great is the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa. What will you say, O deceiver, when you encounter men with your speech?

What would a brother be if he were to leave one unprotected? And what would a sister be if Destruction were to seize her? Driven by desire, I prattle much; unite thy body with my body!

I am not here to be your protector, O Yamī; I will not unite my body with your body. Arrange your pleasures with another than me; your brother does not desire this, O fortunate one. Indeed, I would never unite my body with your body; they call it an evil thing when one approaches his own sister. This is contrary to the mind and the heart of mine, that I, as a brother, should lie upon the bed of my sister. Alas, O Yama, I have found no agreement at all between your mind and my heart. Surely another shall embrace you like a girth-belt, or like a climbing vine around a tree.
One woman indeed approaches another; one shall embrace you as a creeper embraces a tree. Win his heart, or he yours; then make with him a most auspicious agreement.

O friends, we invoke with prayer Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt; I praise him, the most heroic and bold.

O Sarasvatī, you who have come on the same chariot, rejoicing with the ancestors through hymns and self-sustaining powers (*svadhā*), O Goddess—bestow here a portion of nourishment worth a thousand, and abundance of wealth for the sacrificer.

May the lower, the higher, and the middle Fathers, worthy of Soma, arise—those who have gone to the life-breath, free from malice and knowers of *ṛta*; may those Fathers protect us in our invocations.

I have found the benevolent Fathers, and the descendant, and the wide stride of Viṣṇu. Let this homage be paid today to the Fathers, those who went before and those who went after; those who are settled in the earthly realm, or those who are now in the well-favored quarters.

May Mātali with the Kavyas, Yama with the Aṅgirases, and Bṛhaspati, who is strengthened by the Ṛkvans—those gods whom the gods have strengthened and those who [strengthen] the gods—may these Fathers protect us in our invocations.
Truly, this is sweet and it is honeyed; truly, this is strong and it is flavorful. And indeed, no one at all can withstand Indra in battles when he has drunk of this.
Worship with an oblation King Yama, the son of Vivasvat, the assembler of people, who has gone along the great downward paths—the path that he has spied out for many.

Yama was the first to find for us the path; this pasture-land is not to be taken away from us, where our former fathers have passed away, following their own ancestral paths. Where our former fathers have passed away, following their own ancestral paths—where our former fathers have passed away, following their own ancestral paths—where our former fathers have passed away, following their own ancestral paths—where our former fathers have passed away, following their own ancestral paths.

O Fathers who sit upon the sacred grass (*barhis*), come hither for our aid! We have prepared these offerings for you; enjoy them! Come to us with most auspicious protection, and grant us well-being, peace, and freedom from disease. Bending the knee and sitting down to the south, may all of you accept this our oblation. O Fathers, do not harm us in any way for whatever offense we, as human beings, may commit against you.
Tvaṣṭṛ prepares the bridal procession for his daughter; because of her, this entire world comes together. The mother of Yama, the great wife of Vivasvat, vanished while being led away.

Go forth, go forth by the ancient paths, by which your ancestors have departed before you. May you behold both kings, Yama and the god Varuṇa, rejoicing in the *svadhā* offering. Depart, go away, and creep off from here; for the fathers have prepared this world for him. Yama grants him a dwelling clearly revealed by days, waters, and nights, together with his own protection. Desiring you, we kindle you; desiring you, we enkindle you. Desiring them, bring the desiring fathers here to eat the oblation.
Radiant, we kindle you; radiant, we enkindle you. O radiant one, bring the radiant ancestors here to eat the oblation.
The Aṅgirases, our fathers, the Navagvas, the Atharvans, and the Bhṛgus, who are worthy of Soma—may we abide in the favor and the auspicious goodwill of those who are worthy of sacrifice.
Come here with the Aṅgirases, the ones worthy of sacrifice; O Yama, rejoice here with the Vairūpas. I invoke Vivasvat, who is your father, that he may sit down upon this sacred grass (barhis).
Ascend this sacrificial grass, O Yama, in harmony with the Aṅgiras fathers; let the mantras recited by the seers bring you here, and, O King, rejoice in these oblations.
For Yama the Soma flows clear; for Yama the oblation is prepared. To Yama goes the sacrifice, with Agni as its well-adorned messenger.
For Yama offer the most honey-sweet [libation] and step forward! This homage is to the seers, the first-born, the ancients who made the paths.
For King Yama, offer the ghee-rich milk and the oblation. May he guide us among the living toward long life, that we may live on.
Do not burn him up, O Agni; do not consume him with heat; do not scatter his skin nor his body. When you have made him cooked, O Jātavedas, then send him forth unto the Fathers.
When you have made him cooked, O Jātavedas, then deliver him over to the Fathers. And when he goes this way to the world of the departed, then let him become subject to the will of the gods.
He flows through the three troughs; the six wide expanses are but one great [realm]. The *triṣṭubh*, the *gāyatrī*, and all the meters—these are fixed within Yama.

Go to the sun with your eye, to the wind with your breath, and go to heaven and earth according to your duties. Or go to the waters, if that is where it is good for you; take your stand among the plants with your bodily parts. The goat is the portion of austerity; let him heat that, let his glow heat that, let his flame heat that for you. O Jātavedas, with those bodies of yours which are auspicious, carry him to the world of the righteous.

O Jātavedas, let those flames of yours—your swift ones, with which you fill the sky and the mid-air—follow the goat as it goes and encompass it; then, with your other most auspicious ones, make it cooked.

Release him again, O Agni, to the Fathers—he who, offered as an oblation unto thee, moves on, self-sustained. Clothed in life, let the survivor approach; may he be united with a body, full of splendor.
Run past the two dogs, the Sārameyas, four-eyed and brindled, by the righteous path; go down to the benevolent fathers who rejoice in the banquet together with Yama.
O Yama, those two dogs of yours who are the guardians, four-eyed, sitting upon the paths, beholders of men—with them, O King, do you deliver him; grant him well-being and freedom from disease.
The two broad-nosed, life-drinking, copper-colored messengers of Yama wander among the people. May they give us back our life-breath today here, so that we may behold the sun again for our welfare.
For some, Soma flows clear; others attend to the clarified butter. May he go even to those for whom the honey flows.
To those who were of old winners of the Truth, born of the Truth, and increasers of the Truth—the seers who practiced austerity—O Yama, go even to those born of austerity.

Those who are invincible through austerity, those who have gone to heaven by means of austerity, and those who performed great austerity—go even unto them. Those heroes who fight in the forefront of battles, those who sacrifice their bodies for the sake of heaven, or those who give a thousandfold as sacrificial fees—go even unto them. Those seers who, with a thousand paths, protect the sun—the *ṛṣis* rich in austerity, O Yama—go even unto those born of austerity.
Be pleasant to him, O Earth, thornless and a place of rest; grant him wide-spreading shelter.

I summon your mind with my mind; finding pleasure in these houses here, come! Unite with the Fathers, unite with Yama. May gentle, strengthening breezes blow upon you.

Let the Maruts, the water-bearers, carry you upward—their chariots swimming in water—making coolness by means of the goat; let them sprinkle your hair with rain. I have called forth life for the sake of long life, for wisdom, for skill, and for living. Let your spirit go to its own kin; now hasten toward the Fathers.
Let nothing of your mind, nor of your flesh, nor of your limbs, nor of your vital sap be lost here; let nothing of your body perish.
Let not the tree press upon you, nor the great goddess Earth. Having found a place among the Fathers, O King Yama, flourish among the sovereigns.

Whatever limb of yours has been cast away, your out-breath, your in-breath, or whatever has departed from you—let the Fathers, gathering together in one nest, lead that back to you again from pasture to pasture.
The living have driven this one out from his homes; carry him away from here, beyond the village. Death was the wise messenger of Yama; he has sent the breaths of life to the fathers.

Those Dasyus who have entered among the fathers, who move about in the guise of kinsmen eating the unoffered—those Parāpuras and Nipuras who bring [evil]—may Agni blow them away from this sacrifice. Let the fathers settle here like our own kin; making it pleasant for us, may they prolong our lives. May we be able to reach them with oblations, and, living long, may we enjoy many autumns.

The cow which I give to you, and the rice-milk which I give—by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood; by that, may he become the supporter of the people who here are without a livelihood.
Cross over to Aśvāvatī, she who is most gracious, or to Ṛkṣaka, more recently renewed. Let him who struck you down deserve to be slain; let him not find any other portion.
Yama is beyond, Vivasvān is below; beyond that, I see nothing at all. Upon Yama my sacrifice is established; Vivasvān has spread himself out along it.
They concealed the immortal one from mortals; having made her of similar form, they gave her to Vivasvān. And when that was, the Aśvins brought it; Saraṇyū abandoned the two pairs.
Those who were buried, those who were scattered, those who were cremated, and those who were dug up—bring all those ancestors, O Agni, for the eating of the oblation.

Those who were cremated by fire and those not cremated by fire, who rejoice in the midst of heaven through their own offering (*svadhā*)—you know them, O Jātavedas; may they enjoy the sacrifice and the sacrificial knife with their own offering.
Heat gently, do not burn excessively; O Agni, do not scorch your own body. Let your fury be in the forests, and let that which is sustaining be upon the earth.
I grant him this resting place, he who has come here and has become mine. Yama, the wise one, has replied to this: "Let him abide here by my riches.

Together we measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for a hundred autumns. Before a hundred autumns have passed, I have reached the measure; having gone to the light, may I be long-lived, so that it may not be exhausted for a hundred autumns before us.
Out-breath, in-breath, diffused breath, life-force, and sight for beholding the sun—go to the Fathers, the subjects of King Yama, by the path that leads neither too far nor too near.

Those leaders who, performing their labors, have passed away, leaving behind all hostilities and being childless—they, having ascended to heaven, found a world, shining upon the back of the firmament.

The lowest heaven is full of water; the middle one is thick with mist; the third is indeed the radiant sky, wherein the fathers dwell. Those who are our father’s fathers, those who are our grandfathers, who have entered the wide mid-air, who inhabit the earth and the sky—to those ancestors let us pay homage with reverence.

This indeed, and not another, you shall see as the sun in the sky; O Earth, cover him with your garment, as a mother covers her son with her robe. This indeed, and not another, shall you grow old with; there is nothing else beyond this; O Earth, cover him with your garment, as a wife covers her husband with her robe.
I envelop you with the auspicious garment of Mother Earth. That which is auspicious among the living, let it be in me; that which is *svadhā* among the ancestors, let it be in you.

O Agni and Soma, you who prepare the way, bestow a pleasant dwelling and a treasure for the gods, creating wide space. Go there where Pūṣan, who shall escort him, leads him along direct paths as he is sent forth. May Pūṣan, the guardian of the world whose cattle are never lost, lead you away from here; may he entrust you to these Fathers, and may Agni deliver you to the bounteous gods.
May Āyus Viśvāyus protect you all around; may Pūṣan protect you on the distant path ahead. Where the doers of good deeds dwell, where they have gone—there may the god Savitṛ place you.
I yoke these two bearers for you to carry [you] to the world of the departed. Through them, may you go down to the abode and the assembly of Yama.

This garment has first come to you; remove this which they brought here long ago. Being wise, follow after your sacrifices and pious works to where what was given by you in many ways among your kinsmen has gone.

O Agni, clothe yourself all around with the skins of cows as armor; cover yourself completely with fat and marrow, so that the bold one, exulting in his heat and daring, may not leap over you, seeking to consume you.

Taking the staff from the hand of the one whose life has departed, along with his hearing, luster, and strength—right here you remain, and here we, possessing excellent heroes, shall conquer all assailants and adversaries.

This woman, choosing the world of her husband, lies down beside you, O mortal, who have passed away. Preserving the ancient law, bestow upon her offspring and wealth here.

Arise, O woman, toward the world of the living; come to this one whose life has departed, for he lies here as your bed. You have entered into this state of wifehood with this husband who took your hand and held you fast.
I saw a young woman being led away—the living one being carried around from among the dead. When she was shrouded in blinding darkness, I led her from the east toward the west.
O inviolable cow, you know the way; moving along the path of the gods, you go toward the world of the living. This is your lord of cattle; accept him, and cause him to ascend to the heavenly world.

Near the sky, near the reed, you are the most helpful among the rivers; O Agni, you are the bile of the waters. That which you have scorched, O Agni, cause that to sprout again; let the *kyāmbū*, the *śāṇḍadūrvā*, and the *vyalkaśā* grow here.
This is one of your forms, and another is before you; enter into union with the third light. In your resting place, be beautiful in body; be dear to the gods in the highest dwelling.
Arise, go forth, run forward, and make thy dwelling-place in the watery realm! There, in harmony with the Fathers, rejoice in Soma and in the *svadhā* offerings.
Move forward, gather your body together; let not your limbs be scattered, nor your frame. Enter into the settled mind; go to that place where you take pleasure in the earth.

May Agni anoint me with splendor; may Viṣṇu instill wisdom within my mouth. May all the gods bestow wealth upon me; may the pleasant waters purify me with their cleansing flows. May Mitra and Varuṇa encompass me; may the Ādityas and the sacrificial posts cause me to grow strong. May Indra instill splendor in my two hands; may Savitṛ grant me long life.
To him who died first among mortals, who departed first to this world—to Yama, the king, the son of Vivasvat, the gathering place of men—honor him with an oblation.
Depart, O Fathers, and come back again; this sacrifice of yours is anointed with honey. Grant us here wealth and prosperity, and bestow upon us riches consisting of all heroic sons.

May Kaṇva, Kakṣīvat, Purumīḍha, Agastya, Śyāvāśva, Sobhari, Archanānas, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, and Atri protect us, as well as Kaśyapa and Vāmadeva. O Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja, Gotama, and Vāmadeva—may Atri, like a shelter, take hold of us with his salutations; O Fathers who are easy to address, have mercy on us!
Being cleansed, they pass over impurity, bestowing upon themselves a further, more recent span of life. Increasing in progeny and wealth, may we then be fragrant within our homes.

They anoint themselves, they anoint themselves apart, they anoint themselves together; they lick their will and anoint it with honey. Those who purify themselves with gold seize the bull as he flies at the swelling of the river—the sacrificial animal among these women. With that which is your delight, O Fathers, and that which is Soma-like, be united with it, for you have become self-glorious. Listen to us, O swift ones, O seers, you who are easily found when invoked at the sacrifice.

O Atris, Angirases, Navagvas, who possess the sacrifice, who share in the gifts, and who bestow them; you who are givers of sacrificial fees and doers of good deeds—rejoice today upon this sacred grass (*barhis*). O givers of sacrificial fees and doers of good deeds—rejoice today upon this sacred grass.
Now, just as our ancient fathers of old, O Agni, who yearned for *ṛta*, went toward the pure light—meditative, chanting hymns, they cleft the earth and uncovered the ruddy dawns;
performing noble deeds, radiant, seeking the gods, like smelting ore, the gods forged their births; kindling Agni and strengthening Indra, they have prepared for us a vast assembly of cattle.

Like herds of livestock in a land rich in food, the Mighty One has beheld the generations of the gods; even mortals have longed for the *urvaśīs*, for the increase of the noble one, the living man who is near.

We have performed good works for you, O skillful ones; the radiant Dawns have spread out the *ṛta*. All that which the gods favor is auspicious. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.

May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from the eastern quarter, as the earth, shaken by his arms, protects the sky above. We sacrifice to the makers of the world, the makers of paths, who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.

May Dhātṛ protect me from the southern direction, from Destruction; may the earth, shaken by his arm, be as high above as heaven. We sacrifice to the makers of the worlds, the makers of paths, who are here present as the recipients of the oblations of the gods.

May Aditi, with the Ādityas, protect me from the western direction; may the earth, shaken by her arm, be as high above as heaven. We sacrifice to the makers of the worlds, the makers of paths, who are here present as the recipients of the oblations of the gods.

May Soma, together with all the gods, protect me from the northern quarter; like the earth, let him support the sky above, shaken by his arms. We worship those makers of space, makers of paths, who are here as the recipients of the oblation among the gods.

You are the supporter; you are the sustainer; you are the pillar of the lineage.
You are the purifier of water; you are the purifier of honey; you are the purifier of wind.
Protect me from this side and from that side, you two who strive together like the twin Yamas when they come hither. The god-seeking men have brought you forward;

sit down, you two who know your own place. Be well-seated for our Soma-juice. An ancient prayer is joined to you with prostrations; the hymn goes forth like a patron on a path. May all the immortals hear this.

O Agni Jātavedas, being praised, you have carried the oblations away; having made them fragrant, you have delivered them to the Fathers, who have eaten them with the *svadhā* call. Eat, O God, these presented oblations! Seated in the lap of the ruddy cows, bestow wealth upon the mortal who gives. O Fathers, grant a portion of that treasure to your sons, and bestow strength here upon them.

O Agniṣvātta Fathers, come hither; sit down, each in his proper place, O excellent leaders. Eat the oblations presented on the sacrificial grass, and bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
Invoked are our Soma-loving ancestors upon the dear offerings placed upon the sacred grass; may they come hither, may they hear us here, may they speak for us, and may they protect us.

Those who are the fathers of our father, those grandfathers, the Vasiṣṭhas who have followed after the drinking of Soma—with them, may Yama, being well-pleased and desiring [the offerings], eat the oblations according to his wish along with those who desire them.

Those who have thirsted among the gods, panting, knowing the invocation, fashioning hymns with their chants—O Agni, come hither with the thousand praising gods, with the truthful sages, the seers who sit at the *gharma* vessel.

Those who are true, eaters of the oblation, drinkers of the oblation, together with Indra and the swift gods—O Agni, come hither with those of good wisdom, with the later and the earlier seers who sit at the *gharma* vessel.

May Vivasvān grant us freedom from fear—he who is the good protector, the swift-giving, the bounteous. May these many heroes here be present; may there be abundance for me in cattle and horses.
May Vivasvān establish us in immortality; let death depart and immortality come to us. May he protect these men until old age; let not their life-breaths go to Yama.

He who, like a sage among the fathers, has taken his place in the mid-air by his greatness, the guardian of our thoughts—worship him with oblations, O you who have all Mitra as your friend. May that Yama grant us further extension of life.

Ascend to the highest heaven, O seers; do not be afraid. Drinkers of Soma, drinkers of the pressed juice, this oblation is prepared for you. We have gone to the highest light. With his great banner Agni shines forth; the Bull bellows toward the two worlds. He has reached even to the furthest limit of heaven; the Mighty One has grown in the lap of the waters.
When they beheld you with longing in their hearts as you flew upon the firmament—a golden-winged bird, the messenger of Varuṇa, fluttering in the womb of Yama.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. O Much-invoked One, grant us aid on this journey; may we, while living, attain the light.

The jars covered with cakes which the gods have held for you—may they be yours, possessing *svadhā*, honeyed, and dripping with ghee. The parched grains mixed with sesame, full of *svadhā*, which I scatter for you—may they be powerful and sovereign for you; may King Yama grant his approval to them. O Lord of the Forest, give back again that which has been placed within you, so that he may sit in the abode of Yama, speaking at the assemblies.
Take hold, O Jātavedas! Let your bearer be full of splendor. Burn his body completely, and then place him in the world of the righteous.
To those ancestors of yours who have passed away before and those who came after—to them let this stream of clarified butter go, flowing in a hundred channels and overflowing.

The gods and the seasons prepare the sacrifice: the oblation, the sacrificial cake, the ladles, and the implements of sacrifice. Go by those paths traveled by the gods, by which those who have sacrificed go to the heavenly world.
Behold well the path of *ṛta*, O Aṅgiras, along which the doers of good deeds travel; go by those paths to heaven where the Ādityas consume honey, and settle yourself upon the third firmament.

Three birds with beautiful wings, the peacocks of the highest realm, rest upon the back of the vault of heaven. May these heavenly worlds, established by the immortal nectar, yield nourishment and vigor for the sacrificer.

The *juhū* ladle sustains the sky, the *upabhṛt* sustains the mid-air, and the *dhruvā* sustains the earth as the foundation. May these heavenly worlds, whose backs are sprinkled with clarified butter, yield every desired wish for the sacrificer.

Mount the firm earth that nourishes all; stride toward the intermediate space with the *upabhṛt* ladle. Go to heaven with the sacrificer by means of the *juhū*; with the *sruva* as your calf, milk all the swelling quarters without being angered.

"By way of the fords they cross the great slopes"—so it is said of those who perform the sacrifice well, by whom they go. Therein they have established a world for the sacrificer, when the quarters and the beings were fashioned.

The eastern fire is the path of the Aṅgirases; the Gārhapatya fire is the path of the Ādityas; the Dakṣiṇāgni fire is the path of the sacrificial gifts. With all your limbs intact and full of vigor, come near to the majesty of Agni as he is ordained by the sacred word.

May the eastern fire heat you for peace from the front; may the Gārhapatya fire heat you for peace from behind. May the Dakṣiṇāgni heat you for protection and armor. From the north, from the center, from the intermediate space, and from every direction, O Agni, protect us from the terrible.
O Agni, with your most auspicious bodies, carry the sacrificer to the heavenly world, becoming horses that bear the burden on your backs, to where they rejoice in the communal feast with the gods.

O Agni, burn him peacefully from behind, peacefully from the front, peacefully from above, and burn him peacefully from below. You, Jātavedas, though one, are established in a threefold way; place him properly in the world of those who have performed good deeds.
May the kindled fires take hold of him peacefully—of this sacrificial victim belonging to Prajāpati, O Jātavedas. Making him cooked, do not cast him away here.

The sacrifice goes forth, spread out and being prepared, toward the heavenly world for the sacrificer. May the fires enjoy it as it is entirely offered—this sacrificial victim belonging to Prajāpati, O Jātavedas.

The sacrificer has ascended the piled fire, about to fly up from the back of the firmament to heaven. For him, the luminous, celestial path leading to the gods shines forth through the sky for his righteous deed.

The parched grains mixed with sesame seeds, which I scatter for you as offerings accompanied by the *svadhā* call—may they be abundant and powerful for you; may King Yama grant his approval of them.
This is the path, both before and after, by which your ancestors have departed; those who were their leaders and followers carry you to the world of the righteous.

Those seeking the gods invoke Sarasvatī while the sacrifice is being performed; the doers of good invoke Sarasvatī; may Sarasvatī grant what is desirable to the donor. The Fathers invoke Sarasvatī as they approach the sacrifice from the south; having sat down upon this sacred grass (*barhis*), rejoice! Bestow upon us food free from disease.

O Sarasvatī, you who have come on the same chariot with the fathers, rejoicing in the hymns and the self-sustaining offerings, O Goddess—bestow here upon the sacrificer a portion of the *iḍ* worth a thousandfold, and the increase of wealth.
I cause you, O Earth, to enter into the earth; may the god Dhātṛ extend our lifespan. Let this wealth-finder go further and further for you; then, having died, let them be united with the ancestors.

Move forward together and wipe away that which those who were here spoke against you both. O two inviolable ones, I desire this from the giver: that you two shall enjoy your portion here among the ancestors.

May this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) come to us from the auspicious one, yielding good milk and bestowing vital strength. May it, embracing the living ones in their youth, carry these [beings] over to the fathers in old age. May it, embracing the living ones in their youth, carry these [beings] over to the fathers in old age. May it, embracing the living ones in their youth, carry these [beings] over to the fathers in old age. May it, embracing the living ones in their youth, carry these [beings] over to the fathers in old age. May it, embracing the living ones in their youth, carry these [beings] over to the fathers in old age. May it, embracing the living ones in their youth...

I bring this sacred grass (*barhis*) for the ancestors; I spread it out, higher than the living for the gods. Ascend it, O man, becoming worthy of sacrifice. May the fathers recognize you as you depart! May the fathers recognize you as you depart! Just as you gather your body together, I fashion your limbs with the sacred word (*brahman*).
Parṇa, the king, the covering of the sacrificial vessels, has come to us with vigor, strength, endurance, and vital power. Bestowing life upon those who live, grant long life for a hundred autumns.

He who was born as a portion of vigor attained sovereignty over those whose food is stone; worship him with oblations, O you who have Viśvāmitra as friend; may he, Yama, establish us further on the path of life. Just as the five tribes of men prepared a palace for Yama, so do I prepare this palace that it may be mine in abundance.
Bear this gold which your father bore of old; draw forth from the hand of your father as he goes to heaven his right hand.
For those who are living and those who are dead, for those who have been born and those who are worthy of sacrifice—for them let a stream of clarified butter come, an overflowing flow of honey.

The bull of prayers, far-seeing, flows clear; the sun, the furtherer of days and dawns, [flows] from heaven. The breath of the rivers has bellowed into the jars; he has entered the heart of Indra with inspired thought.
Let your brilliant smoke envelop the sky, O radiant one, spread abroad like the sun with its light; for you, O purifier, shine with beauty through your grace.

Indeed, the drop goes forward to the appointed place of Indra; as a friend does not fail the friendship of his comrade, he does not neglect the songs of praise. Like a youth toward maidens, Soma flows together into the jar by a path of a hundred journeys.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; they have shaken off their beloved [impurity]. The self-luminous inspired ones, the youngest, have offered praise; we entreat them.
Come, O Soma-loving Fathers, by the deep paths traveled by the ancestors. Granting us long life and progeny, favor us with the increase of wealth.
Depart, O Soma-loving Fathers, by the deep and ancient paths. Then come back to our houses at the [proper] month, to eat the oblation, possessing good offspring and noble heroes.

Whatever limb of yours Agni Jātavedas abandoned, causing you to go to the world of the fathers—that limb of yours I now cause to swell again; O fathers, rejoicing with all your limbs, revel in heaven.

Jātavedas was sent as a messenger; at evening, at the close of day, he is to be honored by men. You have given [the offerings] to the Fathers; they have eaten them with the *svadhā* call. Eat, O God, these presented oblations. Here, indeed, is your mind; like kinsmen covering a hump, O Earth, cover it over.
May the worlds, the seats of the ancestors, be adorned; I seat you in the world that is the seat of the ancestors.
You are the sacred grass for those who are our fathers.
Loosen the uppermost bond from us, O Varuṇa, and untie the lowest; then, O Āditya, may we be sinless within your law and before Aditi.

Release us from all those snares, O Varuṇa, with which one is bound in the encounter or in the distance. Then, O King, may we live for a hundred autumns, protected and guarded by you. Then, O King, may we live for a hundred autumns, protected and guarded by you. Then, O King, may we live for a hundred autumns, protected and guarded by you. Then, O King, may we live for a hundred autumns, protected and guarded by you. Then, O King, may we live for a hundred autumns, protected and guarded by you. Protected by you, O King... [Note: The final line fragment "tvayā rājan gupitā ra" appears to be an incomplete repetition of the refrain.]
To Agni Kavyavāhana, Svadhā! Homage!
To Soma accompanied by the ancestors, Svadhā! Adoration!
To the fathers accompanied by Soma, Svadhā! Adoration!
To Yama, who possesses the ancestors, Svadhā! Adoration!
This, O great-grandfather, is for you, svadhā; and for those who follow you.
This is for you, O grandfather, svadhā, and for those who follow you.
This for you, father; svadhā!
Svadhā to the ancestors who dwell upon the earth!
Svadhā to the ancestors who dwell in the intermediate space!
Homage to you, O fathers, for vigor; homage to you, O fathers, for sapidity.
Homage to you, O fathers, for your brilliance; homage to you, O fathers, for your wrath.
Homage to you, O fathers; whatever in you is terrible, to that homage! Homage to you, O fathers; whatever in you is cruel, to that homage!
Homage to you, O Fathers, for that which is auspicious; homage to you, O Fathers, for that which is pleasant.
Homage to you, O fathers; the svadhā offering is for you, O fathers.
O ancestors who are here, you who are present here—you [the living] follow them, and may you become the best among them.
Those who are the fathers here, we are those who are living here. May they follow after us; may we be the best among them.
O Agni, we kindle you, the radiant, the unaging god, so that this most praiseworthy fuel of yours may shine in the sky. Bring nourishment to your praisers!
Let the rivers flow together, let the winds come together, and let the winged birds gather; increase this sacrifice with songs. I offer oblation with the flowing libation.
O oblations, protect this sacrifice; O outpourings, likewise protect this sacrifice. Increase this sacrifice with our songs; I offer it with the oblation of the outpouring.
Taking hold of every form and every age, I embrace him; may the four quarters increase this sacrifice; I offer it with the flowing oblation.

May the waters from the Himalayas be auspicious for you, and may those from the springs be auspicious for you; may the waters that flow down be auspicious for you, and may the rains be auspicious for you.

May the waters of the desert be auspicious for you; may the waters of the marshes be auspicious for you; may the waters dug from the earth be auspicious for you, and those brought in jars be auspicious for you.
Digging in the deep, the wise ones, the water-workers who are more skilled healers than physicians—to those waters we speak.

Of the waters of heaven, of the waters flowing in streams—of those waters at their cleansing, you become swift horses. Those waters are auspicious, those waters are disease-removers; just as one is satisfied by them, so may they, as healing medicines, grant you well-being.
From heaven, from earth, from the intermediate space, from the trees, and from the plants—from wherever Jātavedas is distributed, come to us from there, praised and well-pleased.

Whatever majesty of yours is in the waters, whatever in the forests, whatever in the plants, in cattle, and within the waters—O Agni, gather all your bodies together; with them come to us as the imperishable giver of wealth.

Whatever majesty of yours is heavenly among the gods, whatever body of yours has entered into the ancestors, and whatever nourishment of yours has spread among men—O Agni, through that, bestow riches upon us.

To the one with attentive ears, the seer who is to be known, I approach with hymns and words for the sake of receiving bounty. May that from which fear arises be free from fear for us. O Agni, appease the wrath of the gods through sacrifice.

That first oblation which Atharvan offered, which Jātavedas created as the sacrificial gift—this very one I, the foremost, invoke for you. Satisfied by these, may Agni carry the oblation. To Agni, Svāhā!
I place before me the auspicious goddess Ākūti; may she, the mother of thought, be easy for us to invoke. May that hope toward which I move be mine alone. May I find her who has entered my mind.
O Bṛhaspati, come to us through our intention; come to us through our intention. Furthermore, bestow fortune upon us, and be one who is easily invoked by us.
May Bṛhaspati, the descendant of Aṅgiras, recognize this my intention and this speech. He with whom the gods have become deities—may that well-guided Desire follow after us.
Indra is the king of the moving world and of human beings upon the earth; from that which exists in manifold forms, he bestows riches upon the donor. May he, being praised, impel bounty hitherward.
The Puruṣa has a thousand arms, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet; having pervaded the earth on all sides, he transcended it by the measure of ten fingers.
With three quarters he ascended the sky; one quarter of him remained here again. Thus he strode out in all directions, following after his food upon food.
So great are his majesties, and yet the Puruṣa is even greater than that. One quarter of him is all beings; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.
The Person alone is all this, whatever has been and whatever is to be; he is the lord of immortality, even that which was produced by another.
When they divided Puruṣa, into how many parts did they apportion him? What was his mouth, what were his arms, and what are his thighs and feet called?

The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; his arms became the Rājanya (Kṣatriya); that which was his waist became the Vaiśya; from his feet the Śūdra was born. From his mind the moon was born; from his eye the sun was born; from his mouth Indra and Agni were born; from his breath Vāyu was born.
From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved; from his feet the earth, and from his hearing the quarters—thus they fashioned the worlds.
In the beginning, Virāj came into being; from Virāj was born Puruṣa. Once born, he extended beyond the earth behind and also before it.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with Puruṣa as the oblation, spring was its clarified butter, summer the fuel, and autumn the offering.
They sprinkled that sacrifice with the rainy season, the Puruṣa who was born in the beginning. With him, the gods sacrificed—the Sādhyas and those who are the Vasus.
From him were born horses, and whatever animals are of two rows of teeth; from him indeed were born cows, and from him were born goats and sheep.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born; from him the meters were born, and from him the Yajus-formulas were produced.

From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) was gathered. He made those animals—the ones of the air, the wild, and the domestic. Seven were his enclosing-sticks (paridhi), and thrice seven were the fuel-sticks (samidh) prepared, when the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound Puruṣa as the victim.
From the head of the great god, seventy-seven rays were born from King Soma, once he had been produced from Puruṣa.

The variegated lights in the sky, the crawling creatures in the world, and those that move with speed—I honor the days with hymns, seeking Turmiṣa’s favor and the firmament that is easy to invoke, O Agni.

May Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī be auspicious; may Mṛgaśiras be peaceful and Ārdrā bring well-being. May the two Punarvasūs be gracious, Puṣya be pleasant, Bhānu and Āśleṣā my path, and Maghā my merit. May the two Pūrvaphalgunīs be holy here, Hasta, Citrā, and Śivā-Svāti be a source of happiness for me. May Viśākhā be prosperity, Anurādhā easy to invoke, Jyeṣṭhā a good constellation, and Mūla free from harm.
May the *Pūrva-aṣāḍhās* grant me food; may the divine *Uttarā-aṣāḍhās* bring me strength. May *Abhijit* grant me merit; may *Śravaṇa* and the *Śraviṣṭhās* provide me with excellent nourishment.
May the great *Śatabhiṣaj* grant me wide space; may the two *Proṣṭhapadās* grant me secure shelter. May *Revatī* and the two *Aśvayujīs* grant me fortune; may the *Bharaṇīs* bring me wealth to me.

Whatever constellations are in heaven, in the intermediate space, in the waters, on the earth, those which are among the mountains, and those in the quarters—whatever moon traverses while ordaining them, may all these be auspicious for me.
May the twenty-eight auspicious and propitious [days] grant me union. I resort to union and security; I resort to security and union. Let there be homage to day and night.

May there be well-being for me; may my morning be auspicious, my evening auspicious, my day auspicious, my deer auspicious, and my bird auspicious. O Agni, having gone to the immortal state and returning again with joy, may my invocation be auspicious.
O Savitṛ, drive away from me all those who revile, who cause harm, who speak ill, and who mock; drive them away like empty jars.
May we consume the sinless, the auspicious, and the purifying snot; may the sinless one and the one who goes to merit urinate upon your nose, O evil one!
These drops which spread in all directions and rise up in the wind, O Brahmaṇaspati—making them flow together, O Indra, make them most auspicious for me.
May there be well-being for us; may there be fearlessness for us; let our homage be to Ahar and Ura-tra.

Peaceful is the sky, peaceful the earth, peaceful this wide atmosphere. Peaceful are the waters rich in moisture; may the plants be peaceful for us. Peaceful are the primal forms; may what has been done and what remains undone be peaceful for us. Peaceful be the past and the future; may everything indeed be peace for us.
This goddess of speech who is supreme, the divine one sharpened by sacred knowledge (*brahman*), by which she created even the terrible—by that very power, may there be peace for us.

This mind of yours, O Supreme Lord, which is the Brahman sharpened by sacred power—by that very means through which you created the terrible, may there be peace for us. These five senses within my heart, with the mind as the sixth, have been sharpened by the Brahman; by those very means through which they created the terrible, may there be peace for us.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, may Viṣṇu be auspicious, may Prajāpati be auspicious. May Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman be auspicious to us.

May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, may Vivasvān be auspicious, and may Antaka be auspicious. May terrestrial and atmospheric portents be auspicious to us, and may the planets moving in the heavens be auspicious to us. May the trembling earth be auspicious to us, and may meteors and that which is struck down be auspicious. May cows with red milk be auspicious, and may the earth as it flows downward be auspicious. May a constellation struck by a meteor be auspicious to us; may sorceries be auspicious to us, and may magical spells be auspicious. May buried charms be auspicious to us, and may meteors and regional calamities likewise be auspicious to us.
May the lunar planets be auspicious to us, and may the Sun together with Rāhu be auspicious. May Death and the comet Dhūmaketu be auspicious to us; may the Rudras of fierce splendor be auspicious.

May the Rudras be auspicious, the Vasus be auspicious, the Ādityas be auspicious, and the Fires be auspicious. May the great seers and gods be auspicious to us; may the gods be auspicious and Bṛhaspati be auspicious.

Brahmā, Prajāpati, Dhātṛ, the worlds, the Vedas, the seven sages, and the fires—by them has this auspicious rite been performed for me. May Indra grant me protection; may Brahmā grant me protection. May all the gods grant me protection; may every god grant me protection. Whatever peaceful things the seven sages know in this world, may they all be auspicious for me; may there be peace for me, may there be fearlessness for me.
Peace, peace, peace, with all forms of peace!
Whatever here is terrible, whatever here is cruel, whatever here is evil—may that be stilled, may that be auspicious; may there be peace for us in every respect.

May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be auspicious to us. May Indra and Soma be auspicious for our well-being and for health; may Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious to us in the winning of booty. May Bhaga be auspicious to us, and may our praise be auspicious; may Puraṃdhi be auspicious to us, and may riches be auspicious to us. May the praise of the true and well-governed one be auspicious to us; may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious to us.

May the Ordainer be auspicious to us, and may the Sustainer be auspicious to us; may the far-reaching [Earth] be auspicious to us with her self-sustaining powers. May the two great worlds, Heaven and Earth, be auspicious, may the mountain be auspicious to us, and may the invocations of the gods be auspicious to us.

May Agni, whose face is light, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa and the Aśvins be auspicious to us. May the good deeds of the doers of good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us.

May Heaven and Earth be auspicious to us at our first invocation; may the mid-air be auspicious for our sight. May the plants and the trees be auspicious to us; may the victorious Lord of the Atmosphere be auspicious to us.

May the god Indra with the Vasus be auspicious to us; may Varuṇa, the one of good renown, with the Ādityas be auspicious; may Rudra, the healer, with the Rudras be auspicious to us; and may Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine wives hear us here for our well-being.

May Soma be auspicious to us, may the sacred prayer (*brahman*) be auspicious to us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious to us, and may the sacrifices be auspicious. May the measurements of the sacrificial posts be auspicious to us, may the plants be auspicious to us, and may the altar be auspicious. May the far-seeing Sun rise for our welfare; may the four quarters of space be auspicious to us. May the firm mountains be auspicious to us, may the rivers be auspicious to us, and may the waters be auspicious.

May Aditi be auspicious to us through her sacred laws; may the Maruts, the singers of fair hymns, be auspicious to us. May Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and may Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may the All-Being be auspicious to us, and may Vāyu also be auspicious to us.

May the divine Savitṛ, our protector, grant us peace; may the radiant dawns be auspicious for us. May Parjanya be auspicious for our progeny, and may the Lord of the Field be a source of well-being for us. May the Lords of Truth be auspicious for us; may our horses be auspicious and our cattle likewise be auspicious. May the Ṛbhus, the skillful-handed doers of good deeds, be auspicious for us; may the Fathers be auspicious for us in our invocations.

May all the gods be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī, together with our inspired thoughts, be auspicious. May those who accompany us be auspicious, and may those who grant gifts be auspicious; may the celestial and terrestrial beings be auspicious to us, and may those belonging to the waters be auspicious to us.

May the god Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us, may Ahi Budhnya be auspicious, and may the ocean be auspicious. May the swelling Son of the Waters be auspicious to us, and may Pṛśni, protected by the gods, be auspicious to us.

May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus take pleasure in this newly fashioned prayer being performed. May the celestial and terrestrial ones, those born of the Cow, and those who are worthy of sacrifice, hear us.

Those who are the officiating priests of the gods, worthy of sacrifice, the venerable ones of Manu, the immortal guardians of *ṛta*—may they grant us today wide space for our movement. Do you ever protect us with your blessings! May that be so, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may that be so, O Agni. May this be peace and well-being for us; may this recitation be auspicious. May we attain a firm footing and a secure foundation. Homage to the vast sky, the dwelling place! Dawn rolls away the darkness of her sister and turns her path toward the light. O well-born one, through this may we win the god-ordained prize. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
Indra’s arms are powerful and bull-like; these two bulls are wondrous and victorious. As the first to join, I shall yoke them when the time arrives—those by which the light of the Asuras was won.

Swift, sharpening his weapons like a terrible bull, the striker, the agitator of the people, the roaring one, the unblinking, the sole hero, Indra has conquered a hundred armies at once. With him who roars, who does not blink, who is victorious, who is invincible in battle, immovable, and bold—with that Indra, O men, conquer and prevail in combat, with the bull who holds arrows in his hand.

He who holds arrows in his hand, who carries quivers, who wields power, Indra is the one who brings together the hosts in battle with his troop. Conqueror of the joined forces, drinker of Soma, strong of arm, he whose bow is fierce, he shoots with well-aimed shafts.

Known for his might, steadfast, pre-eminent hero, victorious, swift, subduing, and terrible; superior hero, superior warrior, winner of strength—O Indra, mount your victorious, cattle-finding chariot!

Rejoice after this hero; O friends, rally together after the fierce Indra! He who conquers the villages, who wins the cattle, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, who is victorious in the race, and who crushes with his might—plunging into the cow-pens with force, the irresistible, the fierce Indra of a hundredfold wrath, unshakable, the subduer of armies, and invincible—may he protect our hosts in the battles.

O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slayer of demons, driving away our enemies; shattering the foes and crushing our adversaries, be the protector of our bodies. May Indra be their leader, may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), and Soma go before them; may the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies as they shatter and conquer.
The fierce host of the bull Indra, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts—the roar of these high-minded, world-shaking, victorious gods has arisen.
May Indra be ours when the banners meet; may those arrows which are ours be victorious. May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in our calls for aid!
I have come to this most excellent dwelling; may Heaven and Earth be auspicious to me. May the quarters be free from rivals for me; we do not hate you, may there be safety for us.
From whatever we fear, O Indra, grant us freedom from fear there. O Maghavan, help us; with your protections, strike down our enemies and our adversaries.
We invoke Indra, the one who bestows wealth; may we prosper in our bipeds and quadrupeds. Let not hostile armies come against us; O Indra, destroy the enemies in every direction.
Indra is the protector and the slayer of Vṛtra, the increaser, the most excellent. May he be our guardian from the furthest point, from the middle, from behind, and from the front.
O Knower, lead us toward a wide world—toward the light of heaven that is free from fear and auspicious. O Indra, may we dwell under the protection of your two mighty, firm, and vast arms.
May the mid-air grant us freedom from fear; may both Heaven and Earth grant us freedom from fear. May there be freedom from fear for us from behind, from the front, from above, and from below.

Fearlessness from friend and fearlessness from foe, fearlessness from kinsman and fearlessness from those before us; fearlessness by night and fearlessness by day—may all the quarters become my friends.
May there be freedom from rivals before us; may fearlessness be established behind us. May Savitṛ protect me from the south, and the Lord of Might from the north.

May the Ādityas guard me from the sky, and the fires guard me from the earth. May Indra and Agni protect me from the front, and may the Aśvins grant me shelter on both sides. May the inviolable Jātavedas protect me from the transverse direction; may the creators of beings be my armor on all sides.

May Agni protect me from the east with the Vasus. In that step, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. May he protect me; may he guard me; to him I entrust myself—Svāhā! May Vāyu protect me from this direction with the intermediate space (antarikṣa). In that step, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. May he protect me; may he guard me; to him I entrust myself—Svāhā!

May Soma with the Rudras protect me from the southern direction. In that step, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself—*svāhā*. May Varuṇa with the Ādityas protect me from this direction. In that step, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself—*svāhā*.

May Sūrya protect me from the western quarter, from heaven and earth. In him I step; in him I take refuge; to that fortress I go. May he protect me; may he guard me; to him I entrust myself. *Svāhā!* May the waters rich in herbs protect me from this quarter. In them I step; in them I take refuge; to that fortress I go. May they protect me; may they guard me; to them I entrust myself. *Svāhā!*

May Viśvakarman with the seven seers protect me from the northern quarter. In that step, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā! May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from this quarter. In that step, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!

May Prajāpati, the procreative, protect me together with the firm foundation from the fixed quarter (the zenith). In that step, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he protect me; may he guard me; unto him I entrust myself—*svāhā*.

May Bṛhaspati, together with all the gods, protect me from the upward quarter (the zenith). In that step, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he protect me; may he guard me; unto him I entrust myself—*svāhā*.

May they who are malevolent and seek to harm me from the eastern direction encounter Agni accompanied by the Vasus. May those who are malevolent and seek to harm me from this direction encounter Vāyu accompanied by the atmosphere. May those who are malevolent and seek to harm me from the southern direction encounter Soma accompanied by Rudra.

May Varuṇa, accompanied by the Ādityas, strike those malicious ones who would attack me from this direction. May Sūrya, accompanied by Heaven and Earth, strike those malicious ones who would attack me from the western direction.
May the Waters, accompanied by the Plants, strike those malicious ones who would attack me from this direction.
May they who would do me harm from the northern quarter encounter Viśvakarman accompanied by the seven seers;
may they who would do me harm from this quarter encounter Indra accompanied by the Maruts;
may they who would do me harm from the fixed quarter encounter Prajāpati, the procreative one.

May they strike Bṛhaspati, who is accompanied by all the gods, those malicious ones who would attack me from the upward direction. Mitra rose up from the earth; I lead that fortress forward for you. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
The wind ascended with the intermediate space; I lead you toward that fortress. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both protection and defense.
The Sun has ascended by day; I lead you forward to that fortress. Enter it, go deep within it; may it grant you protection and armor.
The moon rose up together with the constellations; I lead you toward that city. Enter it, penetrate it; may it grant you protection and armor.
Soma has ascended with the plants; I lead you toward that fortress. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
