The sacrifice has ascended with the sacrificial fees; I lead you toward that fortress. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both protection and armor.
The ocean rose up with the rivers; I lead you toward that city. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both protection and armor.
Brahman rose up with the students of sacred knowledge (brahmacārins); I lead you forward to that fortress. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
Indra ascended by means of his heroic power; I lead you toward that fortress. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you protection and armor.
By means of the nectar of immortality, the gods ascended; I lead you forward to that fortress. Enter it, enter into it deeply; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
Prajāpati ascended together with his subjects; I lead you toward that fortress. Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.

Whatever human slaughter they have ordained—whether by Indra, Agni, Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, King Soma, Varuṇa, the Aśvins, Yama, or Pūṣan—from death may he protect us. Whatever the Lord of the World, Prajāpati Mātariśvan, has fashioned for his creatures, and whatever the quarters and intermediate directions wear as their clothing—may those many protections be mine. That armor which the gods, the lords of light, the embodied ones, bound upon their bodies, and that armor which Indra made—that may it protect us from every side.
May Heaven and Earth be my armor; may the Day be my armor; may the Sun be my armor. May all the gods provide armor for me; let not the returning [arrow] strike me.
May the Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī [protect me].
To the first five sections of the Āṅgirasas, Svāhā!
To the sixth, svāhā!
Svāhā to the seventh and eighth [breaths].
Svāhā to the blue nails!
Svāhā to the green ones!
Svāhā to the lowly ones!
Svāhā to those who are synonymous!
Svāhā to the first conchs!
Svāhā to the second conchs!
Svāhā to the third conchs!
Svāhā to those that are near the end.
Svāhā to the most excellent ones!
Svāhā to the northern ones!
Svāhā to the seers!
Svāhā to the crested ones!
Svāhā to the hosts!
Svāhā to the great hosts!
Svāhā to all the Aṅgirases and the Vidagaṇas!
To Pṛthak-sahasrābhyām, svāhā!
Svāhā to Brahman!

Powers were gathered with Brahma as the eldest; in the beginning, Brahma stretched out the sky, the eldest. Brahma was born as the first of all beings; who then is worthy to rival that Brahma? Svāhā to the four-verse hymns of the Atharvans!
Svāhā to the five verses!
Svāhā to the six-verse hymns!
Svāhā to the seven-versed hymns!
Svāhā to those consisting of eight verses!
Svāhā to the nine-verse hymns!
Svāhā to the ten-verse hymns!
Svāhā to the eleven verses!
Svāhā to the twelve-versed hymns!
Svāhā to the thirteen verses!
Svāhā to the fourteen ṛcas!
Svāhā to the fifteen verses!
Svāhā to the sixteen verses!
Svāhā to the seventeen verses!
Svāhā to the eighteen verses!
Nineteen, svāhā!
Twenty, svāhā!
Hail to the great section!
Hail to the triple verses!
Svāhā to those consisting of a single verse!
Hail to the minor ones!
Svāhā to the one for those who do not recite the Ṛgveda!
Hail to the ruddy ones!
Svāhā to the two suns!
Svāhā to the two Vrātyas!
To the two belonging to Prajāpati, svāhā!
To the one who endures poison, svāhā!
Svāhā to those who bring auspiciousness!
Svāhā to Brahman!
The powers were gathered with Brahma as the eldest; in the beginning, Brahma stretched out the highest heaven. Brahma was born as the first of all beings; who then is worthy to rival that Brahma?
With that [power] by which the gods sustained the divine Savitṛ, with that, O Brahmanaspati, endow this man for the sake of sovereignty.
Bestow this Indra upon long life and great sovereignty, so that you may lead him to old age, and he may remain watchful for a long time over his dominion.
Bestow this Indra upon long life and great hearing, so that you may lead him to old age, and he may remain watchful for a long time over his sense of hearing.
Clothe him, clothe him with splendor; make this one free from old age and death, grant him a long life! Bṛhaspati has bestowed this garment for King Soma to put on.
Go well to old age; put on your garment; become a protector against the curse of the young cows. Live for a hundred abundant autumns, and clothe yourself in the increase of wealth.
You have put on this garment for well-being; you have become the protector of the waters against curses. Live for a hundred abundant autumns, and being lovely, distribute riches while living.
In every endeavor, in every contest, we, your friends, call upon Indra, the most powerful one, for our aid.
Golden-hued, undecaying, and possessed of noble heroes, enter into old age and death along with your progeny. This Agni has said, and Soma has said it; Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra have said it.
I yoke thee with the mind of one who is unwearied and foremost. Be a carrier up the slope; having carried it up, run back again.
That immortal gold which was produced from Agni and placed among mortals—he who knows this, he alone is worthy of it. Old age and death come upon him who wears it.
The gold that was fashioned by the sun, which the ancient progenitors possessing offspring desired—that bright [metal] unites you with splendor; he who wears it becomes long-lived.

For life I take you; for splendor I take you; for vigor and for strength. So that through your brilliance, O gold, you may shine resplendently among the people. That which King Varuṇa knows, that which the god Bṛhaspati knows, and that which Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, knows—may that be yours for long life; may that be yours for splendor. Let the bull protect you with cows; let the stallion protect you with vigorous steeds. Let Vāyu protect you with sacred knowledge (*brahman*); let Indra protect you with his powers (*indriya*).
May Soma protect you with the plants; may the Sun protect you with the constellations. May the Moon, the slayer of Vṛtra, protect you from the months; may Vāta protect you with his breath.

The three heavens, the three earths, the three mid-regions, and the four oceans—the Trivṛt Stoma and the Trivṛt Waters—these they call; may they protect you with their triple-folded powers. I appoint for you as guardians the three firmaments, the three oceans, the three radiances, the three Vaiṣṭapas, the three Mātariśvans, and the three Suns.
I sprinkle you with ghee, O Agni, increasing you with clarified butter; may the deceivers not harm the vital breath of Agni, of the Moon, or of the Sun.
May they not harm your out-breath, nor your in-breath, nor your vigor, O masters of illusion! Shining, possessors of all wealth, O gods, run with your divine power!
Vāta unites with Agni through the out-breath; he is joined with the out-breath. Through the out-breath, the gods generated the sun that faces every direction.
Live by means of the lifespan of those who have achieved longevity; live long-lived, do not die! Live by means of the breath of those possessed of self; do not fall under the power of death.

The treasure deposited by the gods, which Indra discovered by means of the paths traveled by the gods—the waters guarded that gold with their triple-layered forms; may they protect you with their triple-layered forms, with their triple-layered protections.
The thirty-three gods and the three heroic powers, acting with affection, guarded [the treasure] within the waters; whatever gold was upon this moon, with that may he perform heroic deeds.
O gods who are eleven in heaven, you gods, may you graciously accept this oblation.
O gods who are eleven in the intermediate space, you gods, may you graciously accept this oblation.
O gods who are eleven upon the earth, you gods, may you graciously accept this oblation.

May there be freedom from rivals before us; may safety be established behind us. May Savitṛ protect me from the south, and the Lord of Might from the north. May the Ādityas guard me from heaven, and the fires guard me from the earth. May Indra and Agni protect me from the front, and may the Aśvins grant me shelter on both sides. May the inviolable Jātavedas protect me from the transverse direction; may the creators of all beings be my armor on every side.
I bind this amulet for you for long life and for splendor—this *darbha* grass, which crushes rivals and scorches the hearts of enemies.
Scorching the hearts of those who hate you, burning the minds of your enemies—O Darbha grass, you who are like the *gharma* vessel, heat all those of evil intent as the *gharma* heats from all sides.
O Darbha, like the *gharma* scorching, O jewel (*maṇi*), burn down the haters; split the hearts of our rivals as Indra shatters the strength of Vṛtra.
O Darbha, O jewel, split the heart of our rivals and those who hate us; rising up, strike off their heads as if peeling the skin from the earth.
Split my rivals, O Darbha; split those who attack me. Split all those of evil heart; split those who hate me, O amulet!
Cut down my rivals, O Darbha; cut down those who attack me. Cut down all those of evil heart; cut down those who hate me, O amulet!
Tear away my rivals, O Darbha; tear away those who attack me. Tear away all those of evil heart; tear away those who hate me, O amulet!

Cut down my rivals, O Darbha; cut down those who array themselves against me. Cut down all those of evil intent; cut down my enemies, O amulet! Pierce my rivals, O Darbha; pierce those who array themselves against me. Pierce all those of evil intent;
pierce my enemies, O amulet! Penetrate my rivals, O Darbha; penetrate those who array themselves against me. Penetrate all those of evil intent; penetrate my enemies, O amulet!

Cast down my rivals, O *darbha* grass; cast down those who attack me; cast down all those of evil heart; cast down those who hate me, O amulet! Tear asunder my rivals, O *darbha* grass; tear asunder those who attack me; tear asunder all those of evil heart; tear asunder those who hate me, O amulet! Block my rivals, O *darbha* grass; block those who attack me; block all those of evil heart; block those who hate me, O amulet!

Crush my rivals, O Darbha; crush those who array themselves against me. Crush all who are evil-hearted; crush those who hate me, O amulet! Grind my rivals, O Darbha; grind those who array themselves against me. Grind all who are evil-hearted;
grind those who hate me, O amulet! Pound my rivals, O Darbha; pound those who array themselves against me. Pound all who are evil-hearted; pound those who hate me, O amulet!

Burn my rivals, O Darbha; burn those who attack me. Burn all the evil-hearted ones; burn my enemies, O amulet! Scorch my rivals, O Darbha; scorch those who attack me. Scorch all the evil-hearted ones; scorch my enemies, O amulet! Slay my rivals, O Darbha; slay those who attack me. Slay all the evil-hearted ones; slay my enemies, O amulet!
O Darbha, that which is your aging and death, let it be a hundredfold armor among your armors; having made this man armored with that, slay his rivals with your heroic powers.
A hundred are your protective shields of *darbha*, a thousand are your heroic powers. All the gods have given you over to him to wear for his protection.
They call you the divine armor; they call you, *darbha*, the Lord of Prayer (*brahman*). They call you the armor of Indra; you guard the kingdoms.

I fashion for you this *darbha* amulet, which destroys rivals, burns the heart of the enemy, increases dominion, and protects the body. When the ocean roared aloud together with Parjanya and the lightning, from that [roar] was born the golden drop, and from that the *darbha* was born.
With an amulet of udumbara wood, may Savitṛ, the Ordainer, provide abundance for me who desire prosperity; may he cause the increase of all cattle within my fold.
May Agni, our domestic fire, who is the sovereign lord of cattle, and this male amulet of udumbara wood, unite me with nourishment.
May Dhātṛ bestow upon me prosperity through the splendor of the udumbara tree, so that there may be manure, fruitfulness, self-sustaining power, and refreshing food in our home.
Whatever two-footed and four-footed beings there are, whatever foods and flavors exist—of these I take the abundance, wearing this amulet made of udumbara wood.
I have grasped the nourishment of cattle, of quadrupeds and bipeds, and whatever grain there is. May Bṛhaspati and Savitṛ bestow upon me the milk of cattle and the sap of plants.
May I be the sovereign lord of cattle; may the Lord of Nourishment place nourishment within me. May this amulet made of udumbara wood bestow riches upon me.
May the Udumbara amulet come to me with progeny and with wealth; may the amulet, impelled by Indra, come to me together with splendor.
May the divine amulet, the slayer of rivals and winner of riches, grant us the acquisition of wealth. May it bestow upon us an abundance of cattle and food, and the increase of our herds of cows.

Just as you, O Lord of the Forest, were born at the beginning together with prosperity, so may Sarasvatī bestow upon me an abundance of wealth. May Sarasvatī bring to me wealth, the swelling of milk, and grain; may Sinīvālī bring them hither, as well as this amulet made of *udumbara* wood.

You are the lord of amulets, a bull; the Lord of Prosperity has produced nourishment within you. In you are all these strengths and riches. Therefore, O *audumbara*, overcome from afar—yea, from afar—the enemy, the lack of vision, and hunger.
You are a village-leader; having risen as a consecrated leader, sprinkle me with splendor. You are brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. You are wealth; grant me wealth.

You are nourishment; anoint me with nourishment. As the house-sacrificer, make me the master of the household. Being made of Udumbara wood, bestow wealth upon us; grant us riches consisting of all heroic sons. I fasten you on for the increase of wealth.
This Udumbara amulet, a hero, is bound upon the hero. May it make our gain sweet and rich; may it grant us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
With a hundred stalks, difficult to shake, a thousand leaves, and most excellent—this fierce Darbha plant, this herb—I bind upon you for long life.
They do not shave his hair, nor do they strike him on the chest, for whom one provides protection with a darbha blade whose leaf is unbroken.
O herb, your tuft is in heaven; you are firmly established upon the earth. Through you, who possess a thousand stalks, we cause our life-span to increase.
He has pierced through the three heavens and these three earths; with you, I pierce the tongue and the words of the evil-hearted.
You are the overcomer; I am the overcomer. Having both become possessors of power, may we overcome our rivals.
Overpower our adversary; overpower those who attack us in battle. Overpower all the ill-hearted ones, and make many for me who are well-disposed.

With this Darbha grass, born of the gods, which has eternally supported the heavens—I, by means of it, have won and shall win all people forever. O Darbha, make me dear to the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya, to the Śūdra and the Ārya, and to whomever we desire, and to every one who perceives.
He who, being born, made the earth firm, who propped up the mid-air and the sky—he whom no evil ever found while he was bearing [the world], may this Darbha grass be for us like Varuṇa in heaven.

The slayer of rivals, with a hundred stalks, possessing thousandfold power, it became the first among plants. May this Darbha protect us on every side; with it may I overcome the armies of those who attack us.

Worth a thousand, with a hundred joints, full of milk, the fire of the waters, the royal consecration of plants—may this *darbha* protect us on every side; may the divine amulet endow us with long life.

Drawn forth from clarified butter, honey-sweet, full of milk, the stabilizer of the earth, unshakable yet able to shake others—driving away rivals and casting them down, O *darbha*, grow great with the power of the mighty!
You traverse the earth with your might; you sit upon the sacrificial altar, beautiful at the rite. The seers brought you as a means of purification; purify us from all misfortunes.

Sharp, a king, invincible, slayer of demons, beholder of all people—this is the fierce power and strength of the gods. I bind this upon you for old age and well-being. Through the *darbha* grass, may you perform heroic deeds; bearing the *darbha*, do not falter in yourself. Surpassing others in luster, shine forth like the sun toward the four quarters of space.
You are Jaṅgiḍa, you are the Jaṅgiḍa; you are the protector, the Jaṅgiḍa. May the Jaṅgiḍa protect all of us—our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
Those spells of the crafty man, the three, the five, the fifty, and the hundred sorcerers—may the Jaṅgiḍa, by its brilliance, separate them all and render them powerless.
Render the artificial roar powerless; render the seven decaying powers powerless. Like an archer striking away an arrow, drive away the malady from the Jaṅgiḍa.

This very Jaṅgiḍa is the destroyer of sorcery, and also the destroyer of hostility; moreover, as a powerful one, may Jaṅgiḍa prolong our lifespans. May that greatness of Jaṅgiḍa protect us on every side—by which he overcame *viṣkandha* with his might, and *saṃskandha* with his vigor.
The gods thrice generated you, established upon the earth; you, the ancient Brahmins know you as "Aṅgiras."

Neither the ancient plants nor those that are new surpass you. The formidable *jaṅgiḍa* is a dispeller of obstacles, a protector, and most auspicious. Therefore, O Blessed One, O *jaṅgiḍa* of immeasurable power, before these fierce ones devour you, Indra bestowed his own vigor upon you.
O Lord of the Forest, Indra has indeed bestowed his fierce vigor upon you; O Herb, drive away all maladies and slay the demons.
May the Jaṅgiḍa render powerless the bodiless and the body-shattering consumption, the pain in the back, and the *takman* fever that returns every autumn.
The seers, uttering the name of Indra, bestowed the Jaṅgiḍa; it is that which the gods made into a medicine in the beginning, the destroyer of *viṣkandha*.
May that Jaṅgiḍa protect us, like a guardian of wealth protects riches. It is that which the gods and the Brahmins made into a protective amulet, the slayer of the enemy.

The evil-hearted one has come with a terrible eye after committing a sin; destroy them, O thousand-eyed one, through your awakening! You, Jaṅgiḍa, are our complete protection. Protect me from heaven, protect me from earth, protect me from the intermediate space, protect me from the plants! Protect me from the past and protect me from the future; let Jaṅgiḍa protect us in every direction.
Whatever sorcery has been wrought by the gods, or whatever else has been turned against us—let Jaṅgiḍa, the possessor of all remedies, render them all powerless.
A hundred times has it destroyed consumption and demons by its brilliance; ascending with splendor, this amulet drives away those of evil name.
With its two horns it pushes back the *rakṣas*, with its root the sorceresses, and with its middle it repels consumption; no evil shall overcome him.
The wasting diseases that are small and those that are great, and those that are noisy—all those with evil names, the hundred-crested amulet has destroyed.
It has produced a hundred heroes and cast away a hundred diseases. Having slain all those with evil names, it shakes off the demons.
This amulet is a bull with golden horns and a hundred crests; having trampled all those with evil names, it has stepped down upon the demons.
A hundred of the ill-named ones, a hundred Gandharvas and Apsarases, a hundred of those who are ever-present—I ward them off with the hundred-fold filter.
This splendor has come to me, given by Agni: radiance, glory, power, vigor, vitality, and strength—whatever thirty-three heroic powers there are, may Agni bestow them upon me.
Bestow splendor upon my body, power, vigor, vitality, and strength. For the sake of sensory power, for ritual action, and for heroism, I receive you for a hundred autumns.
For vigor, for strength, for power, for conquest, for supremacy, and for the maintenance of the kingdom, I carry you around for a hundred autumns.
I sacrifice to you for the seasons, for the seasonal periods, for the months, and for the years; to Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Samṛdh, and the Lord of all that has come to be.

Consumptions do not hold him back, nor does a curse reach him, whom the fragrant scent of the healing *gulgulu* reaches. From him the consumptions flee in all directions, like deer or horses. Whether you are *gulgulu*, whether you are from the Indus (*saindhava*), or even if you are from the ocean—I have grasped the name of both for his safety.
May the divine *kuṣṭha*, the protector, come from the Himavat mountains. Destroy every *takman* and all sorceresses (*yātudhānī*).

Three are your names, *kuṣṭha*: *nadyamāra*, *nadyāriṣa*. May this man of the river not suffer harm; for whomsoever I address you, evening and morning, and likewise by day. *Jīvalā* is your mother’s name; *jīvanta* is your father’s name. May this man of the river not suffer harm; for whomsoever I address you, evening and morning, and likewise by day.

You are the best among herbs, as the ox is among moving creatures, and as the tiger is among beasts of prey. May this man not come to harm from the river—to whomsoever I address you at evening, at dawn, and likewise by day.

Three times from the waters, three times from the Aṅgirases, three times from the Ādityas, and three times born from the Viśvedevas—this Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma. The Aśvattha tree, the seat of the gods, is in the third heaven from here. There is the manifestation of immortality; from there Kuṣṭha was born. This Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma. A golden ship, bound with gold, moved in the sky. There is the manifestation of immortality; from there Kuṣṭha was born. This Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, [stands] together with Soma.
The headache, the tertian fever, the one with the stinging pain, and that which lasts for a year—drive away the *takman* in every way with your power, casting it downward.

Whatever flaw there is in my mind and whatever in my speech, may Sarasvatī, being in agreement with all the gods, mend it together with Bṛhaspati. O Waters, do not destroy our wisdom or our sacred knowledge; flow forth as you are wont to swell, for I have been invoked, wise and full of luster.
Do not harm our wisdom, nor our consecration, nor our ascetic heat (*tapas*). May they be auspicious for us; may they be propitious for our life. May the Mothers be auspicious.
May the Aśvins grant us that nourishing food (*iṣ*) which, full of light, has carried us across the darkness.

Desiring what is auspicious and finding the light of heaven, the seers (*ṛṣis*) first sat down to ascetic heat and consecration. From that, sovereignty, strength, and vital power were born; may the gods grant these to him.
The Brahman is the Hotṛ; the sacrifices are the Brahman; by the Brahman the sacrificial posts are measured. The Adhvaryu is born from the Brahman; the oblation is contained within the Brahman.

The ladles full of ghee are the Brahman; by the Brahman the altar is raised. The Brahman is the essence of the sacrifice, as are the officiating priests who prepare the oblations. Svāhā to the immolator!
To the deliverer from distress, I offer my inspired thought, seeking his favor for the sake of easy protection. O Indra, accept this oblation; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.

I invoke the Son of the Waters, the deliverer from distress, the bull among those worthy of sacrifice, the radiant one, the foremost of rituals—the two Aśvins. By means of Indra’s power, may your own power and vital strength be bestowed.

Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity, may Agni lead me there; may Agni bestow wisdom upon me. Svāhā to Agni! Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity, may Vāyu lead me there; may Vāyu bestow vital breaths upon me. Svāhā to Vāyu!
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity, may Sūrya lead me there; may Sūrya bestow sight upon me. Svāhā to Sūrya!

Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may the Moon lead me there; may the Moon bestow it upon me. Svāhā to the Moon! Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Soma lead me there; may Soma bestow milk upon me. Svāhā to Soma!
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Indra lead me there; may Indra bestow strength upon me. Svāhā to Indra!
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity, may the Waters lead me there; may immortality attend me. Svāhā to the Waters!
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity, may Brahman lead me there; may Brahman bestow Brahman upon me. Svāhā to Brahman!
You are the prolonger of life, you are called the wise remedy. O Ointment, grant us well-being; may the Waters bring peace and security.
Whatever jaundice, wasting disease of the limbs, bone-splitting pain, or neuralgia there may be—may this ointment drive all that consumption out from your limbs.
May the collyrium born from the earth, auspicious and sustaining life for man, grant us freedom from untimely death, swift motion like a chariot, and innocence.
O Breath, protect my breath; be gracious unto my vital force. O Nirṛti, release us from the nooses of destruction.
You are the offspring of the ocean, the flower of the lightning-flashes. Wind is your breath, the sun is your eye, and you are the milk of heaven.
O divine collyrium from the three-peaked mountain, protect me on every side! Neither the plants of the plains nor those of the mountains surpass you.
This destroyer of demons and dispeller of disease has spread through this middle world. He drives away all maladies and destroys all afflictions from here.
O King Varuṇa, man has spoken much falsehood here; therefore, O you of a thousand powers, release us from this distress.

Whatever we have said, "O Waters, O Invincible Ones," or "O Varuṇa," from that, O thou of a thousand powers, release us from distress. Both Mitra and Varuṇa followed thee, O Ointment; having followed thee for a long distance, they have turned back again for their own enjoyment.
As one debt from another, bring together the spell (*kṛtyā*) made by the spell-maker into his own house. Crush the ribs of the evil-hearted one with the eye of the mantra!
Whatever ill-omened dream is among us, whatever is among our cattle, and whatever is in our house—let that which is dear to the evil-hearted one be released upon him as a disease.
This mountain-born ointment, born of the waters, of vigor, and of strength, produced from Agni Jātavedas—may it bring four heroes and make the quarters and intermediate directions auspicious for you.
The four-hero ointment is bound upon you; may all the quarters be free from fear for you. Stand firm like Savitṛ, the noble one; let these subjects bring tribute to you.
Take up one [of these], make one a jewel, bathe with one, and drink one of them. May the four-hero [ointment] protect us from the four bonds of Nirṛti and from the grasp of the female spirits.
May Agni protect me with Agni for the sake of out-breath, in-breath, long life, luster, vigor, splendor, well-being, and prosperity—*svāhā*!
May Indra protect me with his Indra-power for out-breath, in-breath, long life, luster, vigor, splendor, well-being, and prosperity—*svāhā*!
May Soma protect me with his Soma-nature for out-breath, in-breath, long life, luster, vigor, splendor, well-being, and prosperity—*svāhā*!
May Bhaga protect me with his fortune for out-breath, in-breath, long life, luster, vigor, splendor, well-being, and prosperity—*svāhā*!
May the Maruts protect me with their hosts for the sake of out-breath, in-breath, long life, luster, vigor, and splendor. Svāhā! For well-being and prosperity!

Prajāpati bound you first, so that you might be invincible for the sake of heroism. Therefore, I bind this upon you for long life, luster, vigor, and strength; may it protect you as one who is invincible.

Stand upright, guarding with vigilance; let not the Paṇis nor the sorcerers deceive you. Like Indra, shake off the Dasyus who attack us; overcome all enemies, O invincible one! May he protect you from behind.
Even those striking and slaying in their hundreds have not prevailed against you. In him, Indra bestowed sight, breath, and strength; may the invincible one protect you from behind.
We clothe you with the armor of Indra, he who has become the sovereign king of the gods. May all the gods lead you back again; may the invincible one protect you.

In this amulet are a hundred heroic powers; in this invincible one are a thousand vital breaths. As a tiger, trample upon all enemies. Whoever shall attack you, let him be cast down; may the invincible one protect you.

Drawn forth from clarified butter, rich in honey, full of milk, possessing a thousand breaths and a hundred wombs, bestowing vital strength—may he who is auspicious, who brings delight, who is full of vigor and full of milk, protect you as he is spread out. May Savitṛ make you so that you may be supreme, without rivals, a slayer of rivals, and a controller over your kinsmen; may he who is invincible protect you. O Night, the earthly realm has been filled with the abodes of the Father; vast one, you spread across the seats of heaven, and the brilliant darkness rolls toward you.
Whose further shore is not seen, nor its end, wherein all that moves comes to rest—O vast, dark Night, may we reach thy further shore unharmed; O auspicious one, may we reach the further shore.
O Night, those who behold men—your watchers, ninety-nine, eighty-eight, and also seventy-seven;
sixty-six, O wealthy one, fifty-five, O gracious one; forty-four, and thirty-three, O vigorous one.

Two and twenty, and eleven as the lowest—by these protectors, O Daughter of Heaven, guard us this day. Protect us; let no one who speaks evil have power over us; let no one of ill intent have power over us. Let not the thief of cattle, nor the wolf of sheep, have power over us today; let not the robber of horses, O Blessed One, nor the sorceresses of men have power over us. Let the thief run away by the highest paths; let the robber flee beyond the biting rope; let the malevolent one pass far away.
Now, O Night, make the serpent headless with its pungent smoke; crush the jaws of the wolf; strike the thief upon the wooden post.
O Night, we dwell in you; we shall sleep; do you remain awake. Grant protection to our cattle, our horses, and our men.
Furthermore, whatever [belongings] we have here and whatever is within our inner clothing—those we entrust to you.
O Mother Night, entrust us to the Dawn; O Radiant One, may the Dawn entrust us to the Day, and the Day to you.
Whatever flies here, whatever creeps here, and whatever mountain-like iron [is here]—from that, O Night, protect us.
Protect us from behind, from the front, from above, and from below. Guard us, O Radiant One; we are here as your praisers.
Those who perform their duties at night, those who remain vigilant toward living beings, and those who protect all cattle—they watch over us in our own persons; they watch over our cattle.
O Night, I truly know your name; you are indeed named Ghṛtācī. Bharadvāja knows you as such; may she watch over our possessions.

The vigorous, youthful maiden, the mistress of the house, the Night of the god Savitṛ and Bhaga—she who is swift as a horse, easily invoked, and endowed with gathered splendor—has filled heaven and earth with her greatness.
Deep and most exalted, she has risen above all things; the most glorious ones have ascended her. Desiring it, O Night, that auspicious one approaches like Mitra with his self-sustaining powers.
I praise you, O auspicious and well-born Night; come hither with a gracious mind. Protect us, O Night born of noble power, and those things belonging to cattle that thrive through nourishment.
O Night, longing for the lion, the tiger, and the leopard, I take up their splendor. As you shine forth, you assume the many forms of the horse’s neighing and the man’s cry.
May the Night, the mother of the snow, be auspicious and easy to invoke for us, following after the sun. O fortunate one, take heed of this hymn with which I praise you in all directions.

O radiant Night, you take pleasure in our hymn like a king; may we be masters of all heroes, may we be possessors of all wealth. As the Dawns have shone forth one after another, you have truly assumed the name *Śamyā* (the Peace-bringer). Those who wish to harm my riches—O Night, through you they shall find no drink; for no thief is found here, none whatsoever is found again. You are auspicious, O Night, like a well-fashioned chalice; as a young woman, you bear a form that spreads in every direction. Possessing eyes and longing, you display your wondrous beauties; like a celestial being, you have not left the earth behind.
Whatever thief comes today, whatever mortal enemy with evil intent, may Night, having encountered him, strike off his necks and strike off his head.
As one who draws back his feet, as one who withdraws his hands; he who approaches as a thief departs crushed. He departs, he departs well; he departs upon a withered stump.
Now, O Night, make the serpent smoke-breathing and headless; strike out the two eyes of the wolf; with that, slay him upon the wooden post.

O Night, those oxen of yours that have sharp horns and are very swift—with them, ferry us today across all difficulties forever. Night after night, may we cross over unharmed in our bodies; may our enemies not cross over, like those without a boat in the deep.
Just as the *śāmyāka* bird, when it falls, is no longer found, so, O Night, cause him to fall who seeks to harm us.
You have clothed the thief who steals cattle and goats, as well as the robber; and also him who, having covered the head of a horse, desires to lead it away.
O fortunate one, whatever wealth they distribute today during the night—enjoy that for us, so that you may approach others as well.
O Night, deliver us all to the Dawn free from sin; may Uṣas grant us to the Day, and the Day to you, O Radiant One.
I am unbounded; my self is unbounded; my eye is unbounded; my ear is unbounded. My out-breath is unbounded; my in-breath is unbounded; my diffused breath is unbounded; I am everything, unbounded.
Impelled by the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, being thus impelled, I take hold of you.

In the beginning, desire arose within that [Being], which was the first seed of the mind. O Desire, being of one womb with the Great One through desire, bestow upon the sacrificer the increase of wealth.

O Kāma, you are established by your own power; all-pervading, radiant, and a friend to him who seeks your friendship. You are the fierce conqueror in battles; bestow strength and vigor upon the sacrificer.
For him who yearns from afar, for the inexhaustible counter-stake, the quarters of space have lent their ear; through desire they have generated the light of heaven.
Through desire has desire come to me, from heart to heart. May that mind of theirs which is yonder come here unto me.
O Desire, whatever desire we fulfill for you with this oblation, may all that be fulfilled for us; then, partake of this oblation—svāhā!

Time, the horse with seven reins, thousand-eyed, undecaying, and rich in seed, draws [the world]. Upon him the wise poets, possessed of inspired vision, mount. All worlds are his wheels. This Time carries seven wheels; he has seven naves, and immortality is his axle. He anoints all these worlds; as the first god, Time moves onward.
A full vessel is placed upon Time; we behold him indeed existing in many forms. Facing toward all these worlds, they call that Time the one in the highest heaven.
He alone brought all beings together; he alone went around all beings. Being their father, he became their son; therefore, indeed, there is no other splendor higher than him.
Time generated yonder sky; Time [generated] these earths as well. In Time, that which has been and that which is to be are set in motion and spread abroad.
Time created prosperity; in Time the sun burns; in Time indeed all beings exist; in Time the eye perceives clearly.

In Time the mind is contained, in Time the vital breath, and in Time the name is established. By the arrival of Time, all these creatures rejoice. In Time is austerity, in Time is the highest, and in Time is the sacred word (*brahman*) established. Time indeed is the Lord of all, he who was the father of Prajāpati. Impelled by him, born from him, and established in him, Time—having become the *brahman*—supports the Supreme Lord (*Parameṣṭhin*).
Time created living beings; in the beginning, Time created Prajāpati. Kaśyapa was self-existent from Time; austerity was born from Time.
From Time the waters came into being; from Time arose the Veda, austerity, and the quarters. By Time the sun rises; by Time it sets again.
By Time the wind blows; by Time the great earth exists. The vast heaven is established in Time.
In ancient times, Kāla indeed brought forth the past and the future as his son. From Kāla the *ṛc* verses arose; from Kāla the *yajus* formulas were born.
Kāla set in motion the sacrifice, providing an imperishable portion for the gods. In Kāla the Gandharvas and Apsarases dwell; in Kāla the worlds are established.

In Kāla this god Aṅgiras and Atharvan abide. Having conquered by means of the Brahman this world, the highest world, the meritorious worlds, and the holy supports, that supreme god, Kāla, moves through all the worlds.
Bringing to him every night what does not fail, like fodder for a standing horse, may we rejoice in the increase of wealth and in nourishment; O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.
That which is your arrow, O Vasu, that is this wind; with it, be gracious to us. May we rejoice in the increase of wealth and in nourishment; O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.
Night after night may Agni be our lord of the house, morning after morning may he be the giver of goodwill. Be the giver of wealth, O Vasu of every kind; kindling you, may we nourish our bodies.

Every morning may Agni, our householder, and every evening may he be the giver of goodwill; be the bestower of wealth upon every wealth. Kindling you for a hundred winters, may we prosper. May I never be one whose food is burnt from behind. Homage to Rudra, the eater of food and lord of food; homage to Agni. O assembly-fire, protect my assembly and those members of the assembly who sit therein. O Indra, invoked by many, may they enjoy the full span of life, bringing tribute to you day after day, just as one brings fodder to a standing horse, O Agni.
From the world of Yama you have come hither; you, the wise one, impel mortals toward their dissolution. Alone on your chariot you travel, O Knower, measuring out the dream in the womb of the Asura.
At first, Viśvacaya saw you as a bond, before the birth of Night, on that single day. From there, O Dream, you have come hither, hiding your form from the physicians.
Seeking greatness, the vast one turned away from the Asuras toward the gods. To that Dream, the thirty-three [gods], having attained the light of heaven, granted sovereignty.
Neither the fathers nor the gods know this [dream], whose whisper moves within this world. Men have placed their dream in Trita Āptya; the Ādityas are instructed by Varuṇa.

Upon him the evildoers have laid their cruelty, while the doers of good [attain] a holy life through sleeplessness. You revel in heaven with your highest kinsman; you were born from the mind that was being heated.
We know all your origins from of old; we know, O Sleep, who is your sovereign here. Protect us here with glory, O glorious one; go far away from our enemies.
Just as they collect a sixteenth part, just as a half-share, just as a debt, even so do we collect all evil dreams upon that which is unpleasant.

Together have the kings gone; together have the debts gone; together have the *kuṣṭhas* gone; together have the *kalās* gone. Whatever evil dream is among us, we drive that evil dream away to our enemy.

O you who are the offspring of the wives of the gods and the son of Yama, may that dream which is auspicious be mine; that which is evil, we send forth to our enemy. You are not the mouth of the harsh ones, nor of the black bird.

We know you, O Dream, to be such as you are; therefore, O Dream, like a horse that carries a body, like a horse that bears a load, drive away from us the one who harms the gods, the hater. Whatever evil dream is among us, whatever is among our cattle, and whatever is in our house—let that which harms the gods and hates us be cast off by him like a necklace. Having removed nine cubits from us, we cast all evil dreaming upon our enemy.

The impulse of ghee, common to all, that one increases the gods throughout the year with oblation—may our hearing, sight, and breath remain unbroken; may we ourselves remain unbroken in life-span and luster. May breath call upon us; we invoke breath. Earth, atmosphere, Soma, and Bṛhaspati have bestowed luster; may they grant it to us.

O Heaven and Earth, you have become the gatherers of splendor (*varcas*). Having taken hold of splendor, may we move together along the earth. As the cows, approaching, attend upon their glorious master, so may we, having taken hold of glory, move together along the earth.
Make a pen; for that is your protection, O leaders. Sew it with many wide layers as armor. Make iron forts, unassailable. Let not your cup leak; make it firm.
The eye and the beginning of the sacrifice, and its mouth—with speech, with hearing, and with the mind, I offer this sacrifice spread out by Viśvakarman. May the gods come, being well-disposed.

Those who are the priests of the gods, and those who are worthy of sacrifice, to whom the oblation is made as their allotted portion—having come to this sacrifice together with their wives, may all the powerful gods rejoice. O Agni, you are the god who guards the vows among mortals; you are to be praised at the sacrifices.
O Gods, whatever vows of yours we, being less wise than the wise, have violated—may the knowing Agni, who has entered into the Brāhmaṇas as Soma, fulfill all that.
We have come unto the path of the Gods; whatever we are able to perform, let us carry it out. May Agni, the knower, sacrifice; he indeed is the Hotṛ; may he arrange the rites and the seasons.

May speech be in my mouth, breath in my nostrils, sight in my eyes, and hearing in my ears. May my hair be free from grayness, my teeth free from discoloration, and may there be great strength in my arms, vigor in my thighs, speed in my shanks, and stability in my feet. May all my limbs be unharmed, and may my entire self be undecaying. May my body be united with my body; may I attain all life through my teeth. Sit comfortably for me, fill me abundantly, and as the purifying one, dwell in the heavenly realm.

Make me dear among the gods; make me dear among kings; make me dear to everyone who beholds me, whether they be Śūdras or Āryas. Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati; awaken the gods with the sacrifice. Increase the lifespan, the vital breath, progeny, cattle, fame, and the sacrificer.
O Agni, I have brought this fuel for the great Jātavedas; may Jātavedas bestow upon me faith and wisdom.
O Jātavedas, with this fuel-stick we cause you to increase; likewise, do you cause us to increase through progeny and wealth.
O Agni, whatever logs of wood we place before you, may all that be auspicious for me; accept it, O youngest one.
These are your fuel-sticks, O Agni; being kindled, become the fuel itself. Bestow long life upon us and immortality upon our teacher.

Hari, the fair-winged one, has ascended to heaven with his radiance. Those who seek to harm you as you fly up to heaven—strike them down with your heat, O Jātavedas! Fearless and fierce, ascend to heaven with your radiance, O Sūrya.

The iron-netted, illusory Asuras who wander about with iron fetters and hooks—those I subject to you by your heat, O Jātavedas. With a thousand spears, crushing the rivals, protect us like a thunderbolt.
May we see a hundred autumns.
May we live for a hundred autumns.
May we awaken for a hundred autumns.
May we flourish for a hundred autumns.
May Pūṣan [grant] these hundred autumns.
May we live for a hundred autumns.
May we adorn ourselves for a hundred autumns.
For many more than a hundred autumns.
I open the aperture of both the narrow and the wide by means of my creative power (*māyā*). Having extracted the Veda from those two, we shall then perform the ritual acts.
You are living beings; may I live, may I live out the full span of life.

You are those upon whom one lives; may I live upon you; may I live out my full span of life. You are those who live together; may I live together with you; may I live out my full span of life. You are those who cause life; may I live; may I live out my full span of life.
O Indra, live; O Sūrya, live; O gods, live! May I live! May I live out the full span of life!

Praised by me, may the boon-granting Mother of the Vedas, the Pāvamānī verses, inspire the twice-born. Having bestowed upon me long life, vital breath, progeny, cattle, fame, wealth, and Vedic splendor, depart for the world of Brahman!

From that treasury from which we drew forth the Veda, within that very place we deposit this again. This has been accomplished through the power of Brahman; with that austerity, O gods, protect me here!
O Indra, we invoke you, the bull, when the Soma is pressed; as such, drink of the sweet food.
O Maruts, mighty ones of heaven, that person in whose dwelling you drink is indeed most well-protected.
Let us worship Agni with hymns—the ordainer who has bulls for food, cows for food, and Soma upon his back.
May the Maruts, well-praising with beautiful hymns, drink the Soma from the Potar’s cup according to the season.
May Agni drink the Soma from the Āgnīdhra vessel, accompanied by the Ṛtu, with the Suṣṭubh metre and the beautiful hymn.
May Indra, the Brahman, drink the Soma with the Ṛtu-rite from the Brāhmaṇa who chants well and offers fair hymns.
May the God, the giver of wealth, drink the Soma with the R̥tu-rite from the well-praising and well-singing Potar, according to the season.
Come hither, for we have pressed the Soma for you; O Indra, drink this! Sit upon this sacred grass of mine.
Let the two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you here, O Indra; listen to our prayers.
O Indra, we Brahmins, possessing Soma and having pressed the juice, invoke you as our ally, you who drink the Soma.
Come to us who have pressed the juice; come to our beautiful hymns of praise. O fair-cheeked one, drink of the soma-plant!
I pour it into your two flanks; let it flow through all your limbs. Seize the sweetness with your tongue.
May it be sweet for your enjoyment, honeyed for your body; may the Soma be a blessing to your heart.
O you who are far-seeing, let this Soma flow toward you like women gathered together, O Indra.
With his powerful neck, his ample belly, and his strong arms, Indra strikes down the Vṛtras while seated at the draught.
O Indra, go forth at the head; you are the lord of all by your might. O slayer of Vṛtra, strike down the Vṛtras.
Long be thy hook with which thou bestowest wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the Soma.

This Soma of thine, O Indra, is purified upon the sacred grass; come hither, hasten to it, and drink! O powerful one, O lord of cattle, O thou who art honored by the powerful, this [Soma] has been pressed for thy delight; O Akhaṇḍala, thou art invoked.
O grandson of the bull, O great-grandson, you for whom the *kuṇṭapāyya* [offering] was prepared—upon you he has fixed his mind.
O Indra, we invoke you, the bull, when the soma is pressed; as such, drink of the sweet food.
O much-praised Indra, take pleasure in the pressed soma that provides wisdom; drink and pour yourself forth until you are satisfied.
O Indra, with all the gods, further our sacrifice that is accompanied by devotion, O praised Lord of the People!
O Indra, these pressed Soma-drops, the bright drops, go forth to your dwelling, O Lord of the Good.
Take the pressed, excellent Soma into your belly, O Indra; yours are the heavenly drops.
O lover of songs, drink our pressed juice; you are anointed with streams of honey. O Indra, this glory is indeed yours to bestow.
The imperishable splendors of the worshiper attend upon Indra; having drunk of the Soma, he has grown strong.
Come to us from nearby, and come from afar, O slayer of Vṛtra; graciously accept these our songs.
Since you are invoked between the far distance and the near distance, O Indra, come here from there.
O Sūrya, you rise up toward the bull of renowned glory, the one who performs manly deeds, the archer.

He who by the strength of his arms shattered ninety-nine fortresses and slew Ahi, the slayer of Vṛtra—may that Indra be our auspicious friend. May he milk for us [wealth] consisting of horses, cattle, and barley, like a wide-flowing stream.
O Indra, praised by many, take pleasure in the pressed Soma that finds the power of will; drink, and pour yourself forth until you are satisfied.

Drink thus as of old; let it exhilarate you. Hear our prayer and grow strong through our songs. Make the sun manifest, cause the nourishments to swell, slay the enemies, and pierce through for the cattle, O Indra.

Come hither; they call you one who desires Soma. This [juice] is pressed: drink of it for exhilaration. O wide-extending one, pour it into your belly; hear us like a father when you are invoked. Full is this beaker; Svāhā! Like a pourer, he has filled the vessel for drinking. The dear Soma-drops have turned together toward Indra for exhilaration, moving clockwise around him.
We praise with songs that Indra of yours—the wondrous subduer of attackers, who rejoices in the exhilarating food of wealth—just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls.

We quickly implore you for that which is celestial, bountiful, and encompassed by powers—like a mountain rich in nourishment, providing food, yielding booty in hundreds and thousands, and abounding in cattle.
I beg you for that heroic strength and that sacred prayer for the sake of first awareness, by which you protected the *yatis* and Bhr̥gu when wealth was at stake, and by which you aided Praskaṇva.
That by which you released the great waters unto the ocean—that, O Indra, is your virile power. At once that majesty of his cannot be attained, he whom the two worlds have cried out after.
Your songs, most rich in sweetness, your hymns of praise, surge upward—songs that win the prize, acquire wealth, and provide inexhaustible aid, like chariots seeking booty.
Like the Kaṇvas, the Bhr̥gus, and the Sūryas, they have attained every desire. Exalting Indra with their hymns, the Āyus and the Priyamedhas have raised their voices.

Indra, the breaker of forts, overthrew the Dāsa with his hymns; finding wealth, he scattered the enemies as he bestowed it. Impelled by prayer and increasing in body, the giver of much filled both heaven and earth.

I send forth my voice to stimulate you, the powerful and bounteous one, adorning my speech for the sake of the immortal. O Indra, you are the leader of human settlements and the foremost pioneer of divine tribes.

Indra, whose leadership is bold, encompassed Vṛtra; whose leadership is transformative, he frustrated the wiles of the deceivers. He struck down Vyansa, burning fiercely in the forests, and made manifest the lowing of the cows during the nights.

Indra, winner of the light, generating the days, has conquered the hostile armies with his eager followers, being their helper. He caused the banner of the days to shine for Manu; he found the light for the great battle.
Indra entered into impetuous strengths, bestowing many heroic deeds like a man. He has enlightened these prayers for the singer and has extended this bright color of them.

They celebrate the great and mighty deeds of this Indra, well-performed and manifold. With his encircling power he crushed the crooked ones; with his magical arts, he of surpassing might, overcame the Dasyus.

Through battle, Indra by his greatness created wide space for the gods—the lord of the good, the filler of the people. At the seat of Vivasvat, the inspired singers and sages praise those deeds of his with hymns.

The conqueror of the terrified, the excellent, the giver of strength—he who won the light of heaven and the divine waters; he who won the earth and this very sky—the wise rejoice after Indra. He won the steed and he won the sun; Indra won the cow that provides much nourishment. He won golden wealth and enjoyment; having slain the Dasyus, he protected the Aryan race.

Indra won the plants and the days; he won the lords of the forest and the mid-air. He shattered the fortresses and drove away the disputants; thus he became the tamer of those who act with overweening pride.

We invoke for our good the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty—the one who hears us, the fierce one for our protection in conflicts, the slayer of Vṛtras, and the winner of riches. Our prayers have risen upward, O Vasiṣṭha; magnify Indra in the assembly for glory, he who has spread himself through all things by his might. May he be the listener to the words of one such as I.

A cry has been raised, O divine Indra, a kinship-call, when the spoils were being distributed in the contest. For among men, one’s own life-span is not perceived; therefore, carry us across these very straits.

I harness the prize-seeking chariot with the two bay steeds; my prayers have reached him who accepts them. With his greatness, Indra forced apart the two worlds, he who struck down the Vṛtras without opposition.

Even the waters swelled like barren cows; your singers, O Indra, have attained the Eternal Law (*ṛta*). Come toward us like Vāyu with his teams of horses, for through our prayers you distribute spoils of war.
May these exhilarating draughts delight you, O Indra, the impetuous one who bestows great wealth upon the singer. For alone among the gods you take pity on mortals; O Hero, rejoice at this libation!

Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas praise with hymns Indra, the bull, who wields the thunderbolt in his arm. May he, being lauded, grant us wealth in heroes and cattle. And may you [O gods] protect us always with your blessings. The impetuous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, the conqueror of the swift, the powerful king, slayer of Vṛtra, and drinker of Soma—having yoked his two bay steeds, may Indra come hither; may he exhilarate himself at the midday libation.

O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma, rejoicing at this sacrifice, O you who possess bull-like wealth! May the self-sustaining drops enter into you both; bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.

May your swift-gliding, fleet-footed coursers carry you hither; come forward with your arms. Sit upon the sacred grass; a wide seat has been prepared for you. Rejoice, O Maruts, in the sweet food of the soma-juice.

For this worthy Jātavedas, we have fashioned this hymn with our intellect, like a chariot; for his providence toward us is auspicious in the assembly. O Agni, in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.

Come hither, O Agni, on one chariot with these [gods], or on separate chariots, for your horses are powerful; bring the thirty-three gods accompanied by their wives according to your wonted way, and rejoice!

We, seeking aid, call upon you, the wonderful one, as those who bear a heavy burden, O matchless one—yes, we call upon the wonderful one for the sake of booty. We call upon the wonderful one for the sake of booty.

Come near to us for our ritual service and for aid; he, the youthful, the fierce, the bold, has come to us. For we, as friends, have chosen you alone, O Indra, as our victorious protector—him who in former times brought this and that wealth to us. That very Indra I praise for you, O friends, for his protection—the lord of bay steeds, the master of men, the subduer of peoples—for he is indeed the one who rejoices [in our songs]. May that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.

I offer a hymn to the most generous, the lofty one of vast wealth, whose true strength is powerful and firm—like the rushing of waters down a slope, his irresistible bounty is opened wide for all life and for power. Then let all your desires follow you like waters flowing downward to the libations of the one who offers oblations; when Indra’s beloved, golden, shattering thunderbolt strikes against the mountain as if it were a rock.

To this formidable one, bring the sacrifice with reverence, like the radiant Dawn, for him who is most worthy of praise—he whose majestic form and Indra-powerful name were made for glory, even as the bay steeds are brought for his guidance.

O Indra, praised by many, we here are yours, we who move about having taken hold of you, O Lord of abundant wealth. For there is none other than you, O lover of songs, who can sustain our hymns; accept this speech of ours as you would the earth.
Great is your heroic power, O Indra; we belong to you. Fulfill the desire of this singer, O Maghavan! The vast heaven yields to your heroism, and this earth of yours bows before your might.

You, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, have shattered that great and wide mountain into pieces with your bolt. You released the obstructed waters so they might flow; indeed, you possess all conquering strength as your own alone.
Like birds plunging into water, guarding themselves; like the thundering roars of a rain-cloud; like waves breaking from the mountains, exulting—the hymns have resounded toward Bṛhaspati.

Reaching toward the cows, Bṛhaspati brought forth the Aṅgirases, just as Bhaga leads Aryaman. Like Mitra among people, he anoints the husband and wife; like a charioteer in battle, he speeds the prize-winning steeds.

The sacrificial offerings were hospitable, vigorous, desirable, golden-hued, and of blameless form. Bṛhaspati, having overcome the mountains, drove out the cows as one winnows barley from the chaffers.
He sprinkled the womb of Order with honey, casting down the flame of the sky like a meteor. Bṛhaspati, lifting the cows from the stone, split the skin of the earth as if with water.

With light, Bṛhaspati drove away the darkness from the mid-air; as the wind drives the spray from the water, so he scattered it. Having reached out and touched Vala’s stronghold, Bṛhaspati brought forth the cows, just as the wind drives the clouds.

When Bṛhaspati shattered the strength of the devouring Vala with his fiery heats and hymns, he seized what was encompassed by him—as the tongue seizes with its teeth—and made manifest the hidden treasures of the ruddy cows.
For Bṛhaspati knew that secret name of these lowing ones which lay hidden in their dwelling; like a bird breaking open its eggs, he himself drove forth the ruddy cows from the womb of the mountain.
He beheld the honey sealed within the rock, like a wretched man seeing a fish dwelling in the water; Bṛhaspati, having split it open with a roar, drew it forth as one takes a cup from a tree.
He found the Dawn, he found the Sun, he found the Fire; with his song of praise, he dispelled the darkness. Bṛhaspati extracted the marrow from Vala, who was embodied in cattle, as if from a joint.

Like forests stripped of their leaves by winter, Bṛhaspati took pity on the cows of Vala. He performed an act never before imitated and one that shall not be repeated, since the sun and moon rise from each other in succession.

Like a dark horse adorned with golden ornaments, the Fathers decorated the sky with constellations; they placed darkness in the night and light in the day. Bṛhaspati split the mountain and found the cows.
We have offered this homage to the Cloud-god who roars aloud after many [days]; may that Bṛhaspati bestow upon us vitality through cattle, horses, heroes, and men.

Truly, my hymns, seeking the light of heaven, have all sung in unison, yearning for Indra. Like wives embracing their husband, like maidens their bridegroom, they cling to the bounteous Maghavan for his aid.

My mind never turns away from you; O Much-invoked One, I have fixed my desire upon you alone. Like a king, O Wondrous One, sit down upon the sacred grass; let there be a drinking-place for you at this Soma-pressing.

Indra is the repeller of thirst and hunger; he alone, the Maghavan, rules over wealth and treasure. Indeed, these seven rivers flowing down the slope increase the vital strength of that impetuous bull.

Like birds settling upon a tree with beautiful foliage, the exhilarating Soma juices, dwelling in the vessels, have settled within Indra. Their vanguard, flashing with power, has found the sun and the Aryan light for mankind.

The gambler does not discern what has been won when Maghavan wins the sun as his total stake. No one else, O Maghavan, neither one of old nor one of today, can equal that heroic deed of yours. Maghavan has taken possession of every clan; the Bull gazes down upon the lowing of the people. He at whose libations Śakra takes delight overcomes his assailants with the potent Soma juices.

When the Soma juices flow together toward Indra like waters to the ocean or like streams to a lake, the inspired singers increase his greatness in the place of sacrifice, as rain increases the barley with its divine bounty.

Like an enraged bull he rushes through the mid-air, he who made these waters have noble lords; that Maghavan found light for the man who presses the juice, for the prompt giver, and for the one who offers oblations.
Let the axe arise together with light; may it be a well-milking cow of Truth as of old. Let the ruddy one shine forth with his pure radiance; let the Lord of the Good blaze like the bright sky.
O Much-invoked One, may we overcome evil-minded poverty with cattle, and all hunger with grain. May we, as the first, win riches through the kings and by our own heroic band.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below against the malicious one. May Indra from the front and from the middle grant wide space to us, his friends, as a friend.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the lords of celestial wealth and of that which is on earth. Bestow riches even upon the lowly singer who praises you. Do you ever protect us with your blessings!
And we, O Indra, seeking this very goal and devoted to you, the Kaṇvas praise you with hymns.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, I have no other desire than this; at the new work of the skillful singer, I have fixed my mind solely upon your hymn of praise.
The gods desire one who presses the soma; they do not long for sleep. Unwearied, they overcome negligence.
O Indra, we, seeking you, cry out to you, O Bull; take note of this of ours, O Vasu.
Do not deliver us over to the reproach or the censure of the hostile enemy; my resolve is centered in you.

You are a wide-spreading armor and a front-line warrior, O slayer of Vṛtra. With you as my ally, I speak forth for the sake of power that slays Vṛtra and for victory in battle; O Indra, we turn you toward us.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, may the worshippers turn your mind and your eye toward us.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, we invoke all your names with every song for the sake of overcoming our adversaries.

With a hundred powers of the one praised by many, we magnify Indra, the sustainer of the people. I invoke Indra, who is invoked by many, for the slaying of Vṛtra and for the winning of booty in battles.
Be victorious in the contests for booty; O Śatakratu, we implore you, O Indra, for the slaying of Vṛtra.

In glories, in the conquest of armies, in battles and in renown—O Indra, overcome our adversaries! For our protection, drink the most powerful, glorious, and watchful Soma, O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers!
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, those vital energies of yours which exist among the five peoples—I choose them for myself.
O Indra, come; bestow upon us great renown and invincible splendor. We cause your strength to increase.
Come to us from nearby, and also, O Śakra, from afar; O wielder of the thunderbolt, O Indra, come here from whatever world is yours.

May Indra indeed drive away great fear from us; for he is steadfast and active among the people. May Indra be gracious to us, so that no evil may reach us from behind, and may there be prosperity before us.
May Indra grant us freedom from fear from all directions; he is the conqueror of enemies and active among the people.

Now we bring forth our speech and our songs to the Great One, to Indra at the dwelling-place of Vivasvat. For he has never found wealth as if it were among those who sleep; a poor hymn is not praised among the givers of riches.

You are the opener of the stall for horses, O Indra, the opener of the stall for cattle; you are the opener of the stall for barley, the powerful lord of wealth. A helper of men from of old, one who does not let desire diminish [the giver], a friend to his friends—him indeed do we praise here.

O Śacīvan Indra, performer of many deeds, most radiant one, this wealth all around you is indeed made known. Therefore, seizing it as the conqueror, bring it hither; do not let the desire of the singer who loves you go unfulfilled.

With these days, with these drops, being well-disposed and warding off want with cattle and horses, may we—driving away the Dasyu with Indra, with the drops, and with those whose hatred is dispelled—seize upon nourishment.

O Indra, may we grasp wealth, may we grasp nourishment, may we grasp riches that are manifold, brilliant, and reaching unto heaven. May we grasp divine providence, which is full of heroic vigor, preeminent in cattle, and accompanied by horses.

Those exhilarations gladdened you, those manly powers, and those Soma juices, O Lord of the Good, in the slayings of Vṛtra; when for the singer who had spread the sacrificial grass, you, irresistible, struck down ten thousand Vṛtras.

Battle after battle you indeed approach with boldness; you strike down fortress after fortress here with your might. When, O Indra, through your friendship, you brought low the guileful one named Namuci in the distance by means of your bow, you slew Karañja and Parṇaya with the most piercing path of Atithigva. You shattered the hundred fortresses of Vaṅgr̥da; they were not to be turned back, yet they were utterly destroyed by R̥jiśvan.

O renowned Indra, you with your chariot wheel—difficult to withstand—crushed the ninety-nine thousand and sixty followers of Jana and Rājña, who had come with their kinsman Suśravas. You protected Suśravas with your aids and Tūrvayāṇa with your rescues, O Indra; you made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king.

O Indra, you who are protected by the gods, may we be your most auspicious friends in this exalted state. We shall praise you, and through you, possessing excellent heroes, may we attain a further extended and longer life.
O Bull, the soma being pressed, I pour it out for you to drink; satisfy yourself and enjoy the exhilaration.
Let not the foolish, the greedy, nor the mockers deceive you; do not favor those who hate our sacred prayer.
Here let these [soma-draughts], rich in cattle, exhilarate you for great bounty; drink like a wild ox at a lake.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, even as he is known—the Son of Truth, the Lord of the Righteous.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the red sacrificial grass where we raise our voices together in praise.
For Indra, for the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honey-sweetness, since he found it in his vicinity.
O Indra, O wielder of the stone, being summoned toward us, come with your two bay steeds to drink the soma.
Our seasonal Hotar-priest has sat down; the sacrificial grass has been strewn in due order; the pressing-stones have been yoked at dawn.
These prayers, O you who are borne by prayer, are being offered; sit upon the sacred grass. Enjoy the sacrificial cake, O hero.
Delight yourself in these libations of ours, in these hymns, O slayer of Vṛtra, in these chants, O Indra, lover of songs.
Our thoughts caress the vast drinker of Soma, the Lord of Strength, even as mother cows lick their calf—Indra.
So do you rejoice in the soma-juice for the sake of great bounty; do not deliver your worshipper to reproach.
O Indra, we who long for you, bearing oblations, sing your praises; and you, O Vasu, are well-disposed toward us.
Do not release us from afar; come hither, O lover of bay horses, and rejoice here, O self-sustaining Indra!
Let the two long-maned steeds, dripping with ghee, carry you hither on a comfortable chariot to sit upon the sacred grass.
Come to our pressed Soma, O Indra, mixed with milk—the one which, along with thy two bay steeds, seeks us.
Come, O Indra, to that exhilarating draught pressed by the stones upon the sacred grass; will you not indeed satisfy yourself with it?
Thus have my songs gone forth from here toward Indra, sent out to turn him hither for the drinking of the Soma.
We invoke Indra here with hymns for the drinking of Soma; will he not surely come at our songs of praise?
O Indra, these Somas have been pressed; accept them within your belly, O Lord of a hundred powers, O possessor of wealth through your strength!
For we know you, O Sage, as the winner of booty and the bold one in battles; therefore, we seek your favor.

O Indra, come with your bulls and drink this pressed juice of ours, mixed with milk and mixed with barley. For you alone, O Indra, in your own dwelling, I urge the Soma for your drinking; may it take delight in your heart.
We Kuśikas, seeking aid, invoke you, the ancient Indra, for the drinking of the pressed soma.
O Indra, the mortal man whom you protect well goes first to horses and cattle; him indeed you satisfy with even greater wealth, as the conscious waters flow from all sides into the ocean.

Like divine waters, they approach the sacrificial offering; they look down upon the expanse as if it were the wide firmament. The gods lead the seeker of the gods forward; like suitors, they take pleasure in the beloved prayer.

Over the two of them you have bestowed praiseworthy speech, they who, with uplifted ladles, worship as a pair. Without effort he dwells and prospers in your service; auspicious is the power for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Then the Aṅgirases first attained vital strength, they whose fires were kindled through their skillful work. The heroes found all the Panis' wealth as food—cattle and horses, and the herd of beasts.

Atharvan first stretched out the paths with sacrifices; from there, Sūrya was born, the guardian of the law, the beloved one. Uśanas Kāvya drove the cows hither together; we worship the immortal birth of Yama.

Whether the sacred grass is strewn for the sake of good offspring, or the hymn proclaims its resonance in heaven, wherever the pressing-stone speaks as a pious singer of praise, Indra truly delights in those arrivals.

I send forth a potent, true draught for the Bull to drink; O Lord of the Tawny Steeds, Indra, come for the sake of the pressed juice. Rejoice here with our nourishing songs, praised by all our prayers and with all our power. In every endeavor, in every battle, we, your friends, call upon Indra, the mightiest one, for his protection.
May he surely come if he hears us, with his thousandfold aids and with strengths, to our invocation.
I call after the ancient dwelling-place the hero of mighty counterpart, whom your father called before;
they yoke the ruddy, bright one as he moves around those who stand still; the luminous realms shine in heaven.
They yoke his two beloved bay steeds to the chariot on either side—red, bold, and carrying the hero.
Bestowing a signal for him who has no signal, and a form for him who is formless, O men, you were born together with the dawns.
O Indra, if I alone were the lord of wealth as you are, my worshipper would be a possessor of cattle.
I would learn from him and I would wish to give to this wise one, O Lord of Might, so that I might become a lord of cattle.
O Indra, your bounty is a cow for the sacrificer who presses the Soma; swelling with milk, she yields for him both cow and horse.
There is no restrainer of your wealth, O Indra, neither god nor mortal, when you, being praised, desire to bestow riches.
The sacrifice strengthened Indra when he spread out the earth, fashioning a diadem for himself in heaven.
We choose for ourselves the protection of you, Indra, who have grown great and have conquered all riches.
In the exhilaration of Soma, Indra extended the mid-air and the luminous realms when he split Vala asunder.

He drove forth the cows for the Aṅgirases, making manifest those that were hidden in the cave; he thrust Vala downward. By Indra, the luminous realms of heaven—firmly established and made secure—are not to be shaken from their stability.
Like a surging wave of waters, O Indra, this hymn of praise hastens toward you; your exhilarating draughts have shone forth.
For you, O Indra, are indeed the increaser of the *stoma* and the increaser of the *uktha*; you are the maker of prosperity for those who praise you.
May the two long-maned bay steeds carry Indra to the Soma-drinking, to the sacrifice of the bounteous giver.

With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci, when you conquered all rival hosts. When they sought to escape by means of magic powers and attempted to scale heaven, O Indra, you shook down the Dasyus.
O Indra, drinker of Soma, becoming superior, you have scattered the assembly of those who do not press the juice in every direction.

I shall proclaim your two bay steeds at the great assembly; I win for you, the conqueror, the desirable exhilaration that, like ghee, is poured out beautifully by the bay steeds. Let my songs enter into you, whose form is golden.

For they have sung together toward the golden womb, urging on the two bay steeds as if to the celestial seat. Like milch-cows filled with milk, they satisfy him with their bay steeds; sing forth strength for Indra, who is accompanied by his bay steeds.

That thunderbolt of his is golden, made of iron; it is tawny, desirable, and tawny within his two hands. Splendid, with beautiful jaws, its fury and arrow are tawny; tawny forms have been infused into Indra.

Like a banner in the sky, the beloved one has been established; the thunderbolt has spread out like a tawny steed in its speed. Piercing the serpent, he whose jaws are tawny—being of iron—he has become one who bears tawny flames with a thousand points of fire.

You, O Indra with golden hair, were pleased by the ancient sacrificers who praised you; you take pleasure [in the sacrifice], for all that is yours is worthy of praise—your perfect bounty, O golden-born one, is desirable.

The two beloved bay steeds carry Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the exhilarated one worthy of praise, to the intoxication in his chariot. For him who desires many libations, for Indra, the golden Soma juices have flowed.

The golden drops have been prepared sufficiently for his desire; the golden drops urge on the two swift bay steeds for the steadfast one. He who goes according to his pleasure with his bay coursers has attained his heart’s desire for the golden one.

Tawny-bearded, tawny-haired, made of iron, he who grew strong at the swift draught as the drinker of the golden Soma; he, the possessor of wealth, who with his tawny coursers shall carry us across all difficulties.

Whose two golden jaws fly open like two hearing-eared dogs as he shakes them for the sake of booty; when he cleanses his two golden jaws over the prepared cup, having drunk of the exhilarating, desirable juice.

And indeed, the Lord of the Bay Steeds, like a courser to the prize, has neighed at the seat of the beloved one within the two dwellings. For even the great *dhiṣaṇā* (the vessel of inspiration) was made eager by his might; you, the beloved one, have assumed lofty vital power.
Desiring both worlds with your greatness, you take delight in every new hymn that is dear to you. O Asura, make manifest the beloved dwelling of the cow for the sake of the golden-hued Sun.

O Indra, let the yoked teams of men bring you, the desirable one with golden jaws, upon your chariot. Drink of the offered honeyed mead, delighting in the sacrifice at the communal feast where the ten fingers labor.

You drank of the pressed juices of former times, O Lord of Bay Steeds; and now this libation is yours alone. Rejoice in the honeyed Soma, O Indra, and pour the bull-like strength entirely into your belly.

Drink here, O Lord of Bay Steeds, of the juice shaken in the waters, pressed by the men; fill your belly with it—the juice which the stones have mixed for you, O Indra; with these, increase your exhilaration, O you who are borne by hymns.

I offer a powerful, true draught for the Bull to drink; O Lord of Tawny Steeds, I present this pressed juice to you for your journey. Indra, rejoice here with our songs, praised by all our prayers and with all our power.

O Lord of Power, through your aid and your heroism, the eager ones who know the Eternal Law (Ṛta) have gained vital strength. Possessing offspring, O Indra, they stand in the house, praising you as their companions at the feast.

He who, as soon as born, was the first wise God and encompassed the gods with his creative will—he before whose breath the two worlds trembled through the greatness of his manly might, he, O people, is Indra.
He who steadied the trembling earth, who set the agitated mountains at rest, who measured out the wide mid-air, and who propped up the sky—he, O people, is Indra.

He who, having slain the serpent, released the seven rivers; who drove forth the cows by opening Vala’s enclosure; who generated fire between two stones, the destroyer in battles—he, O people, is Indra.
He by whom all these decaying things were made, who cast down the Dāsa race into the depths; he who, like a gambler winning the stakes, seized the wealth of his enemy—he, O people, is Indra.
Of whom they ask, "Where is he? of that terrible one they even say, "He does not exist. He destroys the prosperity of the enemy like a gambler's winnings; provide for him, O people—he is Indra.

He who is the impeller of the weak, who is [the helper] of the emaciated, who is [the protector] of the suppliant Brahmin and the singer; he who is the guardian of the one who has set the pressing-stones in motion, O fair-cheeked one, and who possesses the pressed Soma—he, O people, is Indra.

He under whose command are the horses, whose are the cows, whose are the villages, and whose are all the chariots; he who begot the Sun and the Dawn, who is the leader of the waters—he, O people, is Indra. Him whom the two contending armies invoke from opposite sides, both the higher and the lower enemies; whom those mounted upon the same chariot invoke separately—he, O people, is Indra.

He without whom people do not conquer, whom those fighting invoke for protection; he who has become the counterpart of all, who shakes what is unshakable—he, O people, is Indra.
